I am a big fan of racing games that have weaponry. Especially kart racers (woefully underrepresented on PC) do something to me. I f*cking love the inspired tracks, the brights colors, the high-speed racing and the tension the weapons add. This game has at least half of those, so needless to say I love it.
This game doesn't need explaining, it's an arcade-y racer with guns and cars. You drive fast and shoot hard, it's exactly what you'd expect. The game has tons of content: massive amounts of cars and tons of weaponry, a large selection of maps and gamemodes (which up until now have all been really enjoyable) and a really extensive single-player campaign mode and some interesting mechanics. You basically have to climb the ladders of your competition pool until you have the most wins out of everyone in the cup, then you can enlist in the tournament and when you win that you get a more difficult competition pool where you'll do the same. Along the way you can attract sponsors by winning frequently, who will give you extra money for donning their ads while doing well in races. There's also random sponsor events which have large prize pools and team-based gamemodes. There's a lot of variation in the campaign mode and it's loads of fun, it also lasts for a really long time if you want a good dollar to gameplay ratio.
This game is amazing man, whole-heartedly recommended. If you like guns, cars and arcade games, get this.

In short; Would recommend, but maybe wait a while before buying. And god help you if you're using a keyboard.
EDIT #1: After some tweaking of graphics options, I find the stuttering to be much less of a problem. If you want to minimize performance impact, sent Anisotropic Filtering to Medium, and all LOD options to low, then restart your game. I found this to be extremely helpful, and it still looks better and has exceptionally better draw distance than The Lost Chapters.

Star Trek Online (STO) offers players the chance to put themselves in the star trek universe with their own captain, crew and ship.  I personally enjoy flying around the galaxy, visiting systems and races I watched from my childhood in an effort to further the Federation, Romulan or Klingon empire.
There is a good mixture of ground and space PvE that you can run solo or with a bunch of friends.  Of course like any MMO there comes a point in this game that turns into a grind for gear or ships ... but this is to be expected.  Not to go into too much detail, there are micro transactions but you also have the option to spend time (collecting in game currency) or drop a couple of pounds (£/$).  The micro transactions are not imposing, and I feel they don't interfere with your gameplay or experience (unlike SW:TOR).
I would recommend this game to any Star Trek fan simply for the fun of flying your own ship blasting Klingons and Romulans alike.

First off this game will never win any graphics awards as it has a simplistic system because they have a "in game workshop" where you can make your own missions and scenarios in an in built creator.
The game itself is very enjoyable as it seriously takes time to have fan service to all movies and series' that make up the cannon universe.
The story takes place 32 years after the end of Voyager ad 20 years after the events in the JJ Abrams Star Trek reboot where Spock and Nero get pulled into an alternate timeline after the Romulus system gets destroyed.
They link everything together in a compelling storyline that fills in plot holes from the franchise along the way.
They have returning actors reprising theircharacters in voice overs for certain "seasons" or sections of the game.
The Away team (ground) combat is a little basic compared to other  MMO's but the space combat...oooh the space combat...is some of the most fun I have had in a Sci-Fi game in ages.

I'm really struggling with this one. Is it even a game? In the strictest sense, yes. But you may find it much more frustrating that some of the old hardcore 80s games that no one could get passed the 1st level.
I won;t go into what this game is about, as there are a load of reviews that say what this is.
Its not a game in the strictest terms, Its more of an intellectual excercise. A role playing game where you take on the role of an agent.
Some missing are fun to do, others are down right ridiculous. For example, (possible spoiler alert) i just did a mission where it offered you a template to use, You have to research someone, fill in the blanks and then send an email to social engineer a way in. the issue is that if you were not 100% gramatically correct, you couldn;t get past it. And sending the same email over and over trying to get it right kinda breaks the immersion, as it simply wouldn;t work like that ITL. The rwecipient would have become a little suspicious.
I'm finding more and more that i'm heavily relying on looking at spoilers in the forums trying to find out what on earth i'm supposed to be looking for this time..
Apparently the IRC and other help factors are still active, but i have never gotten a response on any of them.
If you are looking for a game that you can jump straight in, this is not for you. If you are looking for a game that is pick up and play, this game is not for you.
If you are looking for something that will challenge your intellectual and creative pants off., this game may well be for you.
I strongly suggest trying the demo from their main website before buying the full game, But remember, if you find the demo hard, you won;t get very far in this game. The missions can be infuriating, sending you off with little idea what you are supposed to be looking for. and beyong the first few missions, the difficulty becomes greater exponentially.
If you want to try something new, give this a go. I got this so my wife and i could try and work together solving the missions. Sadly the UI was too small to have on the TV, so that idea went down the pan after a couple of missions.
Is this a good game and would i recommend it? Thats a tough one, as it would be a different answer depending on whom i spoke to.
The idea is great, the missions leave a little a little to the imagination, and sometimes are truly baffling.
I'm going to give this a thumbs up, purely that its a great concept. However personally, i'm starting to get annoyed with having to check forums for every other mission just to give me an idea of where to start. let alone how to get the correct answer.

I generally don't recommend this.  But I DO RECOMMEND this game if you:
1) You haven't done much in the way of crafting / survival gaming, and want something non-overwhelming.  Just know there are better games for it once you are more comfortable.  Though it's not necessary to start with something like this either.
2) You are a survival game junkie, and are completely good with something you can just play for a little, but you won't get sucked into playing past it's welcome (about 70% of my time was "past it's welcome" time because I had so much fun in the first 30%.  I felt a sort of "wasted time" feeling with that last 70%, whcih was just used to make a bigger base, produce tons of bakes potatoes, and map the large explorable mode map.  I would play the scenario 1-2 times, but skip explorable, it really doesn't extend the game life.
3) Just love underwater stuff (I will say a game about underwater is a lot better than the underwater parts of non-underwater focused games).
4) If they add 400% more content to the game.  I've read second had that they are not going to update the game any more, so don't get your hopes up.
If this was an Early Access game, I'd say that it has promise. However, as a finished game, it's rather lacking, and there isn't much to do, really. I would suggest Subnautica if you're into the sea.
Think Minecraft, but set entirely underwater at the bottom of the ocean with more realistic enemies and a prettier graphics engine.

I Bought this on the sales as iv bought a number of game development products. I have a strong background in programming but when it comes to developing games i prefer to spend less time on the coding and more time on actually bringing an idea to life. This product allows me to do that.
I want to establish outright the products iv tried and why i prefer this over them, for my use:
Game maker - decent, will get the job done and has a scripting language. This product is better for RAD as it supports out of the box isometric view controls, 3d model support, lights etc without having to fuss over scripts etc.
AGK - This one is script only and therein lies the problem. Whilst its nice to have a crossplatform API, when developing a game writing all the logic and testing etc takes too long.
Clickteam Fusion - Just dont ever buy clickteam, wasted my money, its segmented and supports many platforms if you use only the core plugins, this product crushes it simply for game development anyway maybe not for app development.
Ok so the main reason is this product is simple for 2d and simple 3d games - there it is!

When I bought my first gaming PC 20 days ago, I got this game plus 3 others from the CroTeam for free. First thing I installed was Gas Guzzlers Extreme as I was a big fan of Vigilante VIII and similar vehicular combat games. Although its not Vigilante VIII or Twisted Metal in its essence, it is coming pretty close to it and I was very satisfied overall.
Pros:
1. Graphics are excellent, both enviroments and cars. Many tracks and lots of cars.
2. Physics are very satisfying as you can wreck lots of things and lose a lot of car parts in progress.
3. I was never hardcore into racing except for Need for speed Underground 2, but racing itself is pretty nice, had no problems with the driving model.
4. Combat ofcourse. Feels nice when you blow up your oponnent to pieces during the fullspeed or smahing them in the arena.
5. Game modes. Incredible variety of modes. There is something for everyone: Capture the flag, zombie defense, deathmatch, regular racing, battle racing, team deathmatch... almost endless
6. AI. If you play singleplayer and need a challenge, by choosing from 4 different difficulties, you will be challenged.
7. If you have a group of friends to play this game with, multiplayer is just awesome, you can lose a lot of time to it.
8. Optimization. There are plenty of graphics settings if you are struggling to reach your desired FPS.
Cons:
1. Multiplayer: As this game didn't have a lot of marketing and its developed by a really small team in Croatia, its not very known. Because of that, it is difficult to find others to play it with. I've been lucky and found a group of Americans.
2. No splitscreen. As there are not so many players online, it would be nice to have splitscreen. I was sad as I could not play it with my friend when he came over to my house.
I would recommend this game if you are looking for some combat on wheels. It is a quality game!

An Exercise in Frustration
I really wanted to like this game, but found myself increasingly frustrated. I've given up at this point. Too often you're sure you have the right answer, but it's just wrong. What's wrong about it? Who knows. You had to find three different clues to assemble your answer. Any of them could be wrong. And good luck doing actual research for you clues and trying to avoid forum posts discussing the solution. And then when you finally give up on trying to figure it out yourself and check those spoilers, you still can't figure it out.

If you like ARGs or solving mysteries then you should definitely be playing this right now. Live missions are fun. Story missions are fun. The community is fun. The phone calls you get (if you so choose) are fun. IRC is fun. Some agents go out to locations for missions and Periscope their journey. They meet up with people and collect intel or other items to relay to the other agents to continue solving whatever puzzle there is at the moment.
You don't have to get super involved, the story missions are easily worth more than the price, but if you do get involved you will be warmly welcomed as we are always looking for more agents to help stop the summoning of mythological creatures by building paper boats and floating them in the pond for Dispatch.

This is by far the best engine I've come across regarding ease of use and capabilities.
~Pros
-Friendly environment(simplistic UI)
-Vast amount of starting content(graphics, music)
-Coding is not required(the engine uses a simple, flexible and powerful visual scripting system)
-Excellent and highly responsive support on the forums, especially on their Discord channel(just don't be impatient and get mad with those who are trying to help you just because your issue didn't get resolved immediately, they're only humans you know)
-You can prototype games extremely fast
~Cons
Haven't really found anything yet.
~Limitations
-Cannot create VR games
-Exporting options are currently limited to PC, Android, iOS, HTML5
-Very simple lighting and custom shaders
-Even though you can create 3D games, the map editor does not include terrain elevation tools
-It does not support highly detailed 3D models(max 4000 tri polys)

Huge range of functionality! Can produce a wide range of games, 2D, 3D, Menu/Text based. Exports to Android, HTML5 and Windows, uncommon for a lot of hobby style game engines. FANTASTIC team working on it, quick to fix bugs and great built in bug reporting system. Totally recommend from series game dev teams to the hobbiest.

Especially for the money, I don't think you'll find a program more fun to use when putting together your games. I haven't found a more flexible engine (Short of maybe Unity, which still requires extra licensing) to quickly piece together scenes and basic mechanics to sketch out game ideas without diving into a million menus. They don't even have to be simple prototypes, as I am also able to implement complex mechanics in no time at all using easy drag and drop scripting. I have found that my only limitation so far has been my own terrible math skill.
The included demo projects and sample files are great and somewhat informative, but could certainly use some clarification. (I believe there is supposed to be some updated content coming soon that may fix that) Either way, the included documentation and link to the wiki contain loads of helpful information to get people started. It is also similar enough to a number of other game maker software titles that it isn't too challenging to pick up if you have ever worked with another game engine, coded your own, etc. I feel like newcomers could benefit from some kind of production workflow explanation to get started, but there is a lot of information on google that got me started just fine.
Basically, everything is self contained within GG Maker, and you could potentially build your entire game (graphics and all) right inside the engine without ever touching another program. The built in sprite editor is nothing fancy, but it certainly does the job. And that is one of my favorite aspects of GG Maker/Engine 001, I think. Tile editor, sprite editor, animation sequencers, interface designer, build sheets for fonts, built in pitch variation on audio, 2D/3D camera views, lighting, etc. Of course, it seems the main purpose is to be an Action RPG engine, it truly doesn't have to be anything of the sort. A downside being a large number of finished (and an even larger number of unfinished) games available out there tend to be formulaic Action RPGs using the stock graphics and little imagination. But there are a few really great looking releases that showcase just what you can pull off with a bit of patience and thought.
One time purchase gets you a fully licensed 2D game engine (With basic 3D features), the ability to import every resource yourself or design your own in the creator, construct a game from the ground up with no coding knowledge, release for Android, HTML5, and PC. Top down, side scrollers, platformers, isometric, first person, third person, action rpg, turn based, tactical, etc. You can use the built in systems and make a simple Rpg, like anyone with RPG Maker, or you can design your entire game to the extent of your creativity. YOU have to design the systems for YOUR game, but GG Maker allows you to do it like nothing I have ever used before. Highly recommended.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who saw a game he really wanted to play. But it was rated T for teen, and his overprotective mother wasn't sure if she should let him play it. But she did, and the boy was happy. That boy was me, and that game was Vigilante 8.
Fast-forward 15 years and I still hold that game as special. And apparently, so do the developers of Gas Guzzlers Extreme. They've stated that they have enjoyed games such as V8, Twisted Metal, etc. It may not be the exact same thing, but it sure feels similar. At least, the deathmatch game mode does.
Gas Guzzlers Extreme contains many different game modes. (Team) Deathmatch is reminiscent of how V8 used to play, as it pits you against a bunch of opponents in a chaotic match of cars with weapons mounted on them, with the only objective being to kill eachother. However, there are also game modes that resemble a normal racing game, with the addition of the guns of course. It's very enjoyable to be able to shoot a swarm of rockets at that guy who just cut you off and passed you. (even though that's the whole point of racing, it doesn't make it any less satisfying to blow up the jerk)
The only issue is the speed. Of course for the racing modes I like things fast, but for the deathmatch modes it's much harder to control a speedy car in an open map, especially when you're trying to aim at your enemy. The different weapons have some aim assist, but for the most part you have to have your enemy in front of your crosshairs. Still, I just finished a team deathmatch that came right down to the wire (the final score was 30 to 29, we won) that was intensely fun.
Of course, there is an online mode, if you can find people to play with. Come on, if you're a fan of Vigilante 8, Twisted Metal, or even Mario Kart, you'll like this game. If you like racing and guns, you'll probably like this game. There's even a demo they've provided so you can see how it plays, if you're not sure. Oh, and if you like zombies (I don't, but that's me) there's a zombie DLC.

It is rare that a game can make me angry within three minutes of play but Fable Anniversary has managed to make me want to give up PC gaming within TWO minutes. This is a lazy, half-baked port if I ever saw one. Something as basic as mouse support for menus should have been included on day one. I wait, with anticipation, for weeks now to play this. I even considered buying The Lost Chapters on Steam to tide me over. I probably should have bought it and forgot about Fable Anniversary. How can I enjoy the immersive world of Fable when the menus are so awful and the game lags on my reasonably powerful PC? The chicken chaser developers have shown utter contempt to PC players with this port. They advertised this port as a 'favour' to all the loyal PC fans out there who have waited and waited. Lionhead and Microsoft shouldn't have given us the favour if they were not going to be bothered to do it properly.

The laggy graphics can be improved on NVIDA cards wtih a bit of rigging around. Improves experience greatly.

The camera tries to adjust itself every time you move it slightly and that irritates me to the point that I can't play the game as it makes me really dizzy.
The voice over is good, the graphics are decent, but I wasn't taken by the starting "quest." I would be happy to get past the training, but the camera movement and controller being bugged put me off completely. I am a mouse + keyboard person usually, but the controls here feel like a bad port from the console.

Okay. So I played 30 mins of Fable Anniversary and surprisingly, considering from the reviews, I didn't get a single crash or froze. But I did get frame drops from 60fps to 25fps once, until I turned off the game's Vsync. Now I have 60fps to 85fps ingame. I understand that Vsync will produce the smoothest gameplay without any tears, but for this I didn't see that much tears. My graphics card is an EVGA NVIDIA GTX 650 TI SSC 1GB, and my CPU is an AMD FX 6300. My card is a simply mid-to-high end graphics card that handles older games such as Skyrim, Far Cry 3, and TOMB RAIDER game.
So what's the point?... Well, my PC isn't really a high-end computer especially with a cheaper AMD processor and Nvidia Card inside. I don't know why it works for mine but doesn't work for anyone else. Some reviews I read said that they can't even play the game at all.
I bought and owned the Fable Lost Chapters PC version when it was on sale, also played the original version on the first Xbox console; they're both really good ports. The game's good for what it is, just wish Microsoft could double check the game before publishing it on Steam to correct performance, and also the graphics aren't that appealing. So basically the assets in the game are exactly from xbox 360 port of Fable Anniversary, same unaccurate face models, bloomy blur, sharpen textures, and same old audio recordings. For this port, they included a hard difficulty mode that you can choose when starting a new game (that's all she wrote for this port). Unless you're a console person, you're force to use a controller since there's no mouse controls available yet.
I would somewhat recommend this game if you don't own a Xbox 360 anymore (mine got the red ring of death) and own a 360 wired controller for your PC, otherwise you're more likely to buy it on the console instead of PC. And also I wouldn't buy this game now, if I were you I would rather buy this version only if it's on sale. So far the remake did some justice by keeping the gameplay mechanics and the story the same as the original, too bad graphics didn't make it to the cut.
Thanks for reading my review :)

There has only ever been two games in existence that I have stated are "the best game of all time" and the original Fable held the title for years. With that being said, quite obviously, seeing the "HD" remake finally come to PC deserved more than my attention.
I understood that no mere remake would ever come close to the experience I had when playing the original, nor did I expect this anniversary edition to be held to such a high standard. What I did expect however was to go on a glorified nostalgia trip and bellow in the good times of yonder and upon release, I did not think this game could offer that due to the sheer amount of bugs and crashes that occured, jest I forget the bloody awful blur that was everywhere, but a few patches later, it is absolutely worthy of merit. There are however, some gripes which still have not been "fixed".
A PC game should use a mouse and keyboard apppropriately in whichever way makes it easier for the user. Good PC ports understand this simple concept and use both inputs as intended, however, poor ports which have clearly been rushed out and unpolished do not and often retain keyboard controls where they should not be. Sadly, Fable Anniversary is the latter. No mouse controls in menus whatsoever is frustrating beyond comprehension and should never occur.
It still makes me wonder how when the game was originally released, it can pass quality control, not only by Lionheads testers, but by this distrubution service. It should not be legal to advertise and sell a product as a polished fully-working release when this is quite clearly not that. It is truly sadenning to see how poorly Lionhead Studios performs since Molyneux's depart and the fact this thing was released in such a state shows an utter lack of respect for the PC audience as a whole. Of course, as previously mentioned, the majority of gripes have been fixed now, but the release sure was off-putting.
Graphically, it does overall look quite pleasing. The environments are relatable to the original and look most grand. The models however, espescially the hero, look laughable and plastic.
The "Heroic Mode", which was advertised as an extremely hard mode, was really not noticable. Apart from the lack of resserection phails (lives), the game was overall quite forgiving in both combat and items. Well, I came into this expecting something along the lines of 'In Memoriam' (Missing, if you're in the US).
Sort of a follow-the-breadcrumbs style of game using real-world browsers.
And it sort of is.
You're playing as an agent of this undercover agency designed to protect against supernatural (I think) threats.
You get hints and clues, and it's really up to you as to how you go about deciphering them.
So, the good stuf first.
I love the idea. This whole blending of real-world and game is right up my alley.
But that's about it for the good stuff.
On the con-side however.......
The objectives themselves for each chapter are very vague. Add to that, a lot of the clues are bewilderingly worded, so you spend a lot of time either researching things that you don't have to because the answer the game is looking for is right in front of you.
Or, you spend a few hours doing a hunt-the-hidden-answer, as you try to figure out which of the bits of information you have will actually allow you to progress.
If you've ever played some of the old text-based adventure games where you had to find the correct word for the game to trigger correctly, you have an understanding of what is going on in this game.
It doesn't exactly help that the difficulty-level is all over the place.
You jump from dead-easy into a maze of strangely worded questions that absolutely requires prior knowledge to figure out.
And of course, with these types of games comes an inherent shelf-life.
If you happen to buy this game a year from now, is there any guarantee that any of the embedded web-sites needed are still around?
It's a very neat concept, it's just not very well executed.
EDIT: Are you f*cking kidding me?
A puzzle-hint involving a FaceBook account??
Okay, first of all, there is no 'clear link' between the Rosenberg Clinic and Superterram Life Sciences.
One does neurological research, and the other is a body farm.
One is in Montreal, the other in Texas.
There are no documents, mails, telephone-taps or anything else that would make this company any more interesting than any of the others.
The only real link is that it's the only company-name that actually pops up in the search-engines.
That's not deduction, that's just mechanical grinding until you eliminate suspects.
And besides, are you really telling me that we can find a higly classified document re. medical experiments on the intranet, but apart from that we only have a vague browser-history to go on?
That is honestly just bad writing.
Even if I were willing to forgive that, using FB as a part of your game is.....
Well, let me put it this way; if having a FB account is required for completing this game (which it is), I would strongly suggest that you put it on the list of game-requirements, along with processor, GPU and all that.
Had I known it was a pre-requisite, I wouldn't have touched this game with a proverbial ten-foot pole.
And before you say "Just use a pseudonym and create a FB account".....
That would violate the ToS of FB, and is technically illegal.

An enaging but occasionally infuriating play.
The game is beautiful, and can be peaceful when nothing is trying to eat you.
The controls alternate between simple and impossible, often requiring an online search to understand.
The basebuilding was very entertaining, though the mechanics were a bit esoteric. Items occasionally disappeared, for example, when I accidentally removed the floor from beneath them.
Poor controls and wonky construction quirks aside I find only two faults with this game.
-Many of the environments could have been mesmerisingly peaceful had not each been accompanied by predators. Having even a single area that was safe to float would have allowed the player to enjoy the environment much more.
-The ending was rather lackluster.
In the end I enjoyed this game. The resource collecting and equipment progression seemed balanced, and the game provided enough help to make each progressive task challenging, but not impossible. (There is a harder mode for those who enjoy impossible.) An interesting game!

Engine001 or GGMaker is simple, clean, and versatil. While most engines focus on raw power, this one focuses on ease of use and versatility. Engines like RPGMaker are restrictive on functionality and genera, were as GGMaker is only limited by ones creativity and imagination. I'd recommend this engine to anyone who is just getting into game design, or someone simply looking for something new and easy to use.

If you ever wanted to make a game, especially a classic perspective RPG, a platformer, 3D or even the next Binding of Isaac, this is for you. It's pretty good - I've been using the original (Engine 001) for years.

The idea is good, but its implementation have issues. I clearly see where much of the sources of inspiration come from. I like writing tools like this myself (just for fun) I may have a more keen eye on where improvements could be made. But there is room for improvement (but I won't go into those now. I am waiting more a better release first, as I expect these to be temporary issues) But I am wondering if the developer is commited enough? Because there are some very basic issues that should have been adressed in the very beginning of the development. (More in the comments section)
I'll keep an eye out, and will change this review when improvements are made. But for now, let's just settle for a 'getting there' mark. I will put recommended, because there is no 'mmmm' (middle, either way mark)
Edit: I have mentioned a few things in the comments section. But I won't dig deeper, because I assume the dev knows already. I am happy to change this opinion once the application is more stable.

As a beginner in game development, I recommend this software to anyone who wants to learn to make a variety of games, with a rather easy to learn interface and scripting system. While some say the interface is 'outdated,' It is still easy to look at, and most importantly use! This program comes with extensive documentation, so you can always have something to look to if you forget what does what.
The mapping system is very nice. There is a small learning curve when it comes to the layers, but it is easy to get past. The lighting system is wonderful, and easy to use. you can set the color, radious and even effects like a strobe effect to it.
Can you make your dream game with this software? Of course! Currently there isn't any online multiplayer that can be accessed easily, but you can make old-fashioned local multiplayer games with split screens and multiple controls. (up to 4 players, not bad!) You can make tower defence, rpg, action, platformer, card, board game, racing game, and a whole lot more. If you are willing to put the time into learning this engine, (which shouldn't take long) you can most definitely make your dream games.
What did I dislike about GGMaker? The lack of built-in tutorials. While it brings you through the basics, I'd love to see more on advanced topics, and taking some of the communities tutorials implemented.
If you want to try-before-you-buy, go to the GGMaker website and click on the 'download trial' button. And you can go to
and look through to see what you can learn. They also have a forum where you can ask questions if you are having difficulties.

I have only 4 hrs for the steam version, but I have played this game probably more than any other and probably have close to 500 hrs logged on this game over the past decade or so.
This is in terms of a role playing experience, probably the best game ever created. It is much more unforgiving, but not necessarily difficult than Oblivion and Skyrim. It is the last pure RPG in the elder scrolls series.
Contrary to popular belief, this game is actually larger than both oblivion and Skyrim, before expansions. Everything except some random loot is hand placed. Everything. It is one of the most immersive experiences ever. There is little voiced dialogue but I feel it is made up by the massive amounts of DEPTH that is in the text conversations and just the sheer amount of background and lore and history you get from speaking to NPCs.
Story wise in terms of pure "Feeling important like a hero factor" Morrowind stomps both Skyrim and Oblivion. Oblivion you are second fiddle to Martin septim. In Skyrim, literally nobody gives a damn about you or your importance, your goal is so ridiculously simple (Slay alduin and the dragons) and has so little depth to the story. Morrowind's story is so epic, and you feel like you are truly doing something of great and supreme importance, even though the impact was so much smaller than the end goals in Oblivion, and Skyrim in terms of the overall story of Tamriel.
This game has not aged well, but luckily has more mods than oblivion and skyrim put together including several freaking amazing visual mods that basically make it prettier than either of them. The combat is lackluster and mostly just dependant on your stats, which honestly the most efficent way to level up is to train from Npcs simply because otherwise it can be a bit of a pain.
If you play this game you will understand how "casualized" and gutted skyrim especially is. It's still an excellent, amazing game don't get me wrong, but it doesn't hold a candle to the amount of depth that is contained in probably the greatest game ever made in the history of mankind.

is something unique. At first glance a typical Dating sim/Puzzle hybrid,
goes well beyond conventional "bare-bones" gameplay mechanics expected from most Dating sims and presents some of the most hilarious and offensive dialogue I have ever read. The dialogue is witty and raw, the girls are sexy and the very slow-paced gameplay is both relaxing and rewarding.
This game is explicity for adults, featuring heavy sexual themes and strong language.
You wake up early one morning, ambushed by a mysterious woman you'll know as Kyu, the Love Fairy. Being the sexually-awkward teenager that is the main character, your only response options to the sight of a pretty lady are "HI!! HELLO!!" and "Uhhhhh...". Classy.
Kyu becomes your love mentor as she drags you along different locations to meet some girls. She's extremely rude, urging, swears constantly and is very casual about talking about sex, leading to some great dialogue against the awkward main character. It's a hysterical adventure as you meet girls with wildly different personalities and authentic-feeling reactions to dialogue options.
At the end of the day, it's a Dating sim. You know what the story's main plot is: having sex with everyone. Still, the game has amazing writing that makes the adventure and the characters believable and likeable.
mixes a variety of gameplay modes in ways to give the player as much choice as possible as he progresses through the game. The game is structured around a day-night cycle with calendar timeline, visual novel-esque sequences and a puzzle game which acts as Dating. The puzzles are the main meat of the game and are more than traditional
games.
The puzzles have no time restraints and reward patience and careful planning, limited rather by the number of moves you can make before the girl gets bored on the date and leaves. After all, when you're with a woman you need to take the time to do it right. The Dating parts of the game are where you'll spend the most of your time, using what you've learned about the girls, boosters and upgrades earned by giving them gifts or just talking to them in order to solve the puzzle and impress the girls on their date.
When a girl likes you enough (having impressed her on multiple dates), she'll ask for a place to stay for the night. Oh, yeah.
The audio is brilliant. There is not a single line of dialogue that doesn't have full, high-quality english VO. The characters sound as authentic as you'd want them to and it's clear that a lot of direction was put into this aspect of the game. The music features a pleasant mix of instrumental pop, upbeat elevator music and (of course) a touch of sexy, slow jazz.
Nothing negative to report. Sufficient options, no bugs encountered during my playthroughs and everything worked nice.
The girls are sexy and tasteful, the dialogue is raw and the gameplay is solid.
is an unexpectedly intricate, deep-rooted hybrid of both the Dating sim and Puzzle aspects, ensuring that progression in one aspect of the game directly affects the other and, with time-passing consequences to failing dates, encourages the player to learn about the girls as much as possible, carefully plan moves and pick the right time for everything.

Let's start off with the good. This game is amazing, and I have been playing for quite a while. The combat for the most part is amazing, and reminds me of the good parts about the Battlefield series. It is fun to play the game with vehicles, most which aren't too hard to unlock, and it is also fun to play as an infantry soldier, running from point to point and taking out bad guys with your shiny new gun. The gunplay uses a system of projectiles, where you must aim slightly above your target, depending on the range, just to hit them, and while I really enjoy that, there are some times where it is slightly frustrating. For example, you and an enemy both have an M1 Garrand, and are at the same health, and shoot at the same time at the same body part, maybe the chest, you will both die, and there will be no victor of that gunfight. I do enjoy this feature, because it makes the game slightly more realistic, but I do not care for it when there are glitches that occurr then, that disrupts the gameplay. Granted, this is in development, and I will not get too down on them because of that, the vehicles can be slightly bugged too. When an enemy car drives in front of you and your vehicle explodes with you in it, instead of you getting killed by the enemy, you are counted as committing suicice, penalizing you for getting killed by an enemy. Same goes if you are in someone else's car, and they drive into a rock, exploding a car. It is not considered a team kill, and instead, you are penalized for being in someone else's car and having nothing to do with being killed. Last thing I LOVE about this game is the class system. Different classes can have different vehicles and perks, and can help each other out on the battlefield. Many times in a game have I played as an infantryman and used a tankers tank as cover from enemy fire, and the tanker would act as moving cover, moving slowly for the infantry to move up on a point. The only thing I don't like about this game, is it seems that it takes way to long to unlock weapons. Getting the ribbons is the so-so part, but getting the credits is a different story. It takes way too long to unlock most of the weapons in the game, causing many new players to be shut down by the idea of continuing to play the game at all. If they could either reduce the prices by at least 75% or maybe even %60, this game would be better for infantry, but still not balanced. The only way to combat this, would be to raise the prices of the vehicles, %30, maybe %40, to make the game more balanced, so while there might be 3 infantry on 1 side with an STG-44, on the american side they might have 1  Jeep and, using the turret, be able to take out all 3 of those infantry, whilst being taken out by the forth or fifth. That's all I have to say about the game, and I really enjoyed playing it, and plan on continuing to do so. If I were to rate this game out of 10, it would be somewhere between 7/10 to 9/10.

I've got over 500 hours into this game, still have not earned enough dilithium to buy one of the "premium" ships. To buy a ship costs $10-$20 or more FOR 1 F'ING SHIP! And there is no way to buy through steam. Long story short:
PAY-TO-WIN or GRIND-AD-NAUSEUM.
As a trekkie myself, I found the game quite enjoyable, for the first few hundred hours. The last couple hundred hours have been a painful, repetitive, attempt to grind for something I know is not going to be worth it in the end. The game is free, but only limited amounts of it. Your inventory is quite limited, you are limited to a few of a certain kind of characters to play as. You cannot access the higher class ships without paying cash or grinding for literally months to earn dilitihium (which you must refine, but are limited to only 8,000 refined per day) then finally using it to buy "zen" in an overpriced player driven "zen" exchange market. After buying additional inventory slots, and banks slots, and character slots, you can forget about buying a ship through "grinding" in anything less than a year.
I had hoped to at least earn ONE higher class ship before writing this review, but have gotten tired of the monotony of this game, and with so many other good games out/coming out, this one is soon to be obsolete anyways. Perhaps that is why the dev's are charging so much for their content, and trying to make it pointless to try to earn anything through "grinding." That is why I say this game is PAY-TO-WIN, and that is why I cannot recommend this game to anyone other than the hardcore Star Trek fans. And to them I say this, enjoy this game until level 50-60. Thats it. Unless you want to repeat the same content literally thousands of times to maybe earn a ship. Do not spend your cash on this game. You will have to go outside of Steam. This game is years old, and on its way out. Spend your money on a newer, better game.

Since I wrote my original review, there have been patches implimented into Fable Anniversary Edition! The game comes off as more stable, but still has rendering issues in the Arena when it comes to the cut-scenes with the hero, audience, Jack of Blades, and Lady Grey scenes. I also am confused by the system used to assign keys for the D-Pad. I assign them, but cannot seem to use them. Those are my only urks at this moment.
Aside from the urks of rendering issues with certain points of the game, Fable feels like the original. The game-play is very smooth with the XBox 360 controller and the Fable 2-3 controls (unless you are assigning to your D pad, as mentioned before). The game matains the feeling I had with the Original Fable and Lost Chapters versions of the games and gives you a nostolgic feel when you play it.
If you are a big Fable fan, and can get past the issues of rendering delays, and the D-Pad issues, then I would reccomend the game! Despite the flaws, it is still a lot of fun and a great trip down memory lane for those who once played it on the Xbox. There is much the world of Albion has to offer you, once more!
If you cannot stand those problems I listed, I suggest waiting for more patches or look into getting Fable: Lost Chapters instead (You cannot play that version of Fable with a gamepad unless you get a seperate program that allows it. It is a strictly a Keyboard and mouse version of the game). If you are still on the fence, the best I can tell you is to wait for the game to go on sale and take a chance on it.
As for the DLC, you do not need it. The DLC only gives you the ability to BUY the items in game, and they items are insanely expensive or hard to find. I was hoping we got the items off the bat once you became an adult, but nope. Unless it goes down to super cheap, I suggest you save your money and play the game as is.

This is an amazing experience if you've never played an underwater survival game before. As somebody who is deathly fearful of the ocean, my first hour in the game was spent on my toes with my heart racing. Then I started to ease into the experience. The calming music, the awe inspiring imagery, and the sensation of being safe washing over you every time you step into your base. Out of the 3 and a half hours it took for me to beat the first mode of the game, I wasn't bored for a single second.
This game brings out real, powerful emotions in me. The surge of panic when you hear rushing water around you and know that a predator is about to make contact with you. The gut wrenching feeling when you jump over a cliff and careen downwards into an entirely new ecosystem in the depths below. And the awe and wonder the first time I heard the singing of a whale and turned around to see it floating by directly over me.
The experience was short, but it was incredibly solid and memorable. I sincerely hope that a FarSky 2 comes out with more building options for your base and longer scenarios.
I do not believe the game is worth the asking price of $14.99, but I got my copy in a bundle at an extremely low price. I'm sure it will go on sale for much cheaper from time to time as well. The game simply does not have enough raw content to warrant such a high price, but the experience is well worth getting it on sale.
FarSky falls short compared to other survival titles.

*** Fun game that is NOT worth the full price of $15 USD ***
*** ABANDONED EARLY ACCESS GAME ***
Now that I have those disclamers out of the way...This game is a watered down (pun intended) version of Minecraft that takes place under the ocean. The object is to survive below water and reconstruct your submarine to get yourself back to the surface.
This game does offer a sandbox version to it, which has its limit of replayability.  You can play this game in 3 modes, adventurer, which is how everyone starts off (allows death and respawning). Survival mode where you have just one life and submarine pieces are harder to locate and sandbox mode which in some part requires you have played a few games in the first 2 modes to be able to play sandbox mode.
The game offers a grand total 8 predators that you can fight and kill in the game and 3 of the 8 are sharks, so really 6 different predators if you count sharks as one type.  AGAIN, this is an abandoned early access game thus why variety in predators is lacking.  Also, you have a grand total of 3 tools, also because it was abandoned.  This game has only 5 ores you can mine (not including crystals) to use in crafting...again lack of depth due to abandonment by developers.
I have put many hours of game time into this game, most of which was done in early access hoping this game would get better and have more depth added to it, but like many other I was sorely misled that this game would become as great as its developers claimed it would be.
This game is absolutely fun to play, but can be played and won within 2-3 hours of game time. I still play this game often to see if I can beat it faster than the time before.  However, this makes the current asking price of $15 USD a ridiculous amount to ask for 2-3 hours of game play.  I DO RECOMMEND this game, as it IS GREAT to play!!!  But do not buy this game unless it is on sale at 33% off OR MORE.
I struggled long and hard whether this game would get a thumbs up or thumbs down and I have to give it thumbs down as it is an abandoned game by its developers and it is criminally over priced for what it offers.  I do recommend buying it ONLY if it is on sale.

I have only 4 hrs for the steam version, but I have played this game probably more than any other and probably have close to 500 hrs logged on this game over the past decade or so.
This is in terms of a role playing experience, probably the best game ever created. It is much more unforgiving, but not necessarily difficult than Oblivion and Skyrim. It is the last pure RPG in the elder scrolls series.
Contrary to popular belief, this game is actually larger than both oblivion and Skyrim, before expansions. Everything except some random loot is hand placed. Everything. It is one of the most immersive experiences ever. There is little voiced dialogue but I feel it is made up by the massive amounts of DEPTH that is in the text conversations and just the sheer amount of background and lore and history you get from speaking to NPCs.
Story wise in terms of pure "Feeling important like a hero factor" Morrowind stomps both Skyrim and Oblivion. Oblivion you are second fiddle to Martin septim. In Skyrim, literally nobody gives a damn about you or your importance, your goal is so ridiculously simple (Slay alduin and the dragons) and has so little depth to the story. Morrowind's story is so epic, and you feel like you are truly doing something of great and supreme importance, even though the impact was so much smaller than the end goals in Oblivion, and Skyrim in terms of the overall story of Tamriel.
This game has not aged well, but luckily has more mods than oblivion and skyrim put together including several freaking amazing visual mods that basically make it prettier than either of them. The combat is lackluster and mostly just dependant on your stats, which honestly the most efficent way to level up is to train from Npcs simply because otherwise it can be a bit of a pain.
If you play this game you will understand how "casualized" and gutted skyrim especially is. It's still an excellent, amazing game don't get me wrong, but it doesn't hold a candle to the amount of depth that is contained in probably the greatest game ever made in the history of mankind.

The Black Watchmen (TBW) game really hits the mark as a great Alternate Reality Game (ARG): in TBW you play the role of a paranormal investigation agent, fighting demons, witches and black cults around the world.
The TBW agency is powerful and well connected. While playing, you have the chance to exploit many different personal skills, as you work in front of your computer screen (using the game client or accessing the internet as well). In that case, code-breaking knowledge, social media and social engineering skills will be your assets! Many training missions are provided for your preparation as well, and the players' community is very helpful if you are stuck on a single player mission.
Furthermore, you can play with other agents using the game chat assets: you might even have the chance to actually go in field! Depending on your chosen clearance level in the agency, in Real Life you might be asked to analyse objects or document you receive by mail, or to go out in your town delivering documents or, in some cases, to meet actual NPCs, especially in the occasion of the game Live Events that involve collaboration of all TBW agents for a single mission that might go on for some days.
TBW is a great game, I really think that it is worthwhile to give it a try. You will be surprised!

What can I say.
I've only had this game a few weeks but I've been sucked into the addicting and immersive world of this game. I was a little reluctant to buy this game at first because I wasn't sure if I wanted to be a part of the ARG aspect of it. The great thing about TBW is that you don't have to do any ARG stuff if you don't want. Even the live missions can be completed without any of the extra stuff. However, now that I've realized how awesome the game is though, I've started to get into the ARG aspect of the game.
Basically there are 5 levels of immersion.
Red: The lowest level of immersion. The only thing required for red is an email.
Orange: This level is a bit more immersive. You have to register your phone number and will sometimes get phone calls/voicemails for live missions.
Yellow: Yellow is the highest level conventionally available. To be a yellow agent you must submit your location and will receive mail and sometimes have to do things in your area.
Green: To be a green agent you must submit a full medical report and do a ton of real world stuff. Only 1 of 8 people are selected for green each season.
Black: Classified Info
As you can see, the game gives you a lot of different options to choose from.
Now to the actual game. The game is very addicting and challenging enough to keep you wanting more. You investigate everything from illegal testing to cults to mutants to the apocalypse. The game does a great job of making you feel like you're somewhere you're not supposed to be.
Not only is the game and immersion great, but the community is one of the most welcoming communities I've ever been a part of. You can go to the forums at
and the IRC at
The vets will always be glad to help if you're stuck on a mission.
Anyway, I love this game. It's addicting, fun, immersive, and has a great community.
10/10
TL;DR great game, great community, buy it now.

It was part of a promotional campaign for Halo 2, that appeared for 2 seconds In one of its ads for E3 (or something like E3) that lead people to investigate details about the site, eventually finding coordinates to payphones around america, and a time for each payphone.
Everyone appeared on time to each and every payphone on time, despite one of them being in the middle of a hurricaine at the time.
That, was one of the first ARG's, and is probably the most famous one to have existed.
An "ARG" is an "Alternate Reality Game". And ARG's usually involve investigating websites, history, places, and cryptology to gain details on a fictional story.
Baisically Larping for the digital age.
However, the difference between standard ARG's and The Black Watchmen, is that ARG's are normally used for promoting a product, and they usually end at some point.
While the former is certainly the case (TBW is part of The Secret World MMORPG's lore), This game's selling point it that its missions don't go away after the ARG is over, but as far as I know (S1 Mission 16), these missions don't involve anything in the real world, and you don't need to go anywhere.
In Live missions on the other hand, you need to interact with the community via irc chats and their forum to solve specific events (e.g. Using google to Hunt down 5 german buisnessmen for sleeper agents to assasinate, because they know too much), and do tasks in the real world that're related to the event.
However, you can also choose how involved you are with the game's world by choosing what clearance you want to be.
>>RED CLEARANCE: Nothing irl will happen to you. You can play the game through the client and interact with the                                                 community, and that's about it.
>>ORANGE CLEARANCE: You may get phone calls by providing your telephone number.
>>YELLOW CLEARANCE: You may get phone calls and packages, and you may have to interact with actors playing a specific role.
>>GREEN CLEARANCE: The most known amount you can get involved. You have to be voted for it, and supply a medical exam for this. Missions will involve you, and they may take more than a day to finish.
>>BLACK CLEARANCE: This has been hung over our heads for a while. We don't know what it is.
In conclusion, I'd reccomend this game, as it has some very interesting puzzles based around finding codes based around books, the bible, and historical figures, which might end in you learning about something interesting.
If you have any form of paranoia, I'd
suggest researching this game, or asking someone that knows about this game if it's suitable for you.
>>END REVIEW

The Black Watchmen is an interesting game, if you can call it a game at all. The Black Watchmen is an ARG, or Alternate Reality Game. An ARG is a "game" where you have to go outside the boundaries of what you are given to solve very difficult puzzles. The Black Watchmen is advertised as a PARG, or Permanent Alternate Reality Game. That means that it will always be available for other players to experience it. The Black Watchmen does this perfectly by having a forum for newer players when they get stuck, or for new players to collaborate to solve to puzzles. The Black Watchmen also does a great job at integrating story into the overall experience, so you actually know what you are trying to do. Overall, The Black Watchmen is an exceptional game and I strongly urge you to play it. One more thing, YOU DO NOT KNOW WHAT YOU ARE GETTING INTO.

This is a great game engine. Sure, the UI is a bit outdated, not very intuitive, and overall it has an underground/DIY vibe that doesn't match the shiny rebranding - for now, because development is very active.
Don't expect the software will make all the work for you. It's not a game generator, it's a game engine. You will need to learn how to use it. And yes, it will require programming. Don't believe the "no programming required" crap every publisher throws at you. Even if it's visual scripting, it's still programming. You will need to think. A lot. And you will need to design your game. Nobody will do that for you.
But with a little patience, you can make wonders. Coming from Clickteam Fusion (which is also pretty good, but very different), I bought GG Maker for its 3D features, and I'm really happy with it. I wanted to make a 3D adventure/exploration game, and it has everything I need. Basically, with a bit of tweaking, I was able to create my own 3D tilesets, and use it as a voxel game editor.
It's a rather RPG-oriented engine, but with a bit of creativity I'm pretty sure you can use it for anything. GG Maker seems very versatile. I find the visual scripting system quite refreshing after Fusion's neverending columns of checkboxes. And the community is awesome. Here on Steam, and on
you'll find a team of very dedicated and helpful people.
About the price tag: please, shut up. You can export your games to Windows, Android, and even to HTML5. You can run 3D games in your browser. Do you know how much similar exporters cost for other engines, like Clickteam Fusion or Game Maker? Pretty much the price of GG Maker, except you also have to pay for the software, of course. Do your maths.
Yes, I definitely recommend GG Maker.

The Engine is not worth the money. There are so many better engines out there for a cheaper price. It comes with examples which make the features look quite bad. There is a lot in this engine but the guide it comes with doesn't go into much detail. Sure you can make a basic game with that information but for first time game developers, I would recommend anything but GG Maker especially for this price. Maybe if this was cheaper, it would be worth the time.

First of all, due to the fact that you can download the demo version from the 001 Game Creator store page (directly to the right of the "Purchase" button) and actually try the software yourself... This is more of an FYI about 001 Game Creator (or a defense case for its relevance) then a full-on in-depth review, for now.
Good Ol’ “Double-O-One” Game Creator (is that how to say it? I’ve never known if it’s pronounced James Bond style or if it’s supposed to be “Zero-Zero-One” or something like that) Anyway, If you've never used 001 Game Creator, it's like if RPGMaker and Gamemaker Studio had a baby. Not, quite as easy to use as RPGMaker but it is arguably more versatile like Gamemaker. Just to be clear, I used to love 001 and back then it was legit but I must admit, the software hasn’t quite stood the “test of time” as it is pretty dated by today’s game designing standards. Honestly, if you want truly the fastest (and easiest) game design software, your best bet is RPGMaker MV (since it now uses javascript and has mobile and html web development capabilities) and if you’re going to spend the time learning 001 Game Creator then you might as well just devote that time to learning Gamemaker, Construct 2 or Unity (or some actually relevant software). Sadly, the 001 Game Creator community doesn’t really seem to exist anymore and it’s hard to find answers through tutorials that seem like they haven’t been updated (or looked at) in years. The lack of community involvement is the real tragedy in my opinion. I hate to say it, but even their website is exactly how it was when I was a kid, it’s like an online time capsule of the 2000s! Now, I know that what I’ve said seems like I should be giving 001 Game Creator a negative review... However, (as I sort of alluded to a second ago) I’ve been using 001 for years now (pay no attention to the puny hours I've put into the Steam version thus far) so this is basically a thumbs up to that software and all the memories I have with it. But, don’t completely write it off, there are still a lot of really neat features that 001 offers: Setting up levels is a breeze and character, enemy and npc implementation is still my favorite compared to any other game design software. As I mentioned before, it’s the community involvement that has had the most detrimental effect on 001. It is up to us whether 001 Game Creator flies high or fades away.
With all that said, the Steam version of 001 Game Creator gives you access to features not available in the free version:
• License to sell your game, which is extremely important because games made on the free version of 001 Game Creator are not licensed to be sold.
• Mobile and web browser development capabilities.
• Steam treatment so you get fun little achievements and it will log how many hours you painstakingly pour into your game. (You know you love it, don't act like you don't ;P )
Considering 001 Game Creator Ultimate edition retails for around ($250) this edition is a pretty good deal (especially on sale)! The nice thing is if you are using the free version of 001 Game Creator; all files, assets, games made on the free one are fully compatible with this version (Obviously!) In conclusion, I would just create your game with the free version of 001 Game Creator, if you actually make something and want to sell it (or want to develop for mobile/web) then go ahead and buy this version.

I love Star Trek, but I cannot recommend this game.
Myself, my wife, and my 4 kids all have Lifetime Subs to this game, we bought in when Cryptic first introduced the LTS while it was beta.  But you know, it is what it is, they went free to play. I can get over that, they had to do what they had to do.
Then they started selling outfits and such -- cool beans, they have to make money somehow after F2P.
Then they started selling ships -- not ship skins but out-right ships that are 20x better than what you can obtain in-game without years of dillithium grinding.
Then they added lockboxes which require keys only obtainable from their cstore (the p2w shop).
And their latest scheme is making it a mechanic in game to need to expand your ship slots for admirality, which requires zcredits.
You will press the "buy now" button more than you will ever press any other button in this game.  Avoid it.  This game is a whole new level of micro-transactions and pay-to-win.
Want an extra character for farming? Buy Now
Want more storage in your inventory? Buy Now
Want even more storage? Buy Now (multiply that by 16 I think)
Want more bank storage? Buy Now
Want more shared bank storage? Buy Now
Awe! You can't buy that new weapon on the market because your bank account can't hold enough money to buy it? Buy Now
Lockbox Dropped? Buy Now
New ships added? Buy Now (but you better check your bank account, they can get expensive)
Want more bridge officers? Buy Now
Want specail bridge officers? Buy Now
Want more duty officers? Buy Now
Want specail duty officers? Buy Now
Want more ship slots?  Buy Now
Want a new ship? Buy Now
That is just the start. This game will nickel and dime the hell out of you.
Do be warned, there are many that have subscribed to this pay-to-win system, and they will tell you everything they can conjure to get you to play the game so that they have someone other than those who have sunk more money into them game than them in the game to feel significant.  These folks will give you the following excuses:
1) If you grind long enough you can obtain everything in-game that you can in the cstore
- This is an ambiguious statement, your life-span isn't log enough for this to happen if you pay $0.00.  Even if you could, the markets are controlled by the people who CAN purchase things like ship modules, keys, etc from the cStore giving them a very clear advantage in-game by use of their wallet.
2) You can gain the dillithium easy and fast to get everything in the cstore
- This is outright false.  In order to "grind fast" you have to either a) spend money or b) soak about the first 7 months of your play-time into grinding the dillithium to get 8 characters to grind this dillithium.  Once you do, I'm sure you'll be so sick of grinding dillithium you will have already uninstalled.
3) Then don't pvp, there is no competition elsewhere!

These T6 ships make it possible to continue playing the game (else you will die, over and over again), and then, if you want the T6 perma-passive bonuses from the ship, you MUST purchase it from the Cstore.

I know I've only played for '3.8 hrs on record' however, I've played a lot longer off-Steam, so I can vouch for Star Trek Online...It is a truly great game. No need to 'combine it' with any other game...XD! Star Trek Online is what I'd like to call "One possible Future of System Shock 2". As one can probably guess, it's a sci-fi/adventure themed MMORPG set in a future timeline of the Star Trek Series. Players who are fans of the Star Trek Series will feel right at home here, in spite of a few shortcomings (Which I will be highlighting below). The videos on the product page make it very tempting to play, and players have several options as far as diving into it is concerned. It works very swell on my system, so it'll most likely work at least well on most common systems today also. Here are the pros (Of which there are many) and cons (Of which there are few).
Pros...
1: The ability to create an epic character of one of many races familiar to fans of the Star Trek Series!
2: The ability to mold and shape your character as you see fit (His or her appearance).
3: The ability to select one of three Career Paths (Very similar to System Shock 2)!
4: The ability to complete many quests (Called missions), plus an awesome tutorial.
5: The ability to do Research & Development (Another similarity to System Shock 2)!
6: The ability to eventually expand your Career Path with up to two of several Specializations.
7: The ability to own several Star Ships and epic equipment for said space-faring vessels!
8: The ability to requisition weapons, armor, and even shields for your character.
9: The ability to upgrade all this equipment (And sometimes even your Star Ships)!
10: The ability to lead an away team of several NPC Bridge Offiers and also Duty Officers.
Cons...
1: The main 'down-side' is the way the updates are carried out-Usually in the morning, when I play, plus they take roughly 3 hours per update. Sometimes, they can happen twice a week, but usually only happen once per week. The 3-hour waiting time sometimes is less than 3 hours though.
2: Another 'down-side' is...Quite simply, I've no one to play with! In addition to this, most missions can be completed with virtually no help at all, though this might not be a bad thing.

Fable Anniversary is a colorful Action RPG set in the pomporous fantasy world of Albion. The player takes control of the hero and progresses from childhood to adulthood, making critical choices that affect your story. Quests are a dime a dozen, and although there might be more loading screens than most would expect from an open world game, it does nothing to contain the exploration of the wondorous realm. Albion is a fantasy like none other, with humor and intense action waiting behind every door. The combat is fluent and enjoyable; Not easy but not difficult to grasp. If you've played the other Fable games, it plays just the same. Yet the thing that stands out the most for me is the players interaction with the rest of the world. The expressions are fun and make for a very interesting mechanic, and the whole alignment system (as in good/evil) is one of my personal favorite mechanics of the game. Seeing the halo hover over my pomporous hero's head is very satisfying to say the least, and really gives weight to the choices presented to the player.
Acclaimed as the best in the series, it's easy to see why this game receives so much love. Most of everyone is fully aware that this is a remake, and the original is available on steam. So is it worth $30? To me, very much so. It is a vast improvement from the original in all the best ways, without straying from the original greatness of the earlier edition. I know that some people prefer the original version, and there's nothing wrong with that. But this game isn't for those people, it's for new players to enjoy the game with a new and modern life in it, and for the true hardcore fans who are excited to revisit this beloved world in a new way. I understand that a lot of people are having problems with framerate and texture (which i haven't experienced my whole time in the beta), but the developers have been and will remain active! They have been great at addressing everyone's problems and fixing them, and i'm sure they will continue to do so. As for me, I'll continue to support Lionhead in hopes that this is the beginning of something great. Fingers crossed for Fable Legends and Fable 2 Anniversary!

The obvious joke of praising this game as being a magnum opus and "highly recommending it" as GOTY aside, I think you get the same amount of value / humor from it in simply viewing its trailer as in purchasing the full game. The full game itself is pretty shallow and you're often just wandering around hoping to trigger the next sequence of dialog or strange visuals. There doesn't seem to be much indication of where you're meant to go.
I bought this game knowing it would "probably be dumb" and highly experimental but I was hoping it would at least still be enjoyable to play and include some interesting mechanics. Unfortunately, its shtick of being uber low budget and over the top wears thin early, as the first level includes navigating the same hallway back and forth in what may be an abstract Playable Trailer / P.T. nod, but isn't all that comical, interesting, or suspenseful. The game's humor largely fell flat for me. It's so odd and "out there" that parts of it made me smirk including a later area where you're instructed to buy a hot dog from "Hot Dog Man" but the game's mechanics and lack of explanation of what you're meant to do was far too obscure or strange for me to get very into it, even as a joke.
Potato Thriller includes frequent use of Microsoft Sam esque vocals, adding to its very low budget / low brow presentation, including a funny sequence of someone threatening that you better leave their house after trespassing into their woman's room before the owner kills you, but the moments between these kind of funny segments were really unclear how to even trigger the next amusing dialog, and I lost my patience inbetween the hit or miss comedy as I wandered around the levels unsure of what to do or where to go.
If Potato Thriller included more competent or engaging base gameplay I would be more interested in spending more time with it, but when left to only its strange sense of humor to carry it I felt like I was just wandering around aimlessly in a pretty bland environment.
Might seem like a joke but actually a great game 10/10.

Well I'm glad I found this game in a bundle with some good games, cause this game is baaaad! Really, let me sum it up:

Ugh. I've gained a recent respect for hidden object games and picked this one up in the Winter Sale. Sadly, it's probably the worst of the genre I've played.
There are only about 6 locations and you have to find the same objects over and over again in each one. This is easier said than done because all the objects are so blurry and the resolution of the scene is so low that you are basically clicking on smudges and hoping that is what they want.
This has nothing to do with the typos or bad translation or whatever is going on. The game tells you to click on a "duck" when it really means "swan". It wants a "beer" when it asks for "juice". And what is a "bulp"? A light bulb, obviously.
It's also incredibly short; I finished in about an hour.
I'd advise against this one, no matter how cheap it goes.

I could forgive the spelling mistakes, since it seems like English is not the game developers' native language. However, the game suffers from several flaws that make this (thankfully short) experience pretty painful. For a "hidden object" game, the picture quality is atrocious, as if the game assets were saved as low-quality jpegs. Some of the objects you're asked to find are ambigous, such as being asked to find a "bird", but only one of the four birds on the scene will actually count. Other times, the objects are completely mislabelled, like being asked to find a "duck" when they mean "swan", or being asked to find a "flute" when they really mean "grasshopper".
There's only really 6 scenes in total in this game, but the game forces you to replay the scenes over and over as a form of padding, I guess in an attempt to stretch out the game. It doesn't work: Once you've found the pelican the first time around, it's really not that hard to find the same pelican at the same exact location the 2nd, 3rd and 4th time you're asked to replay that scene.
I bought the game at 50 cents, and I'd say it was just barely worth it for the laughs, in the "so bad it's good" sense.

This game is probably one of my favourites of all time. It can get frustrating at times, but I love how difficult it can be - it makes it extra rewarding when you work out the problem!
It seemed a tad expensive when I first saw it, but it really appealed to me - and god-damn it's worth it! It really is worth the punt if it sounds like your kind of game. The user interface is simple, but clean and well polished.
It's a mix of puzzles, cipher/code breaking, hacking (things like email accounts) and researching (digging for information online). The story is great, if a little far-fetched/fantastical. I love how it ties in with the real world - I've even had real-life mail come through with a mission. The developers seem to be very dedicated to the game, adding many new events, live missions, and extra community sandbox missions.
I've been off on so many tangents whilst researching to complete the missions. You can spend hours looking into the completely wrong thing, but you learn so much in the process. A lot of the story is based on medicine and occultism, and it is interesting to learn about these subjects.

Thankyou, Alice & Smith, for creating this game! It truly is one-of-a-kind, and in my eyes, a great success.

The Architect is a puzzle game of varied difficulties by Spooky Star. In order to understand how the difficulties work, you must understand how the game is played: You find yourself on a translucent board made of blocks, all of which are on different levels. You can’t jump up but you can drop to a different level. Gathering certain objects of one color allows you to bring a block one level up per object. Gathering objects of another color allows you to bring a block down one level per object.
Difficulties, then, are based on whether you need to gather all the objects or not before you exit the level.
Larger, harder levels are labyrinth-like, so that even in the easiest difficulty you will have to consider your moves carefully – after all, you have only a limited amount of objects in the board meant to raise or lower blocks, and you might end up walking yourself into a dead end.
The puzzles themselves are pretty great if you’re into harder puzzles that make you think through each step, particularly on the higher difficulty settings.
The controls weren’t too bad but they weren’t overly good, either. I feel like they could’ve put a bit more thought in them, and while it’s hard to describe precisely why, I’ll just say the combination of mouse and keyboard felt a bit awkward sometimes.
There was an attempt to put a bit of a story on the puzzle, but I don’t feel it’s that good nor that it was needed. I do appreciate the effort in trying, though. The basic idea of it is: you’re just a mysterious object tasked with bringing a world to life. It’s interesting and gives it a nice touch, but there was no need to try and add depth to it.
The graphics were probably what bothered me the most. They weren’t bad, but they were confusing. I do understand the need to make the blocks translucent so as not to block the view of lower levels, yet at the same time this made the puzzles much harder. It’s probably also part of it – to add difficulty to the puzzles – but at some pints it was just annoying, as most of the angles on larger levels became confusing – was that at the same level or lower? – more than once I fell on a lower level because of this and locked myself out of moves, or even lowered/rose a platform thinking it was going to be at the right level when it really wasn’t – or when I was really seeing one beyond.
All in all, The Architect is a really nice puzzle game but I found it far from relaxing, and relaxing is how I like my puzzles best.
