The AI is really good and challenging and the sponsor battles/races sometimes leave me thinking "Wow, this is really happening with bots" or "Wow look at those graphics" when we get a good even game of CTF or last man standing with this booming Quake esque voice making every kill epic. The cars feel powerful and the customization diverse. I haven't had any problems with there not being enough maps either. Get it while it's on sale and try it people.

To start I am a big fan of games like Twisted Metal, Vigilante and Carmageddon. I have to say Gas Guzzlers has a similair style.
Some great points:
Arnold & Duke voice for your character (features some memorable quotes)
Great gameplay - explosive, fast paced and fun
Customisable Cars - from cosmetic to performance upgrades
Great soundtrack and humor
Graphics reasonably good
Features MP & Coop
Till now I have not found something which bothers me with the game and considering the cheap price (got it from Steam sale) I would recommend to any fan of vehicular carnage.

As close to Twisted Metal as you can get on PC without having to use an emulator.
Excellent selection of game modes, from your normal Deathmatch with weapons scattered around the map (ala Twisted Metal), Destruction Derby (no weapons, just tons of ramming into each other!), Racing (no weapons, just ramming into each other and trying to win the race), Death Race (racing with guns enabled on the tracks), Survival (comes with the Full Metal Zombie DLC, a very fun co-operative mode where you and friends survive 10 increasingly hard waves of zombies and creatures), Defend the Base (also comes with FMZ DLC, this time you and your friends protect your base from incoming hordes of zombies), as well as a few others I'm forgetting at the moment.
There's a TON of vehicles to choose from, including spin off versions of the Delorean, the Interceptor from Mad Max, the Dodge Charger, a very sexy Lamborghini, a Mini Cooper, among many, many more. I've not counted, but there's at least 20 or so vehicles in the game. You can customize each vehicle with skins, customized license plates, change the color of your rims, upgrade your parts and weapons, etc.
The controls work great, even with a keyboard, though I prefer using an Xbox 360 controller, which the game supports perfectly (just plug it in, launch the game, and you're good to go), The developers made the vehicles feel weighty, and it feels great when doing races. This could've easily been split into two different games, a car combat game and a straight racing game, and they'd both feel great to control.
There's a good selection of maps, which is always a huge plus for any car game. The graphics look really nice, too, every map and car looks nicely detailed. It isn't Gran Turismo levels of graphic fidelity, but for me the graphics in this game are perfectly fine.
I highly recommend the game, I've had a blast with it so far, especially when playing with friends, and I'd also recommend the DLC. Both of them add a handful of extra tracks, the zombie DLC is incredibly fun, especially the Survival mode, and there's a few cars added as well from the DLC!

This game is still as amazing as it ever was. From the opening beats of the theme music, the atmosphere will wrap around you like a blanket and never let go.
This is the only game I have ever found myself just wandering around feeling like I'm 'there'. Its immersion comes from intricately-written storylines, a world full of enormous detail, and a complete lack of hand-holding. Unlike Oblivion, there are no quest markers to follow. If you get lost, you get lost. And wow, will you enjoy getting lost. Everywhere you turn there is something new to see - sweeping landscapes, towering mountains, bubbling lava pools and farming country all await. Even just exploring the little islands that dot the map is an exciting pastime, almost a quest in itself.
If you prefer completing quests and bashing things there is plenty of that as well. Tribunal and Bloodmoon, the expansions in the GOTY edition, have a LOT of bashing things. Be warned: the bashing things mechanic is actually done on dice rolls, and not direct fighting mechanics. This means that to begin with you may not be bashing things as successfully as you might like.
The magic system is great. Shooting fireballs into the deep night sky from the top of a hill is one of my favourite things...but then so is zapping necromancers with massive explosions, so there is something for everyone.
The graphics were impressive for 2002 and I remember being blown away back then, particuarly by the water effects ('Yay, I've got the right shader model!'). However, if you choose it, the modding community has transformed the visuals into a spectacular world which is faithful to the original whilst taking advantage of modern-day technology.
If you really want to live in the world - which you will - you can also add fishing, food and crafting mods and never touch an official quest.
I go back to this game again...and again...and again. It kept me up until the early hours of the morning when it first came out. It's my go-to game when my internet access fails. The Prima guide was bedtime reading for weeks (don't do this until you have thoroughly explored for yourself, however - 'thoroughly' meaning 'for years').
And then there's the musical score...
Don't be in any doubt about whether to buy this. I'm not even much of a fantasy games-type person, but this is less of a fantasy game and more of a living, breathing, utterly believable world in which your role is as important or as minor as you want it to be.
Whether camping around the coast, catching fish for dinner and sitting by the fire, or engaging in huge battles with a big sword, worrying about your levelling and never bothering to sleep, you will eventually love Morrowind more than anything else in your collection. If Bethesda ever manages to capture this feeling in a game again I will be the happiest woman alive...

I'd really like to give a positive review to this game because its the kind of games I REALLY like usually.  Square tactics and collectible card games are the games I prefer over them all BUT...
This game is so badly balanced and the best cards (that gives you totally ridiculous power for their cost and almost guarantee you will win) are either very rare or so common you can stack three of them in your deck even from the lowest ranks.
Ranged minions are totally OP.  They can attack at range without retaliation from melee minions but melee minions still takes damage from them if they manage to finally fight them in melee.  Its also too easy to ''stack up'' a super shooter that will kill everything you summon in a single hit.
Combos are usually ridiculously powerful and the game is based on who will stack the first combo as fast as possible.  There is almost no way to get rid of overpowered minions once they reach a stupid number of hit points.  Gods can be summoned in multiple exemplars too.  Yep, you can have three Athena in play at the same time !!
Finally, The ''summoners'' powers are totally unbalanced and/or enforce you to focus on a single type of strategy for each one.  I mean, Ra ''Heals''.. so if you want to be efficient with Ra.  Do a deck based on healing.  Odin summons minions that can die right on the spot (because they can attack the turn they are summoned) so build a deck based on your minion's death for boosts is the only good option.  Other gods, like Nu Wa.. have totally useless powers which do not offers any combo to counterbalance the overpowerd things some others can do.
The worst of all is the elephant god with his pillars.  They jam your play by reducing the speed of your minions (making them VERY hard to kill because they are hidden in the backlane) and then he stack a few others pillars that boost all the minions he summons or deal damage.  You end up seeing all your minions trying to rush the front but you never reach it.
I REALLY wanted to like this game and waited a few months before blasting it, in order to see if the devs would correct some stupid cards.  But they don't.  So unless you wanna invest a good amount of money be prepared to lose every game (even at low ranks) until you manage to stack the OP cards and combos.

As much as I wanted to like this game (and for a very short while, did), there is absolutely no justification for this game to cost $15. I bought it on sale for $3, and had played it to comepletion in about 4 hours (give or take an hour I spent just exploring for no reason).
As much as I hate to echo everyone else's review, there simply is not enough content to make it worth the original price. It's fun to get to a new level (of which there are currently 3) and explore the flora and fauna, and it's fun to find abandoned bases which you can repurpose for yourself, but that's where the fun ends. The building/crafting is extremely lackluster, the fights are hard to survive, especially when you take into account certain predators which have insane health, and blistering speed. More often than not, your screen will flash red, and you'll spin around to see what attacked you, but more than likely the enemy passed right through you and is now coming at you from the opposite side.
The story is pretty weak and straightforward, which really isn't a big deal to me, especially in a crafting game. Your submarine has broken into 9 pieces, which have been scattered across the ocean floor. Find them.
The text is pretty iffy in terms of translation. It's usually okay, but there are certain phrases where you know what is being said, but the word they used just doesn't fit right.
Glitches. Let's talk about glitches. There are A LOT of them. Plant carrot seeds and get carrots, right? No, silly. Plant carrot seeds and get infinite carrot seeds which in turn can be planted to grow more carrot seeds. Remove window to get window? Nope, you remove that window, you're getting floor.
Oh, and have fun fighting 3 krakens for absolutely no reason.
Honestly? 5/10. This game was just okay, and that's about it.

I'm going to start off by saying that I really wanted to like this game.  I read through all the reviews before making my purchase and even though there were negative ones, I decided I'd find out for myself exactly how horrible this game really is.  Well, I've come to realize that it's not horrible, but it's not great either.  It's just okay.
I have always loved zoo builders and for some reason there's a serious shortage of them out there, so Zoo Tycoon 1 and 2 is pretty much up against Wildlife Park 1, 2, and 3.  I have played both the Zoo Tycoon games avidly and I hold it very dear to my heart, despite its discontinuation.
The Good-
1) I love the amount of animals, but also the amount of out-of-the-box type of animals that came with the DLCs.  I liked the farm animals, the domestic animals, and the animals that are kind of used as "decoration" (Ducks, Butterflies, etc).
2) The graphics are nice.
3) I liked the animations of the people and animals.
4) Unique buildings that are animal themed like horse stables.
The Bad-
1) Graphics are buggy.  When I started my game up, I instantly saw black squares in place of some plants.  It went away when I zoomed in.
2) The camera.  I always feel like I'm TOO zoomed in.
3) Placing water was crazy ridiculous.  You need to dig into the ground then place a water pump and the water keeps filling to whatever level the pump was placed on.  It's just too complicated and to be honest, quite annoying.
4) You can't build on a grid like other zoo games so your zoo ends up looking messy.
5) NO BIOMES.  Nothing is organized into biomes so you have maybe 1 tree for your Savannah exhibits.  The animals like land based on "Hardness" which is just.. weird.
6) Like I said, the menus are unorganized.  You have to hunt for the things your animals want through each menu and if you forget you have to navigate all the way back to the animal (yep, re-scroll and everything) to read their requirements again.  The animals aren't even organized.  Nothing is organized.
7) No themed decorations.  You get maybe 2 flowerbeds and 2 statues.  So difficult to theme anything.
8) The weather.  It might sound cool at first, having weather, but when it starts raining or snowing, suddenly EVERYONE and EVERYTHING is sad because they "Don't like the weather".
9) Every time you want to place staff, you have to place a bulky and unattractive building.
10) Buildings are nice looking, but seriously limited.  Decorations are the same way (as stated above).  For example, there are no restaurants.  Want to feed your guests?  Okay.. do they want to eat french fries and soda?  Because those are some of your main options.
I want to add that Wildlife Park 3 is a much better game but I was attracted to the DLC packs for Wildlife Park 2.  I'll wait until they make DLC for Wildlife Park 3 and continue to support this developer even though I was disappointed in this game.  I love zoo builders THAT much and I think they're doing better and improving.  I will still play my zoo on Wildlife Park 2, even though the bad things I listed get seriously aggravating.

I've always liked simulation type games and looking after animals, this game is done very well.
I love how you can build your zoo from scratch and look after the animals and name them and watch them from close up or above.
And the graphics look quite good.
Though I dislike that each staff member has their own building, to me that is silly and takes up too much space.  It ends up looking rather ugly having these tall staff buildings every where. There should be 1 major staff building for the animal workers and another building for the maintenance staff. And you can employ how ever many staff you need from each building and then asign to them a task or area for them to work. I did work experience at a zoo when I studied land management and the staff get to other areas around the zoo by bicycle or use a ute or other vehicle if needing to transport stuff.
I also dislike that you have to look after and watch the plants needs. That is not fun and I think it's unneeded. The plants should be alive but just classed as a decoration you don't have to look after like what they did in sims 3. Or at the very least I'd rather not have plants tell me they aren't happy and just have a gardener smart enough to look after them himself. So that I wont have to deal with the strangeness of plants telling me they aren't happy.
I also can't figure out how to properly build a water habitat. The game never shows you how to. I end up flooding everything or when I try to lower the ground more I end up with the water deep down the bottom and a massive cavern at the top. Iam not likely to buy the marine world DLC as I hate building marine habitats they always work out wrong. With you having to make a big hole and put a pump in and the water never fills up to the top and it looks ugly.
And underwater viewing tunnels don't work properly either.
When you build it you have one of two options.. you can either build a one-way line into the pool which ends underwater, or build a true tunnel with two exits.
If you opt for one-way visitors enter your tunnel but exit underwater and then swim in enclosure heedless of risk; and then start getting angry because they are stuck.
If you opt for two-way the tunnel acts like an invisible barrier preventing any animals from crossing sides - effectively cutting your pool in half. I did not test to see if this barrier prevents attacks by one species on another. But I did test and proved that they would rather starve to death than go get food just 2m on other side of the under water tunnel. Further animals begged for fellows if split up by a tunnel but don't if both on same side of it. And this barrier effect remained true no matter how deeply underwater the tunnel was placed and how shallow the animal's swim parameters were.
Could be more educational and have descriptions of the animals. Eg. Cheetah: a large feline of the felidae family which inhabits most of Africa and parts of Iran. It is the fastest land animal. It likes to hunt antelope etc.
I am likely to get most of the DLC eventually, except marine or horses as don't like marine habitat building and just horses in a dlc seems boring to me.
Despite the things I dislike this game overall is fun and enjoyable to play. I recommend it and give it 7/10.

Here's the short version; An MMO set in the Star Trek universe that does not really feel like true Star Trek much at all.
Allow me to explain in the long version. This review is aimed at hardcore Trek fans that enjoy proper immersion.
You go through a rank system; you get given command of your first ship at the first true rank; ensign. There's mistake number one! No one becomes captain of a ship at ensign!
The game is 95% combat. No exploration or discovery and a there's a mere smidgen of diplomacy. They removed the exploration features in the game some time ago. If you're into Trek as much as I am, it would be nice to have a ratio of at least 60% combat, 40 exploration and diplomacy. Part of Star Trek as we all know, was about exploring strange new worlds, seeking out new life and new civilisations and boldly going where no one has gone before. You can play some player made Foundry missions which feature exploration, but nothing from the devs themselves.
There are no real decisions to make in your actions and through dialogue. Every mission ends up the same way no matter what option in the dialogue menu there is. If anyone reading this has played Star Trek: Tactical Assault, you know that picking dialogue options actually affected situation outcomes and whether you got a gold or silver rating by playing how a real captain should. That key part of being a captain of a starship has been removed.
Also, it seems that your bridge officers appear to be much more qualified to be captain than you are. In every mission they practically determine what you have to do or you've picked up some gear that must be used to succeed. There is virtually no decision making that comes from your own mind on how to approach a situation and act accordingly. All you do is basically shoot first and ask pointless questions interspersed that don't change anything.
Severe damage to a ship seems reparable in a minute with no penalty to how your ship performs. This allows people to just stroll in and absorb all the fire with no concern to how or how much the ship is damaged. I'm sure the crew of your ship would be ready to abandon you over letting them die needlessly. I would prefer it if crew were reimplemented but became a much more integral part of gameplay such as if lose half your crew, you won't be so efficient. But they also removed crew back in the season ten update. I would prefer it if your damage carried through until the end of a mission. Also, if damage affected systems like EPS conduits and weapons banks and the like, throwing you into a state of heightened panic of your ship being blown to smithereens.
Another thing I dislike is the ability to push your ship far beyond its designed specifications through the use of abilities that can instantly repair hull or rapidly regenerate shields. I don't dislike all abilities, some of them definitely make sense and are acceptable, but there are a few which one bridge officer could not pull off.
Apparently you can just change out parts of your ship no worries without spending months in spacedock. Warp reactor not up to your standards, just remove and replace, simple as that. Ships are designed and constructed with certain components, some of those can't be removed easily. I would prefer it if you were assigned a ship and forced to stay with the default layout. It just helps with the immersion that you're not a revered captain but instead, just there to do your job.
And now, this brings me to my final point. Your ship's weapons and shields are always charged and ready to be put to use. Way to go trying to avoid a hostile situation with all your weapons armed and pointing at the other ship. There are also no alert statuses so you can't select between green, yellow and red alerts; which is undoubtedly one of the integral parts of Star Trek's combat. Yelling red alert and 'charge weapons, energise defense fields' was something I was looking forward to, but alas, doesn't exist.
So that ends the long version of my review. If you like to be immersed in a game full of Star Trek, go and play Star Trek Tactical Assault or something else, not Star Trek Online. The feel of Star Trek is squandered by the limitations and playstyle of an MMO.

We gathered around and laid out the plan. We knew that many of us would not make it back, but we also knew that once we get through the outer defences of archers and crossbowmen, we would be through the wort of it. As long as we survived the outer defences, the castle was as good as ours. We were outnumbered, with 150 of us against Count Grainwad and his 200 trained soldiers. To make matters worse, Count Grainwad was my father-in-law. Relation aside, I was content to take his castle, and with it, the remnants of Swadia. The next morning, after the ladders were complete, we marched towards the castle. Men all around me fell to the ground, as if pinned to the ground by the arrows that pierced them. I drew my bow and began returning volleys of arrows as my men climbed the ladders. I managed to thin the numbers of the archers by a substantial amount, and began my journey up the ladder. Although that ladder had to have been only about 30 feet tall, I felt as if we were climbing it for hours. The tension and whispers flowing within the remnants of my soldiers were high, but I would have none of it. "Stop your talking and return fire", I recall saying to one of my men, who was talking to another about his wife and child he had left back at home, in the village of Tadsamesh. Once we arrived at the top of the ladder, we saw it. Dozens upon dozens of corpses and men screaming in pain as the last morsels of life drained from their gaze, some of them mine, but most of them Grainwad's. The arrows flying all around my head only made me more angry and viscious. That's when I spotted him, Grainwad, commanding a squad of archers to fire at my direction. I felt an arrow pierce my side, but it had done little more than a slight poke, thanks to my armor. I drew my cleaver from its sheathe and ran towards Grainwad. He put up a good fight, but soon he fell to my feet and begged for mercy. I would deal with him later, however, as I had to continue to command my men to finish the remaining Swadian pigs. Derchios Castle was mine. Unfortunately, Grainwad managed to escape before I was able to apprehend them. I would get him eventually, I told myself. I knew my journey wad far from over, a few petty castles weren't going to win the entire realm. I began to set my sights on Dhirim. Soon, Calradia will know my name, and tremble in fear when it is mentioned. Soon, I would be king, and Calradia will only consist of one kingdom, my kingdom, Pugglingtonia, and I will rule it, me, king, King xXx_Booty_Smasher_xXx

This game is a fantastic group experience for anyone wanting to spend an evening stabbing your friends in the back. The Offline part is garbage, and playing the online multiplayer is decent fun, but the game truly shines when you have a large group of friends (4+) on a private server taunting eachother over voice chat and screaming in panic when you pull the shotgun. If you're flying solo, then keep on browsing, but if you've got friends to VC with, this game earns a flawless 10/10.
The only downside is that, rather than fix the server issues (There are no dedicated servers, you have to find publicly run servers to play on or make one yourself.) They instead released a worse version of the game under the pretense of it being a "remastering." The new version straight up removes some of the game elements and changes others,  while adding little, if any to compensate.
Worst of all, in my opinion, is that with the release of a re-mastering, they've removed the ability to buy a 5 pack of the Ship for 20 dollars. 5 friends tossing 4$ in the hat was the single greatest purchase I've ever made on steam, but asking each person to pony up 10$, especially when the game's most fun with friends? They properly shot themselves in the foot with that.
TL;DR This old version is better than the remastered one, and the game is best experienced with friends, voice chat, and perhaps just a little alcohol.

Early access indeed.  If the game got cleaned up and fixed it could be lots of fun, but as of this review - nope.
The graphics are simple but nice
The soundtrack (I only heard 1 song) is nice
It looks like there's a lot of opportunity for unlocking characters and progression
but it's not good yet.
There's no up/down attacking, so you just have to try to line yourself up with the monsters horizontally and hit them that way, but the hitboxes/aiming are a bit screwy.
First char I tried was an archer, and your attack speed is SOOOO slow - and then you have to hope the arrow doesn't go into the wall behind you, or a nearby table, or just 1 pixel too high/low.  It's ridiculous and frustrating. Unplayable.
I could use my special skills about once each before running out of stamina or whatever they cost, and that didn't seem to replenish
I found a claw weapon, but I thought it was gloves.  The game wouldn't let me pick them up/equip so I thought it was bugged and quit to the main menu.
Next I tried a sword & board guy, his attack speed is okay, but it's melee, so you have to get up close and personal, which is the only spot you're in danger.
Made it further with him, found a few of those claw weapons, as well as a helmet that I couldn't seem to equip (it said it required a cuirass?)
I also found 2 ornate rooms, one with a green chest, one with a red, and I couldn't seem to open either.  So it was a huge sense of excitement followed by a sustained "aww this sucks"
saw at least 3 NPCs, but couldn't seem to interact with them at all.  Trainer, Apothecary(?) and Blacksmith(?), sooooo.....no idea.
Only saw 3 monsters - bats that just fly straight towards you (slowly)
-robed figures that just walk straight towards you (slowly), or some of them shoot a bolt
-plants that come out of holes in the wall and shoot left/right
They still managed to kill me.
Third try is a "mage" who just uses a dagger, so not really magey at all (yet?).
I left a room before picking up an item by accident, and couldn't go back for it :(  But it was a shield so I probably wasn't able to use it anyway.
I saw a 4th monster!  A skeleton or maybe it was an armored guy.  It moved FASTER!  got killed by the 2nd one of those.
Attack-speed seems to be a huge problem in this game.  I intentionally stuck with the starter dagger just for a more frequent attack speed.  I found a powerful axe, a powerful sword, a powerful bow, but if I wanted to use those, then if I either miss, or don't kill a thing in 1 hit, there's gonna be a problem while I run around defenseless until I'm able to attack again.
Still nothing to do with those NPCs.  Maybe they're like crafting stations?  I found a couple non-equippable items that I think are crafting materials, but you can only carry 1 at a time and I never found out what to do with 'em.
If an enemy spawns inside you, free damage!  And there doesn't seem to be any way to heal.

Mad, explosive and consistently hilarious, with a uniquely British sense of humour that's actually very rare in mainstream gaming. The animals themselves have nice enough personality and animation to them, and there's a wide variety.
That said, it does have some negative points. The buildings you need to care for your animals are large and a bit obtuse, and you need a lot of them. The whole 'plants have needs' thing is a neat idea, but in practice is nothing but irritating. The AI can be pretty wonky at times, with guests wandering off and getting lost or animals starving to death while staring at a trough overflowing with food. Luckily, these things are managable so long as you're paying attention, it's just more annoying than game-breaking.
That said, I think that if you're really into zoo sims, this is definitely up to par with its main competitors and is a solid game all around. I've put hours into my zoos and think it's definitely worth a buy.

Wildlife Park 2 is a pretty standard game, it is entertaining if you are a fan of tycoon type games. I enjoyed the diverse range of animals that were only increased with the multiple DLC that became available. The game (and DLC) are affordable, and I would not have paid anything more for a game like this. It's fun, you have compelte control of how you play and run your zoo (or Wildlife Park... but really it's a zoo). I like attention to detail, the animal textures are decent and the many life styles factors that affect the wellbeing of each individual animal made the experience more real, catering to each animals individual needs as well as their herd. The mating animations were humerous and I was shocked the first time I saw a pair of Ostrichs going hard at it.. especially when I had the game in fast forward mod.. However there are a few issues with this game. You cannot access all the DLC content in the Main Game, rather playing the individual expansions separetly. I would have liked to use ALL animals and facilities in the one game to make zoos more diverse nd unique, offering more animal types and experiences for the (very ♥♥♥♥ing needy) visitors. Another issue that has put me off the game is the fact about a third if not a half of the animals textures no longer work and instead you have an awkward giant ♥♥♥♥ign square. OKay so as someone who still owns and plays the Zoo Tycoon games, I gotta say this one is pretty interesting. Now I like it even more with the amount of content when the (very inexpensive) expansions/DLC were bought and added.
The landscaping tools allow you to make a very detailed park as far as habitat and such goes. However some of the tools are labelled oddly. I suppose in other games I am used to the 'flatten' tool when in this game it's called 'plateau' but it does the same thing, bringing everything up/down to the same level and flat. A little finicky sometimes as it can be difficult to make a nice small pond in enclosures for drinking/swimming (sometimes there's not enough of a flat spot to put the water pump in so you have to mess around a bit). And the different types of turf are marked by hardness which is a little weird to me. I know some of the species of animals would like certain trees in their exhibits from their country of origin but the animals and trees can be dissatisfied trying to share the same turf type. I don't like the whole bit about micro managing the foliage of the park on top of the animals. That feels a little awkward.
Graphics are actually pretty decent, less cartoony than ZT 2 and (sadly) Wildlife Park 3. I am personally okay with the vast majority of them. Though I have one bug (not sure if anyone else gets this) where animals or people randomly turn invisible. They're still there and sometimes I find them by accidentally clicking on them. But you can't see them. You can see the 'meh' yellow smiley over their heads if they're somewhat unimpressed.
I do hate that the staff all have their own building, and you have to strategically place said buildings to get the most work out of your employees. The buildings take up valuable real estate that could instead be used for decoration or more exhibit space. On the plus side, the workers are pretty dedicated and no major complaints about them, in my humble opion. It would also be nice if they combined several of the staff into 'the Maintenance guy'. Gardener/Handyman/Bin Man could probably be the same dude since their work tends to be more infrequent.
I love the animal selection, though the Swiss Brown Cow is perm-invisible for me for some reason. You can create fairly interesting combinations of beasts for the most part, for mixed compatible exhibits.
Overall I'd have to rate this game (with all extra content) an 8/10 and if they make a 4th game and don't fudge it up like the 3rd one, I'll be the first to flail and yell "Shut up and take my money!"

Also the ui is terrible. Everything is just so darn big, why don't they scale these things down? This game has a concept that could be absolutely amazing if done correctly. Forgetting what this game is like, try to imagine the strategy and luck of a tactical game, the strategy and luck of a card game, and how complex and deep a game could possibly be with them both. Im not going to lie, most of this game's stages were very entertaining, EXCEPT FOR ONE. I found that the space stage is basically just, "Get bored, run back and forth between worlds, recharging so i can attack my enemies again, going to different spice planets, get spice, trade it, go attack again."
Meanwhile, all the other stages are very fun. Cell stage starts you off as a helpless singular cell organism, growing up into one of those wierd things you see floating up on the tops of lakes IRL. In my personal opinion, the cell stage IS NOT as boring as people usually make it out to be, though i will agree it is limited. The creature stage is pretty interesting, and this is where you will be doing most of your tinkering and customization for your creature in this game. The customization, i should mention, is one of the games strong suits.
The tribal stage displays the harshness of your race and sorta throws you into an, in my opinion, again, difficult stage where you compete with your contending tribes. Its warfare is challenging, and in a good way. It lacks individual and interesting building and defending options, but sending tribe members off to collect food was fun. Civilization. Congrats. You've made it to the promised stage, Where your race has yet again divided again into 4 factions. This stage is more interesting, as the warfare is exponentially expanded upon. You can make your own vehicles, planes, and decide wether you'd like to be a bystander, trading for money and riches, or a warlord, crushing your enemies with miilitary might, and doing a few favors for your allied nations. The other races in the space stage are VERY diverse, and in a few cases, the races just seemed the same and just bored me out. So, my total? A good 7/10, Worth its asking price. Truly a game EA DID NOT ruin. Rare, am I right? ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)

So, ♥♥♥♥ whatever it was I said about this game earlier. Let's be fair to this one, and review it as though it's just another Bejeweled game.
Because it does that well. It's addictive, challenging, and has a nice additional element of strategy with stuff like the date gifts. And there's little things that make big differences, like how you can swap gems from any part of the row or column to make a match instead of being restricted to adjacent gems. Once/if you go back to, say, Bejeweled 3, that just feels cramped and constricted. So if it was just a different looking Bejeweled with different mechanics, it would be a fantastic game.
It's still good, but it's let down by some of the dating sim part which I can't let slide. It's not so bad once you're halfway through the game and you get to know all the girls a bit better, but at the start, everyone's obnoxious as hell, especially Kyu. And you have to sit through the condescending and cringeworthy dialogue every time you start a new game, which because of the various achievements which are interesting enough to pursue, you will be doing a few times.
But eh, if they had an option to get rid of the tutorial dialogue, or that part was just improved a bit, I'd have no hesitation saying this was one of my favourite games. As for now, I'll call it mixed but on the good side, like a 6/8 or so.

Currently (22 Jan 16), this game is very, VERY early in development. It aims to be a Binding of Isaac style room-to-room action game with RPG elements like different classes, levelling up and gaining increasingly powerful equipment. But very little has been implemented. Your character is sluggish and can only attack left or right (!). Most enemies do essentially the same thing: walk up to you to try to hit you, with the occasional slow ranged attack. Since you outpace them, the game consists of kiting them around (or getting them stuck behind furniture) while you slowly chip away at their health. Graphics, sounds and music are basic, there's no minimap, and overall it's just a monotonous experience with no end goal.
In its current state, there's no point paying for it. If the developer wanted to gather attention and feedback from more players, this could have been released as a free demo. The dev is actively responding to feedback, hopefully the game will shape up in future.

Armed and Dangerous features you as Roman (leader of a band of rebels called the Lionhearts) on a quest to find the mythical Book of Rule and bring down the tyrannical King Forge. In traditional LucasArts/Planet Moon style, this game is a fantasy third-person shooter with a very British sense of humour and a stereotyped gang of the foolish American, savvy Cockney, Angry Scot and the self-aware, well spoken English robot with a Tea fixation either blundering or saving their way through this fantasy land.of Milola.
The game was a great one for the time with it's relatively simple controls and console-friendly interface, it felt more like a port than a PC game which is understandable, it was an Xbox release. The game has not aged due to it's awfully rendered DivX based cutscenes and suffers from resolutions not common now. The levels lack variety, consisting of missions to blow an objective up or save hostages from the king's ogres and Germans or hold off waves off attackers in a turret segment.
Armed and Dangerous was quite a difficult game, marching out in the slightly repetitive levels will lead to a quick death. However, you are far from alone with two allies who can't shoot for toffee and a vast array of weaponry ranging from Mortar launching Tubas to Land Shark guns and a vindaloo rocket launcher mixed with a quite destructible environment for the time.
Armed and Dangerous was a fun and hilarious title, and still makes for a solid game despite the badly optimised cutscenes. While it slipped under the radar at the time (and still does) it makes for a rather classic yet flawed LucasArts game. Despite the faults and the game being ten years old now, Armed and Dangerous is still the silliest third person shooter you are ever likely to play.

TL;DR
Gets boring very quickly and games last too long, cards are unbalanced.
Full:
Hand of the Gods mixes Hearthstone and chess together. The concept is very good but there are several flaws which I will explain.
1. The cards are completely unbalanced, and therefore are either very difficult to take out, or are very underpowered. One example is the war behemoth, which is 5 mana, and gains 3 attack every time it takes damage.
2. Gameplay is very repetitive. It isn't very dynamic and is very boring as most of the time, you are waiting 3 minutes just for your opponent to perform a turn. Clash Royale was a very successful card game, because it was dynamic, relied on quick reactions, and battles were way more fun and shorter. Hand of the Dogs relies on your patience.
3. There are several imperfections. The pictures of the cards in your hand look completely different when you place them. This can be very misleading as I thought a card wielded a bow, but it was a melee unit.
4. WAY WAY WAY too much luck involved. Battles are basically 50/50 and you might as well play rock paper scissors with your friends.
I don't suggest you waste your time getting this, until several balance changes are done.

Great game.
Easiest way to describe this game is -
Burnout Paradise + Twisted Metal + Flatout.
It's a racing game with guns attached to your car. And as you get farther along, you will unlock new cars as well as weapons and upgrades. There are several modes you play to progress through the career.
• Weapon Race - Just as it sounds, a race with weapons. There is two options, -finish the race by outrunning the competition, or -eliminate the competition and be the last to only finish the race.
• Knock-Out - An eliminator type race. Whoever is in last place will get eliminated when every other racer in front passes the starting line to the next lap. Same options apply, you finish the race by outrunning the competition, or you can simply lay waste to them and win.
• Power Racing - A standard race, no weapons allowed. Although you can still destroy racers by ramming into them or using mines and various power ups you pick up.
Later on in the game, when you get access to the high-end cars, (i.e. - Dodge Viper, Lamborghini Aventador rip offs) you get access to -
• Deathmatch - Kill anything that moves
There's more, but I'll let you find out the rest yourself! After all, this game deserves all the love.

This game is well worth picking up on offer.

It's a wonderful little survival game with a simple crafting system and a great aesthetic. The story mode doesn't last that long but you have the option to play in a Sandbox mode where bonus coins (found randomly during the story mission) can be used to purchase starting equipment to give yourself a head start. There's a day night cycle in which predators will become aggressive, often trying to attack you. You can craft weapons such as a speargun and a knife to defend yourself and create bandages from the nearby local flora. Progression in the story takes the form of collecting submarine parts so that you can reach the surface and escape your underwater prison. You need to upgrade your suit before you can head down into the deeper parts of the ocean to gather the last few parts which, once collected, allow you to finally escape!
Overall a charming, arcade-ish underwater survival game that isn't too serious and is a joy to experience. Great work Farsky devs!

I can't recommend this game in its current state.  It's waaaay too rough with too little to do and the balance is extremely off in many areas.  However, this game seems to have some potential and I will be revisiting this game in the coming months to re-evaluate my review and see how it has grown.  Unfortunately, at the time of writing this review, this game falls straight into my list as being released TOO early, even for early access.
Also, this is a roguelite, not a roguelike.
To the game's credit, there is a tutorial but the tutorial forgets to explain a few very key features including the ability to full heal at campfires (I found this on accident) and a sprint button (which I also found on accident).  Discovering these two features turned the game from nearly-unplayable difficulty to mostly a cakewalk.
Speaking of the sprint button, it feels like a wasted feature.  It costs no resources and the game feels lethargic and syrupy when you're not sprinting, so you have zero reason not to use it.
Combat feels more like a brawler than a top-down action game, because you're limited to left and right attack directions.  It's a bit frustrating, but seems to be a deliberate design choice.  I don't agree with it, but I came to accept it when I starting thinking of the game more like a brawler than a roguelite.  The combat is pretty shallow, too.  Aside from your (very situational and high-cost) spells, you're pretty much relegated to hit and run tactics: move in, swing, move out, repeat.
Enemies drop gold and XP which you are forced chase down.  That's never a fun mechanic and, to make it worse, there are VERY expensive unlocks that take a long time to get that will mitigate this need by giving you a vacuum ability that, according to the tooltips, cost your stamina resource.  Blegh.
Weapon balance is very VERY off, such that there is absolutely zero reason to use anything but the fast-attacking weapons.  The slow weapons take up to 2 full seconds or more to fire again, which is so soooo not worth it.  They don't even do that much more damage than the fast weapons!
Also, as far as I could tell, the game is endless right now.  With a decent gear upgrade and the hit and run tactic and a minimal amount of practice, you won't die.

First off, I LOVE this kind of game and where the developer is trying to go with this game.
- Too much randomness.  While I love procedural dungeons and randomly generated loot, even starting stats on starting equipment, you need to be able to make some choices like what class to start the game with, as that is currently random as well and the only way to change it is to roll the dice by restarting the game!  Ugh!  Also, leave all the random mobs and loot in, that's awesome but just set boundaries on some of it.  For example, put in a simple 'IF-THEN" statement that IF character has just began a game and level 1, THEN we can't spawn 20 mobs in the first room he enters"  ..Limits.  I don't mind 20 bats spawning after i get the feel of the game, but to play the game the first time and get my own life handed to me in 3 seconds by 20 bats almost makes me want to un-install the game and break something in RL.  ..You (dev) don't want potential customers experiencing THAT feeling in the first 5 minutes of their game experience!
- Your character moves too slow, combined with the frustation of not being able to attack up and down from your characters location!  Either make new sprites and add the ability to attack up and down, OR give us about a 25%-35% increase in movement speed please.  Either solution should make this game feel and play a lot better!
- Fix the bugs!  Sometimes when I'm moving right and hit space, my character jumps left right back into the mob I'm running for dear life from!  ARGH!  ..Not cool!  Same thing on the spells, some spells seem to not work when fired in certain directions.  Look at your code and fix it please.
- Maybe add in a device we can find or buy in the game to allow our character to "suck in or vacuum up" all the coins and loot once we kill the mobs in a given room.  This could be really cool and add an incentive to want to finish more rooms jsut to suck in all that money!  Woot!  Woot!
- Add mobs sounds/voices/insults!  Adding even cheesy sounds that come from the mobs could add a lot I think.  make the skeleton warriors say something, and use your randomness generation to have them select from perhaps a number of funny lines or insults when they spawn in and see your character!
Explosions!  We need BOOMs in this game badly!  I don't care how you do it, dynamite, explosive barrels, mines, whatever!  Get some BAWOOOMS! in this game please!
That's about it from me for now, mainly.  Oh wait.. the most important suggestion to the dev:  A lower price please!  This game doesn't compete with current games that do this style of game better and this game is a dollar higher then games like the first Binding of Isaac and Overture!  I recommend a price tag of $3.99 tops, but that's up to you.  I think the increased sales you'd get at $3.99 over the current $5.99.. as well as the lower amount of refund requests would pay off bigtime for you!
By the way, my early access score on this game was a 39%.  Watch my video to see how exactly I scored it if you want to see how I came up with that score for this game!
Please keep working on this game dev!  I want to re-evaluate in the coming months and be able to give it a lot better score!  ..Rememeber, that "value" is the most important part of every score I give games, psst.. your price [..wink, wink]  ..Thanks again for the free evaluation copy of this game dev, and please take my negative score as inspiration to make this game better!

First and foremost, I just wanna put it out there that I picked up a key for this game from a giveaway the dev was doing, so thanks for that, dev. Alright so lets get to the review part of this.
The game is called a "pixel art action adventure roguelike", however, the art is bland as ♥♥♥♥. I can barely stand to look at it because its just so dull and lifeless. I seriously hope that the dev changes the color scheme and character designs, especially for the main character(s). The music is generic techno♥♥♥♥♥♥that the dev probably found from a single google search of "retro music". Its very uninspired and boring. But thats not what matters with these types of games, right? No, what matters is the gameplay.
However, I am sad to say that even the gameplay, which should be the crutch of the game, is simple, bland, and boring like everything else in the game thus far. Everything reeks of amateurish design and a lack of effort to make something original. The game also has no story as to be expected, so don't get your hopes up.
To put it simply, do not buy for now. I am not saying to completely disregard it, but in its current state, it is a bug riddled mess that can barely even be called a game. If you're interested in it, just follow its progress, as im sure that the dev will address the issues that I have stated. For now though, this game is not even worth a dollar. To the dev, I recommend lowering the price of the game and increasing it when it is actually enjoyable and able to compete with other indie games that are of higher quality than yours. This game is possibly the best zoo simulation game on the internet. First, you have to pick the environment you want. From Costa Rica to Himilayas (heck, even a crater). Then, you have to build your whole zoo from scratch. No, not one of those crappy iphone apps where you get a colossal enclosed area and you just tapped on animals to feed them (and somehow get money from the animals), you have to actually BUILD it.
This brings me to one of the bad things about the game; The prices are insanely off-bordered. A pig costs 10 dollars, while an extremely rare Napoleon Wrasse from a DLC costs 48 dollars. In real life, the Napoleon Wrasse would cost thousands.
Anyway, after you start adding pens, you can put animals. They start off pretty hungry and possibly near-death, so what do you do? Either abuse the system and buy 1,000 lemon trees for cheap, or get a greenhouse for 500 dollars.
Once you get an entrance, you can open up the zoo for visitors.
Brings me to another bad thing; every visitor is so picky I can't even laugh about it.
If you have the Crazy Zoo DLC, every single kid will not stop whining about wanting to climb something. Sometimes, I just put them in with some monkeys and tell them to climb the monkey slide. It's so annoying.
You can put a wide variety of machines for visitors to use, like vendors, shops, and other stuff to take all of their money. Then, they complain to you that they ain't got no money. What do you do? Well, you have them take your money from an ATM and re-pay the same amount! YAY!
Also, they want to pet the "cute" animals. Even if you only have dead anglerfish around, they want to pet cute animals. It's so freakin' annoying.
Notheless, this game is great, and I recommend it.

I'm a Trekkie, always have been, always will be. Star Trek Online seemed like it was going to be the be-all and end-all of Star Trek games. For the longest time, I believed this to be true...
I deeply regret that it has taken me over 1000 hours of gameplay and several hundred dollars to come to the conclusion that this game blows. It is a poorly "slapped together", savage abomination of an RPG, with a Star Trek licence.
The space combat is quite fun but it is not ST. The ships don't move in 3D, you're on a 2D plane. You spend your time casting a bunch of buffs and debuffs and the ship auto-fires. Where's the fun in that? You can't warp unless you're in "sector space". The entire galaxy is mapped and explored(sorry Enterprise, you're redundant now). You can't target subsystems like a warp core or shield generator. Standard ST ship systems, ie. a tractor beam, don't exist unless you have trained a bridge officer in that ability. You can't capture enemy starships. I mean, even the damage physics are severely lacking; your ship stays in one piece until it explodes. I could go on but the list is near infinite.
The ground combat just plain sucks. I'm not even going to elaborate.
The story is, however, quite interesting.
This is a typical "freemium" game. It claims to be free to play but you'll be coughing up a lot of dough if you ever want to feel like you're getting somewhere. Don't be fooled, once you're maxed out they'll release another $150 expansion just to keep your wallet from looking healthy.
In my humble opinion, the absolute worst thing about this game: It is highly unlikely that we will see another good ST game in the near future, thanks to these licence hogs.
Overall I give the game a "blegh out of ten". Rather play Bridge Commander.

To start off yes, I grew up watching the orginal series of Star Trek. Im a Kirk fan...This game did not dissapoint. Especially with the new update of the classic 23rd century Federation. KK, so to begin like ay RPGMMO game, you start off with the character creation. Choose from the Kilingons and the Romulans alliances for your captain if you like the baddies. OR be the Federation modern/classic. With your captain, your able to be any number of races under that alliances alegience. Gorn for Klingon and Vulcan for Federation kinda thing. There is uniform and all sorts of nit pick custimization you can do. The important thing that your captain can be... a Enginer ( Repairs stuff and performance of tech/kits ), sceince ( healing and sheilds ablities) or tactical ( DAMAGE) officer.  These are important for they do determine certain objectives or oppertunities for missions and ships/weapons. So off you go to do the missions/storyline with your chosen alleginece captain. Learn to upgrade skills and traits and abilities acording to your captain type throughout the missions. Each mission there is space battle ( using your ships abilities with your crews/bridge officers abilties in space combat) and ground battle ( taking your crew/bridge officers down to a planet or another ship to explore and usualy fight. Thats the best part of the game. There is pretty much two types of rpg your playing here with space/ground combat. So yes, yes. you do level up and gain more skills and abilities acording to your officer type AND your crew/bridge officers AND your ship! Even ship type wise depends on what officer you are. Its important. The ships and space is very well done and Stardocks with the usual shops and missions hubs are everything you would expect. There is in game money credits and real money credits . There is also crafting by collecting various gasses and metals and such. All that RPGMMO goodness is there and done right. PVP, mail, officer trainer... Those that have played these types of games before will get the hang of it fast. New commers will pick it up with rather detailed dialogs and help ques.  With the ground battles its the same goodness, objectives and plenty of dialog to keep the story going and entertaining. Honestly its like watching the old shows with the newest update ( 23rd century). The bleeps/sweeps  ''cough'' the tricorder and corny tech is dead on. So choose those crazy aleins and upgrade that ship with plenty of phasers and  make sure your crew is shipshape to explore the final frontier.

So, just a heads up, I played Ace of Spades before Jagex aquired it, so I might have a little bias here. I'll try and keep it out, but yeah.
TL;DR: If you can put up with the small community, and really like blowing stuff up, this game is great for you!
Honestly, I really like this game. It's a simple arena shooter, with a sandbox twist, capped off with the charm of Voxelation. It's so much fun to run over to the enemy base, throw down some C4 and blow it to bits. I also can't explain how satisfying it feels to look at the minimap, to see the destruction and chaos. That's really what this game boils down to; destruction and chaos.
Of course, as most games do, this one has flaws. It's community isn't exactly thriving (though you'll still be able to hop onto a server at any time), the community itself isn't exactly the best (but of course, not the worst. I'm looking at you, League of Legends), some of the gamemodes are confusing, and a lot of the time, it ends up becoming a sniper war. One other thing is that there's no competitive scene. So, if you're looking for a competitive experience, you may want to shift more towards Block and Load.
The one thing is that I don't believe Jagex is working on Ace of Spades right now. I don't know that for a fact, I imagine if they tried to bring AoS back, it would hurt Block and Load. It's not super buggy, but it does have issues. Nothing major, of course. It feels pretty balanced and doesn't really need too much work anyhow.
Hopefully this review helped you out, whether you buy it or not!

Hiya! I can say confidently that I really enjoy Heroes and Generals in comparison to other FPS games and here's why!
I really enjoy a game that I can play without the worry of over-ranking irredemebly and getting bored. Heroes and Generals' progression system is slow, yes, but like Dark Souls, overcoming great odds to rank up is quite fun! This says I have close to 100 hours now and I've just unlocked all the subclasses (beside the high-ranking strategist positions) so I still have quite the way to go. But saving up your nickels to purchase a shiny new gun is part of the fun! You OWN the guns you buy with hard earned coin, so intimacy with your weapons form over time. Is progression slow? Yeah!! But I haven't been aggressively prompted ONCE to participate in the microtransation orgy, so I could that as a pro.
Also, the maps are GIGANTIC! Seriously guys, when I started playing the main assault mode at rank 5 I was astounded by the map size. Just massive and with higher-res textures than one might expect. Definitely a better looking game than Arma 3 with a similar map size.
And furhtermore, the War mode finally gives meaning to the endless games of multiplayer that other games offer. War is literally a slog accross Europe, where YOUR INDIVIDUAL GAME actually matters for the war effort! I've ended up in several battles for major cities like Berlin where our victory helped cement a win in the war! This game creatively solves the problem of other games where individual matches are meaningless and I really appreciate that!
Guns are incredibly well designed. When I can hear the clank and flop of my soviet machine gun it's all good.
Microtransactions are completely avoidable, do not appear mid-match or anything, and I have done completely fine without them.
Pros:
The sound design is incredible
Slow progression guarantees continuing reward over time
Massive maps are very fun to explore and fight over
Matches carry tangible meaning to the experience
Weapons are each unique and interesting, with good variety between each army
Every match is different, with different routes bringing different experiences to the same map
Textures are more detailed than expected
Hard and rewarding
Cons
Transport vehicles can be fairly bouncy
Tanks are OP when they snipe from a field (but restrictive in-tank vision balances somewhat)
Movement feels floaty at times
Conclusion:
Don't listen to people who can't wait long enough to rank up, you'll have fun in this game regardless of rank. ^w^

You'd completely not guess it from the other reviews here (even the product description mentions it), but this game is at least a little bit like Monument Valley..
But, fortunately, in a
way.
I was half expecting this to be a poorly implemented copy-cat. I' glad I was very wrong.
The comparison goes deeper than the graphical style and puzzle-types, though.
+ It's also quite short (took me a few hours because I was cooking and eating dinner at the time - nom.)
+ It's also cheap; cheaper than MV.
+ It's also got some truely head-hurting puzzles. Not in completing them; you can usually get by by just trying things and seeing what happens. The most you'll need to deviate from that is to look at where you
to be, and then work backwards to see how you can get there.
No; the head-hurtingness comes in trying to work out how on
they think these kind of things up! Even the simpler puzzles are sometime quite surprising and almost mesmerizing as you watch things unfold.
+ It's also got 'additional cast' although I'm not sure much of their potential is realised. (So far?)
All in all, a very pleasant little journey through some impossible physics and optical tomfoolery of puzzles.
There are a few negatives;
- I didn't personnaly find the story very captivating. Predictable and just a little bit preachy.
- The ideas tended to be reused rather too much in the second half, which was a shame given the very strong beginning.
- Controlling the circular motion bits often seemed a little wonky - but maybe that's just me.
Small criticism, really, and I'm definitely looking forward to see what happens in the next installments.
If in doubt, there are two
plusses of this (on Steam) over MV;
+ You can play it with a mouse. Despite the circular control thing, this is way more precise and comfortable.
+ You can play it at 2560x1440 with full AA on a 28" monitor. (If you have the hardware.) Retina display? Phah!

Minimalistic click-to-walk puzzles with an optical(-illusion/-ambiguity) twist.
+ Crisp, minimalistic visual style
+ Fitting, slow, ambient music
+ Good pacing of new game mechanics

You have to turn sections of the 3D puzzle to create a path for Evo to reach doorways and the buttons to open them. Surreal optical illusions are created to make physically-impossible pathways, for example if a gap is obscured then it no longer exists so you can walk over it. There is upside-downery, rubiks-cubery and all manner of fun to test your spatial awareness.
There's the standard cutesy storyline about Evo's journey and then he takes off in his rocket at the end, as expected.
It's clearly a mobile port, it even tells you to "tap". I don't have a problem with this except fullscreen doesn't work properly - windowed is fine though.
No glitches and cross-platform (I'm on Linux).
This is a casual puzzler, not too easy but certainly not hardcore. There is some challenge towards the end but it really doesn't take long to complete the 14 3-part levels. This is mostly due to the fact that there are relatively few options you can take, so if your brain can't handle it you can usually just muddle through by trial and error.
If you're easily disoriented then you might struggle. Personally, I've played The Bridge which is a hard-as-nails puzzler with the same concepts and this was a walk in the park in comparison.
The level design is crisp and clean with good use of pastel colours, pleasant to look at, and who doesn't love a little robot with goggles?
No trading cards. 8 achievements, 3 of which are 'specials' that don't drop during normal progress. These will give you an extra hour or so of playtime.
The quality/quantity is more than adequate for the low price. I would buy it.

(NOTE: This game was reviewed using a key provided by the Developer and/or Publisher)
Video Review:
The "Too Long, Didn't Watch" Review:
Take a wait & see on this one. Active Developer, but it's too raw still. 2/5
The "Meat & Potatoes" Review:
The game was just practically unplayable on release date, so I waited a day or two to drop a review. I am glad I did. While I still cannot recommend this game in it's current state, I can at least point out that the developer has been incredibly responsive and active in updating the game to try and fix it quickly and efficiently. The visuals and sounds are what you expect from a game like this, it doesn't pretend to be artsy at all. That's not the problem, the problem is in fact the gameplay itself. The dungeons are perhaps TOO random, which I realize sounds odd at first, but when you have spawned multiple playthroughs that begin with multiple shopkeepers in a row before you even get to a single encounter, and then your first encounter is nearly a dozen enemies which obviously quickly overwhelm you and end your game before it even gets rolling. The clipping/hitbox issues were even worse, making it impossible to collect items after a battle. Fortunately, the second problem there has already been somewhat addressed, just not enough for my tastes yet. Also, while your enemies can cause damage to you from any direction, your attack is very limited. There is no ability to attack up/down or North/South at all. Only to the left or right, which makes some rooms virtually impossible due to enemy placement. All in all, it is just to raw still to recommend. On the bright side, the developer is active so you can at least take a wait & see approach to this one and come check it out again later and see how much it has progressed. Merely yesterday I would've given this a 1/5, but already it is up to 2/5 for the recent, quick update.
Happy Gaming!

For how much time this game was in developement (even by one guy), I would certainly expect more polish. Just look around the indie scene, and it won't take long to see how many crazy beautiful games are made by one person. This game is by no means in
state fit for sale. I will painstakingly go over some details.
-The title. It says 'Pixel Art Action'. While the main game area is certainly classic pixel art, the character avatar pictures are not. Edit: even some of the enemy-entrance smoke and effects do not seem like pixel art. We can debate it all you want, but its a different thing.
-Clipping between your character and literally every single object in the level is horribly off. I mean it *looks* like there is room to walk around that table, but nope, you
get stuck. And oh boy this is a problem when trying to survive, and frustrating as all get-out when added into a roguelite.
-Wanna change to fullscreen/windowed mode mid-game? Forget it, it kicks you to the main menu, ending your run, with no warning.
-Wanna exit the game, or return to the main menu? Forget it, there is no option to do so.
-Wanna attack up/north or down/south? Forget it.
-Wanna have a visual or sound clue as to when you get hit? Nothing. You need to watch your life bar at all times. It took us some time to even realise we were being hit. Onto the next point:
-Going back to the shoddy clipping - you will get hit even when you are not touching an enemy. Its horrible.
-Level design/generation certainly leaves something to be desired. For example, why the first three room in my very first run all end up as shops? None-the-less, they had chairs set up in such a weird way that you had to walk completely around the room in an awkward fashion. Weird broken levels.
-Even for early access, there are way too many features 'coming soon' or 'not yet implemented'. I mean why couldn't you take 30 minutes some night and write up backstories for the characters? Thats as simple as it gets, if you ask me.
I wouldn't even say keep this on your watchlist. It doesn't even promise anything at all remotely either 1) fresh, or 2) better or competitve with modern roguelites.

I’ve been playing Unreal Tournament since the 1st edition. The good old classic UT99GOTY later was UT2003 then UT2004. In this edition some features were removed that existed in the older UT series like Assault, which was very popular and interesting game type. However there was an improved on the Onslaught game type idea that was introduced in UT2004 and transformed it to game type called Warfare in UT3, also added some sort of single player campaign which is not too bad, the single player campaign was also available in the old UT99GOTY but was presented in a more simplistic manner.
The downfalls are that the game isn’t supported much by modding community anymore especially if you compare it to the old UT99GOTY.  The other thing is lack of players. However, you can still make your own server and play with bots or have a LAN party with friends. If to speak about UT3 Black Edition as a whole is defiantly something worth trying.
I personally would recommend any UT series to try, because this is not a game it’s a legend!

If you like Onslaught from UT2004, you'll probably like this newest edition. However, if you liked Assault, you're going to be very disappointed. The weapons only look better, but perform no differently. Everything handles identically to UT2004 - it's basically just an HD remake that has less content.

While it's certainly not the best in the series, Unreal Tournament 3 is certainly a worthy member of it. It has a sort of back-to-basics approach in the weapon selection and non-vehicle game modes, and the vehicles themselves are actually well-implemented and fun to play with. The maps are well designed, the gameplay's definitely still Unreal Tournament, and the graphics are outstanding (especially considering the great performance!). Only major problem is the singleplayer campaign, which replaced the Tournament with a war... in other words, the campaign's simply stupid. Apart from that, it's a fun game.

Takes everything that all the previous Unreal Tournament games did right and built upon it, and even manages to add in new stuff and still turn it into a highly compelling multiplayer shooter experience.

I was looking for a good Motocross game that I could buy cheap. I saw this was $20 and didn't really want it. Went some where else and got it for $1.42 lol. I have played this game enough to learn how to use the controls effectively (I used an Xbox One controller). Physics are kinda wonky sometimes, but you can learn them to have a consistent racing experience. With my 6.4 hours, at this point in time, I have only raced with bikes and nothing else. Good amount of fun. If you have any idea of the techniques in real life, i.e. scrubbing jumps, you can kinda apply them, mainly just scrubbing though. Also, bike choice has a decent impact on how you race. Like the KTM 450 might be better at this track than the Blaze is (Blaze is Honda, kinda weird that KTM is the only brand mentioned but I dont really care). Trying to use only 1 bike for every track is kinda difficult because some bounce  better or worse. Making jumps hard to complete or just straight over jump them and smash into the next jump. AI difficulty thought did not take me long to reach All time difficulty. Rookie/Amatuer, wow. I can literally destroy those bots. Like start lapping them within 3 laps or beat them by like 40 secs on the 2nd place dude.
ONLINE: I only played once and that was enough for me. Typical 3 lap race, some good battles going on. I was in the lead with around a 1 second lead, I go to make this downhill corner, this F#$%ing dude slams into me and takes me out. I was triggered after that and never touched online again. Desync is dangerous for racing games when you can take people out.
Tracks: Pretty good, I like the motocross tracks, mainly because I can MOB on them. Its so nice when you normally can only double a jump, but if you scrub it just right with speed, you can triple and it gives you like a 1 sec lead. Supercross tracks, ehh, not the greatest, its hard to get precision with kinda wonky physics. Its very easy to go off the track if you are scrubbing, but in supercross, it doesnt make as big as a difference as jumping them clean without casing.
Overall: Pretty damn good for the price I bought it for ($1.42). Online might be better with friends if you are all in agreement not to take each other out on purpose. Only thing I wish is that there was a split screen option, I kinda wanna race my brother but I cant, so we just compare times on tracks. Not as fun but oh well. Go to some of the discount sites. ♥♥♥♥♥. Get the game cheap. It will be a good $2.00 spent.
UPDATE: I have over a 100 hours now. Game is even more of a blast now. There are some new techniques that I have learned or implemented. Insane what you can do if you learn them. Scrubbing is actually existent. On one track, you can actually quad if you scrub hard enough to where it sends you straight instead of up into the air. I bought this game for my bro as well, we race against each other and usually its pretty close. Supercross is probably the most fun. Whoever has the best rythem, speed, and consistency getting through the jumps is usually the person who wins.

Evo Explores is a nice little optical illusions puzzle platformer. OI work like bend over columns to reach other sides or hide gaps to pass them in the background. There are several levels which are completely rotateable. From different angles you can figure out new paths. The game is quite relaxing and the graphics are neat (Unity). The story is about the byte-ppl and philosophical quotes. Your "No.5" robot or "Wall-E" tries to escape the planet. Each of the 13 levels has 3 stages and is well designed.

Note: I'm a sucker for fancy-looking puzzle-games in this price range.
An annoying thing about this game is that it autodetects your system's locale (not system language!) and sets the game's ingame language to that. The Norwegian translation has mistakes and I had to suffer through it until I realised there's a menu.
I completed the game in a little over one hour. I consider that worth the price.
The art-style is pretty (however, the backgrounds could've had slightly higher resolution as I saw some aliasing), the mechanics are well-made and the music fits. The story could've been better, but there are limits to what you can do with one hour where most of the time is spent doing puzzles.
Additionally, how did my actions save the inhabitants? Like.. I completed puzzles, walked through doors and boom, everyone came back to life...

This game caught my eye from the Steam store because the artstyle looked a lot like Monument Valley, the mobile game. I figured this would be from the same developers since the style is unmistakeable. So I first looked into the game and devs before I purchased, but it's not the same devs. However, after reading from the devs who made Evo Explores, they were inspired by Monument Valley for this game, which is pretty clear.
If you've previously played through Monument Valley on mobile, then you will feel like you're playing through it again when playing Evo Explores. The only difference here is the main character, your "companion" that helps you through some levels to complete puzzles, and the storyline was written a bit differently to make more sense with the characters.
It's hard not to recommend this game, because I really like the puzzles it offers. So despite it being very similar to the experience you get from Monument Valley, I would recommend it for fans of MV who wants to play through similar puzzles and anyone who hasn't had the experience of it before, since MV is a mobile only game and this one was introduced to PC players. I look forward to seeing what the devs do with Evo Explores 2, which appears to be under development right now according to the devs Twitter.

The game is mostly fun. One issue I have is that this "Free-to-play" game is too expensive. Let me elaborate:
The basic cards you start off with can get you a few wins, maybe even complete your daily quests. If you're good enough you can try your luck in the arena to get more packs and cards to improve your casual/ranked decks. This is a great system, proven by hearthstone.
The problem here is that crafting cards is extremely expensive. And the favor gain from playing matches if relatively low, including quests. Some quests will net you 150 favor (half of a card pack) and requires you to play 30 God cards from a specific faction. That takes about 5-10 games.
In it's current state this feel way too heavy on the pay to win side. I bought a founders pack for $20 and I still feel underpowered. There are lots of cards I need to craft and none that I can afford to craft.
If they make it easier to gain favor and dust from the arena or reblanace the crafting it might be worthwile.

This game is great. If you are familiar with other CCGs like Hearthstone, Duelyst, or TES: Legends, the learning curve is only a few minutes. You are well rewarded for playing. After only a few hours I've earned 10-15 free packs, which has netted me enough cards to put together winning decks with every class I've tried so far. By the time this game officially launches I am CERTAIN it will be one of my favorites. A lot of the reviews say that there aren't enough cards yet, I see this as an advantage and a huge incentive to start playing now while this game is in early development.
The graphics are fantastic, my only hope is that the main menu gets some distinct personality, because as of this writing it looks exactly like Overwatch. Aside from that and lots of "Temp Art" on the cards, this game is beautiful.
The gameplay is engaging. It's very similar to Duelyst, but simpler, which I like. Matches can take a while, and if your opponent gains enough momentum it can be difficult to come back, but it's not always impossible. It's pretty easy to tell the difference between a match you'll have to fight tooth and nail to make your comeback, and a match that you've clearly lost by turn 4.
I'm glad I gave this game a chance despite mixed reviews, and I highly recommend that you do too.

If you're a sci-fi fan and enjoy the MMO genre, then Star Trek is likely your game. This game, like many of the MMO's similar to it, i.e. Neverwinter, offers the standard experience with ground combat that you would expect from a futuristic MMO. Unique to this game, however, is the space combat, which is an impressive experience that actually gives the player the feel of space combat. Naturally, it isn't perfect, as these games rarely are, giving some rather pathetic tutorials at times along with less than adiquate framerates. Regardless of these facts, the game remains enjoyable on many levels. Aside from the gameplay, I was particularly impressed at the fact they don't force you to purchase all of your special currency. Sure, you can buy the Zen tokens with your own money, butyou can also put some extra work in mining and grinding Dilithium crystals to trade for Zen from other players, meaning you don't necessarily have to pay to play advanced, which I find very respectable, especially in this genre. All things considered, this game takes an 8/9 from me.
