NOTE: to the people who don't like to read, there will be a short summary at the bottem of this revieuw.
This game is awesome. Basicly it's a racing game with weapons and powerups combined with a strange kind of humor that if you can apreciate that kind of humor will make you like the game that much more. I've played the game for about 4 hours now and I think i've seen enough to write a revieuw about it. If I'll encounter more awesome stuff in this game I'll change the revieuw.
The game starts off pretty awesome, You create a profile and get to choose a protagonist for your driver. You get to choose between 2 voices no-one cares about, Arnold Schwarzenegger and Duke Nukem. Of course Arnold and the voice actor of Duke Nukem didn't record these lines but I know who voiced Duke Nukem and I'm familiar with his Duke voice, and although the guy sounds like Duke there's a clear difference between him and Duke's voice, but the develloper went the extra mile and made him really sound like Duke Nukem and that's something I have to give them credit for. I don't know how acurate Schwarzenegger's voice is as I'm not as familiar with his voice as with Duke's voice but it does sound like Schwarzenegger.
After you created your profile you're good to go. You start off with a little bit of cash so you can buy your first car, put some guns on your car and you're off to your first race. At the start there are 3 game modes you get to choose from: Power Race, Battle Race and Knockout Race. Power Race is a race without weapons but with powerups like mines, oil slicks, smoke trails nitro's and repair pickups. Battle Race is a race with powerups and weapons. Those weapons are attached to your roof and can be used to shoot the living hell out of your opponents with weapons like machine guns, shotguns and rocketlaunchers and some of those can even shoot in 2 directions so no one is safe in front or behind your car. Oh, and cars donnot respawn so if you got destroyed it's race over. Knockout Race is basicly the same as Battle Race but this is more like an Elimination race as the last player that crosses the finish line gets eliminated and that goes on till there's only one car left. There's also Last Man Standing after completing the first tournament, which is basicly a battle in an arena that ends when only one car is left.
Now you might be wondering what the goal of the game is. For as far as I know it's winning all the tournaments. To get to a certain tournament you have to race untill you scored enough points to take on the tournament, you'll get points for winning races and killing opponents. Than you can participate in the tournament to compete for the most points which will be rewarded for winning and killing opponents. after you won the tournament you'll get some money and a new car. It isn't the most origonal idea but it works fine.
Another big part of the game is it's humor. Not all of you can apreciate it but it doesn't affect the gameplay if you don't enjoy it but it makes the game that much better if you do. from wheird opponent names like Sum Dum Guy, Kent U. Seemee and Lui Bricant to sponsors with names like Happy Smoke that fill your car with pictures of weed if they sponsor you. I personaly enjoyed this kind of humor. Talking about sponsors, sponsorship is a big deal in this game. They will give you extra money if you win races and you'll unlock special sponsor events that reward you with a lot of cash if you win. Sponsor events are mostly team based games like Capture The Flag and Team Deathmatch. You can get a sponsorship by winning a few races in a row. If you do well they'll pay you more money but if you end up on a losing streak they will stop sponsoring you.
I also want to mention something about the music in this game. The music in the main menu and during the races isn't anything special, but it isn't bad either. it pretty much concists of generic metal tunes that will get you in the mood but nothing memorable. The music in the garage however concists of things like country, jazz and I even heard the Dutch and American national anthems, it just adds to the fun factor of this game.
The only downsides to this game are the ability to restart races during a tournament which alows you to try the smae race over and over again untill you win and the amounth of racing tracks. There aren't that many which can make the game repetitive. In FarSky, you play a scubadiver exploring the seabottom by building bases and mining minerals. You are confronted with the dangerous creatures that live there and must defend yourself when night falls.
The initial experience of wandering the ocean floor I find amazing, and although I love the concept, the game has several massive flaws. Most prominently, it is currently in release state and will not receive another content patch This is it: in about four hours of gameplay you'll have seen everything there is to see. Furthermore, the game is very easy and offers way too much too early. Because of the small scale and poor pacing, it is very easy to get rare minerals early.
It's not that I dislike this game, but the €14,99 pricetag it has as I write this is ridiculous. I'm sure you could get a few more hours out of this, but there are games that offer much more for €14,99. I'd probably say anything over €5,- is too much to ask for this game.
This is a shame, because the game had much more potential. With some numbers tweaking and most prominently, more depth, literally, this game could have been excellent. As is, the game allows you to go no deeper than 350 meters (about 1,000 feet). I'm sure the developer had bigger plans, because the helmets you can make scale very oddly: the first allows you to go to 250 meters, the second 350 meters and the final one: guess!
350 meters +25% damage reduction. Did you guess it?
The developer says the engine has been pushed to its limits and that he will provide more content on his next game. I think this is a succesful first project for any (solo!) developer and it speaks of great potential, but a more humble pricetag is definitely in order.

High-quality, charming, strategy-based RPG made in RPG Maker 2000. The funny thing about it is that it uses the default assets, or at least, the default intellectual properties, in highly customized ways. This level of customization is rare.
A perfect example of how far one can take an RPG Maker game, if only enough time and effort is put in.
This game was originally in Japanese, but it has been translated well into English.

Gameplay
Helen's Mysterious Castle is one of the most interesting spins on the JRPG formula that I've seen in a while. It takes the standard timerbased turns and changes them up by havingf moves and equipment taking up a limited inventory space leading to decisions on which weapon do you want in the long run, or do you want to drop that spell for these boots, or maybe you feel like the investment into this sword will make it better that this other one over time. Overall I'd have to say it has quite good gameplay.
Graphics
It's pixel art
Music
It's all quite good

Other Ups
If you're having trouble it'll put a health up in front of you but you don't have to take it allowing for a mildly adaptive diffictulty, and it's systems also allow for a perfect run of the game (if ytou gring a bit that is)

I rate the game Star Trek Online 3/5. OK. And by "OK" I mean not that bad but not that great either. I can recommend it to some but I personally don't want to play any more of it. I don't have the patience for it and I'm pretty sure I don't have the time either, not when there are so many other great games out there to play and so many other amazing game worlds to visit.
Essentially, Star Trek Online is a fun, highly detailed, hugely expansive adventure game with a very friendly community which is also severely hampered by awkward controls, an obtuse interface, repetitive game design and occasional bugs. This game requires a lot of patience and a lot of time.
+Good (at least adequate) graphics made to run on many different systems.
+Great character customization options (if the options can be deciphered).
+Lots of game options and settings.
+Truly expansive game with HUGE numbers of missions and locations (many of the space stations and such have the exact same layout unfortunately which gets highly repetitive).
+Large ship variety each of which have many subtle and non-subtle nuances about how they fight and what their load-outs can be.
+Free to play and not pay to win with an unusually friendly and helpful community which is always wanting to have new players to join in a game which mostly focuses on cooperative fights against computer controlled characters/events. There are lots of things you can buy with real money if you want to though. You can go up against other players too but most of them are extremely high-level and so have totally overpowered weapons and ships and shields who have been playing for years.
+There's a lot of stuff to see if you just want to fly around and look at stuff in your ship but that can get boring too. Afterall, you don't HAVE to do missions unless you want to see everything the game has to offer. But there is a lot you can see regardless, this being an at least partially open-world game. Lots of stuff for groups of friends to do also.
+/-You can play as the federation, Klingons or Romulans. I only played as the federation as I heard that the Klingons and Romulan factions don't feature campaigns or missions that are as well developed. Unfortunately the Borg and others are not a playable race. While there is a lot to see and do, the game will not let you do whatever you might be able to imagine. (I had hoped for a short while when I first heard about this game to be a good-guy rogue borg cube (we will assimilate some of you if you, you know, want to be assimilated) and I couldn't. Boo hoo!
+/-Classic, largely orchestral star trek music (which might not be for you if you don't like that very much or find it boring like I do) which can get repetitive over time and usually has a self-righteous feeling to it.
+/-Adequate though authentic sound effects.
+/-The game has levels to keep missions difficult and challenging and to reward you with leveled-up equipment as you progress. However, while thoughtful, as this increases replayability, this feature is implemented in a potentially buggy manner. If you enter a mission with a high-level friend and then that friend has to leave then you might be stuck in the mission and will need to find some way of escaping without being destroyed and thus automatically restarting the mission at that high level. You need to escape somehow and then re-enter it for the level to switch back to where your lower-leveled character is so you don't get almost instantly destroyed by high-level NPC enemies. The enemy difficulty leveling should ideally occur in real-time if possible. Still, this is not an issue which necessarily comes up a lot unless you have friends who are all very high level when you are not.
-Awkward controls even with the detailed keyboard and control re-mapping options. This game will make Just Cause 2's controls seem intuitive and streamlined. It might even make the controls in Mirror's Edge feel streamlined. System Shock 2's controls are easier. FreeSpace 2, a detailed space fighting sim, has easier controls than the space battles in this game.
-I mean, the game simultaneously seems to want you to use it like a menu and a 3d game which is usually obtuse. It is difficult to figure out how to do ANYTHING. Equipping a weapon or any other item is needlessly difficult. Indeed most menus, statistics and controls are needlessly obtuse and confusing giving this game a frustratingly long learning curve. I believe IGN's review said it best when it said something like how everything that is usually simple in a game is complex and everything that should be complex in a game (like traveling from one star system to another at warp speed) is oddly simple. This mostly just involves little, irritating things but all these little things combine to make a frustratingly difficult learning curve and this is the number one reason why I don't want to play this game anymore. Also, I have other games I'd rather play as a result despite this game's wonderful community. Even the interstellar map of the galaxy, for example, is hard to understand. Homeworld, this isn't.
-Occasional glitches and bugs throughout.
-The game's friendly AI is mediocre at best and the game's enemy AI is really bad. That's not the worst thing so far as fights are concerned though. The worst thing is that there simply isn't a lot of tactical depth to this game. Stay out of enemy weapon range (or line of sight if you are running around on the ground or a space station or inside a ship) and hit the enemy with your own weapons as quickly and as often as you can. Most tactical depth beyond basic maneuvering consists of figuring out which combination of abilities, special powers, shields and weapons to use at different times and against different groups of enemies (which is often not a very straightforward matter (which is fine in itself). However, this layer of tactical depth is often implemented in an extremely confusing manner which has a long and arduous learning curve to figure out (unless you have good friends (like I did) who will take an enormous amount of time to tell you what to do.) Unfortunately, once you have a combination of abilities, powers, shields and weapons selected, battles would have become a simple button-mashing frenzy if it were not for needing to wait for each item and weapon to recharge between each shot. You can opt to fire one weapon at a time though or fire them all at once in salvos (which is almost always best anyhow). Regardless, after you've decided on a loadout and inventory, the battles themselves get boring FAST.
-Maneuvering, either with your character or with your spacecraft feels cumbersome and restrictive, even with all the myriad ways of customizing your controls. The AI doesn't do much better though (and your own AI team mates and NPC characters have a nasty tendency to get stuck in corners or in tight hallways causing many of the game's areas to have uncharacteristically (uncharacteristic for the world of Star Trek even) large hallways and open spaces.
-You probably have to really love star trek to want to play this game. At least this is the way it was with me. The game world is a messy hodge-podge of every star trek episode and movie ever made and while this can be great for people looking for nostalgia and gives you a huge variety of enemies to fight the world can seem like a real chaotic mess unless you are fairly familiar with most star trek episodes and movies which have ever come out. The game tries to introduce you to things though but this game requires a LOT of reading text boxes to find out what's going on, almost from one minute to the next.
--The game world attempts to control overcrowding and lag issues by having different "instances" or sort of sub-space like parallel universes running at the same time. To actually join your friends and see them you have to figure out how to join their particular "instance."

I just really didn't care for this game. Mostly, I hated the look of it. I think the pastels are supposed to be soothing but I found them difficult to see. Sometimes the monochromatic pieces are so simlarly colored it can be difficult to discern where one piece ends and the next starts. I also found the background to have a vaguely dystopian-nightmare feel that made me uneasy.
As for gameplay, the idea is interesting but there were times where it was hard to tell what the solution was without trial and error because the pieces simply did not line up where they should based on the angles being displayed. For instance, it might look like one piece is totally on another piece until you change the view and then you relize it's not aligned and is hanging over the edge. That would be fine if it was part of the challenge but it doesn't appear to be. Hanging off the edge doesn't seem to effect the physics at all in some puzzles (I.e. a piece that isn't aligned correctly over another piece when viewed from multiple angles will still behave as if it is when solving the puzzle). This can make what should be a game based on intuition and logic a little wonky at times, which is not the same as being difficult.
I also found, next to the sort of dreamsape music, the sound made when you fail a level is harsh and jarring.
Overall, I just really didn't like anything about this game except for its core idea. The music, sounds, colors, menus, gameplay, choices- all of that was a turn-off for me.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing

There is a game called Endless Ocean where all you do is explore the ocean, documenting the wildlife. I thought that was such a cool concept and I played it a ton. While there are a few differences, FarSky reminds me of Endless Ocean.
First of all, FarSky is about being stuck at the bottom of the ocean, trying to survive while you slowly try to rebuild your submarine. You start with a base to live in and to restore your oxygen and a few tools: a drill to mine resources (you will need these to craft other things, such as weapons), an extractor to passively get resources for you (you have to place it somewhere outside), and some food.
You have to get resources, use those resources to craft things, kill animals to get food (or alternatively plant certain foods), and slowly get your submarine parts that are scattered throughout the ocean. The game is so simple, yet so full of life. Think 3D Minecraft, but underwater.
As I mentioned earlier, FarSky reminded me of Endless Ocean, and it does! There is a big ocean to explore with many creatures to see. I really felt immersed while playing. Every time I play, I always find something new, whether it be a creature or an area. It really feels like you're in the ocean, which I think is important for a game like this.
In conclusion, FarSky has a charm that is rarely seen. The concept of being stranded underwater and having to adapt to your environment and survive is fun and I'd love to see more come out of it. As I'm writing this review, the game is on Humblebundle. I would highly recommend getting it just for this game! You don't have to pay much and it's definitely worth a lot more than that.
Also, keep note that while there is a good amount of content, there is definitely a lot of room for more and sometimes can feel a little lacking. Multiplayer would be a really nice addition.

The core ideas here aren't bad, but with no roadmap for improvement this game isn't (and never will be?) the creative sandbox it looks like it should be.
The survival gameplay is a cinch to master. After you realize the drill can drill the floor, and that the floor's texture determines what you get (iron, copper, sand, etc), you'll have no shortage of ingredients. The only threats left are pressure, air supply, and various nasty fish. While the first two are easy to dodge, the viscious fish are unpredictable and more irritating than challenging - once you figure out how to actually attack (intuitive controls lacking), you'll have no trouble fending them off. (but escape is rarely an option - they will hunt you till you get into safety, hence the irritation). All in all, the survival starts off exhilarating but rapidly becomes a chore.
Like in certain other creative sandbox games (which may or may not contain mines), there is a nighttime during which the nasty fishes are more numerous and aggressive. The idea being (I think?) that you go into your base and build amazing cool base parts. Except that the base can only be made from floor, walls, walls with glass, ladder to another floor, plant pot, and 5 crafting stations. Oh, and a stool and a table and some chests. This means that, aside from building an enormous tunnel, there's not much you can do. There's no creativity, the components are extremely restricted in how they can be combined, and the result is generic, boring and bland. The screenshots of the base are the most you'll ever achieve (aside from creating a boring, extremely large pile of boxes filled with plant pots). Also, with night time being "death time" outside the base, you spend half the time idling around your boring cube, which on the plus side is an ideal time to make real-world coffee. Perhaps a bed to sleep the remainder of the night away would improve things  but...
That said, even if there was a bed, the collection of minerals is equally boring. You can either stare at a rockface with a drill or set up an extractor. Either way the minerals are ultimately just a means to upgrade your base (or reach more minerals), which, as I described above, isn't really worth doing.
Once you figure out how to do stuff (e.g. drill the terrain and that spears aren't weapons without a speargun rawr), you can quickly build the highest level suit and complete the "story". There's no reason to stick around after that, and the story definitely isn't reason enough to play this game. All in all, I don't recommend this game.

Helen’s Mysterious Castle:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
What do we know about Helen? Well, she is a young girl of few words, she can’t read but loves a good steak! Helen’s true forte is bravery. She will embark on an epic journey, fighting enemies twice her size in exciting dungeons. Are you ready to play Helen’s Mysterious Castle? I knew you would be!
Helen’s Mysterious Castle is an RPG maker game where you will take the protagonist “Helen” into mazes and dungeons on a floating Island.
The game will start in a cute cottage where Helen lives with her brother, Ardis. Our heroin can’t read at this stage and does not speak either. She has been advised by her brother not to venture into the northern ruins as they are full of dangers. Well, what did she do? Exactly the opposite. She picked up a longbow and started her perilous journey.
As she progresses into her journey, she will encounter a vast number of enemies, such as Orcs, Slimes, Goblins, Skeletons, Zombies, Griffiths, Harpy and many more. However, her first real challenge is to defeat the demon king and his four henchmen – Lord of Darkness, Lord of Poison, Lord of Paralysis and Lord of Silence. Be prepared for epic battles!
A battle will start as soon as Helen touches an enemy. Depending on how far along you are in the game, you might have a selection of weapons (melee and range), magic spells (from books) and protective gears to choose from. The fighting mechanisms are very simple and easy to use. When Helen wins a battle, she is awarded experience points which you can use to upgrade weapons, spells and armour. Later on, Helen will be able to receive upgrades at the local blacksmith, too. Make sure you talk to all characters within the town when you reach that stage to progress further into the story. A quick tip for you - Helen will come across sparkling waters from time to time; these waters will regenerate her health when she drinka it. Also, make sure to break all pots you see laying around; some of them have additional health points hiding in them. Chesta and books (spells) can also be found in the dungeons.
I am absolutely amazed at how good this game is, and pleasantly surprised at its price point, at only $2. Fabulous content and re-playability.

I give this one a 9/10 overall and here's why:
Story
It starts off like an old school RPG with no instructions and barely any dialogue, but the reason behind that comes later in the story and that changes everything, so don't be thrown off until after you've beaten your first boss. It is quite interesting and I did actually like some of the characters. I was left with a sense of accomplishment when it was all over, which is nostalgic in a way.
Gameplay
Here's where things get interesting. The battle system is like something I've never played before, it's really unique. Wait time is the biggest factor when it comes to battles. NOW, HERE'S THE REASON FOR THE -1: You cannot load the game from a previous save after you die, you have to restart the game and then hit continue. Kind of a pain, but not too big of a deal. ALSO IMPORTANT: REFINE YOUR WEAPONS AND ITEMS OR ELSE YOU'LL BE SORRY. I got stuck on one of the final bosses because of this. After you get far enough, a certain person is no longer available, so you cannot refine items which made it impossible to progress.
Sound
Music is an easy 10/10. Sound effects and soundtrack fit this game perfectly especially during the boss fights and towards the end of the game.
Graphics
Good looking game for the price. The animations are well done and the battles are more interesting because of that.
Final Thoughts
Buy this game. This was an interesting journey and I think anyone would be able to enjoy it. It's simple, yet takes some strategy, but one is still left with a sense of accomplishment. So far, this has been one of my favorite games on Steam. I'm looking forward to a sequel, for sure.

This game is great.  First time I played this game I was amazed with the graphics.  Definitely an improvement over Skyrim's.  The next thing I noticed was the voice acting.  Unlike the previous games that primarily used text, npcs will now actually talk to you.  After only 30 minutes of playing I noticed something that made this game stand out from all the other games.  It has an absolutely EPIC combat engine, based entirely on skill but focusing even more so on creating smooth, satisfying animations.  The first time I killed an Argonian slave was the moment I will never forget.  One more strong point of the game, before I focus on the negative ones.  This game was designed around stealth.  Caves, forts, ruins, and houses always give you the opportunity to use stealth rather than raw strength or use of magic.  It's entirely possible that you won't even have to kill one guy to complete 90% of the quests!  Now it's time I warn you of the game's weak spots, for there are many.  The main quest is a very cliche "defeat the Dunmer trying to turn himself into a god at a volcano" kinda deal.  It's obvioiusly stolen from Lord of the Rings and doesn't appeal to me or other loyal Elder Scrolls fans.  I have also noticed that this game has forgotten about the role play aspect of The Elder Scrolls.  No longer does combat, lockpicking, speechcraft and other skills rely on character skill, but now they rely on player skill.  There is also the problem of bad landscape designers; it all seems very bland and a little too repetitive.  In Skyrim we had mountains, Oblivion we had wonderful hills and forests... in this game we have nothing good, nothing new.  Feels like I'm exploring my neighborhood, not a new fantastical world.  Aside from those main issues, there are only a small amount of bugs and quircks about the game.  For example, the loading times are ridiculous when compared to newer games like Skyrim.  If you're looking for a beautiful, action packed, incredibly realistic game, then this is the one you want.  If you liked the original Elder Scrolls games such as Skyrim, Oblivion, and Elder Scrolls Online that focus more on role play and, at least for Skyrim, a good storyline then I'd suggest you skip this one and wait for The Elder Scrolls VI.  Don't take my word for it though!  Buy it and try it out for yourself!

Indie Game The Movie shows exactly how hard and tough the lives of indie game developers can be. Let's be honest, we all take these developers for granted. Ever since the release of Braid, one of the first commercial and financially successful games, there's been a crazy amount of new indie games and developers.
But what drives these developers, and at what cost ? Indie Game The Movie shows just that. Indie developers shouldn't be compared to big studio companies. It would be easy to do that, but it would also be unfair to these people. These developers all show that it requires an incredible amount of dedication, passion and - sometimes - even isolation to work on their game - AND finish it. It's not just about the money; these games are something personal. And, as gamers, we get the chance to find out what that something exactly is or could be.
A great documentary that all serious gamers should see.

Wunderdoktor is a lovely little game. Surgeon Simulator by way of paper-collage animal-people, you are tasked with curing a bunch of strange boils and parasites and ghosts from your patients before they snuff it. Its artstyle is impressive, music is quirky and fun. The narrative is good enough to keep you going, though nothing super special.
My main issue with the game is its feeling of being 'on-rails'. Whereas in something like Trauma Centre you would have to pick the right treatments for the job, Wunderdoktor has you fix the patients in a specific order. This can be problematic when you really just want want one swinging parasite out of the way but nooo, you have to stitch this together first. Things like that.
Still, very enjoyable overall. Would recommend.

7/10 objective rating
PROS:
- Art style is very cool, and visually rich
- Dexterity mini-games are varied enough to feel fresh almost every patient.
- Story plot is engaging enough to see through to the end
- Sound design and soundtrack is subtle, yet perfectly tuned to the gamplay
- Mini-games a good balance between easier ones and more challenging ones that make you kill a patient over and over again. The final patient is very much the hardest level of the game...!
- Creative names and character design.
CONS:
- Confusing as to how long the game is (at one point you see something pop up as an act 8 thing...but there are only 5 acts)
- A bug occurred where I had to restart my game (a pill overlay stayed on my screen even though I had restarted with the patient)
------------------------------------------------------------------

So, I got this game for free through Humble Bundle... In a way, it's bizarre that this... thing, actually has a price, as it's effectively a demo for the full game. If you can't be arsed to make your way through the whole of this review, all you need to know is, this is a great way to make you realise how this game could be fun with friends, but not on your own, and not as it is.
Being older than I appear, and growing up in a time when Steam Sales would sound like magic beans rather than allowing me a way to convert pocket money into actual jollies, I would spend my time leafing through the back pages of White Dwarf, imagining what it would be like to be able to play the games contained within. One such was Talisman, and I spent a terrifying amount of time imagining what the fabled game would actually be like to play.
Now I know. I'm really glad my 12 year old self got that gift for free.
Should you pay for it? No. No. The game could potentially be fun with friends, and this version is fine for working out the mechanics of the actual game, which you are definitely not buying here. It's kind of astonishing they still charge you extra to buy the tutorial, although I have been informed it was originally released as a work in progress before the multiplayer was released. That still doesn't mean there is any point in paying for it now, and playing it alone seems desperately sad. I cannot imagine why anyone would benefit from playing this game rather than the main one.

FarSky is a game that really surpassed my expectations.
I had seen images of this game here and there and they never really blew me away, but I decided to give it a go and WOW was I in for a treat.
Ok so I made a mistake at the start of the game by pressing sandbox...It gave me a seed which had no gold in sight, and copper was way below my starting maximum pressure...but I learned the game's mechanics with that and it felt pretty fun. So I went to the story mode.
SPOILERS BELOW
-----------------------------------------
Day 1 - My submarine was destroyed through some unknown means...I was still able to communicate with my friend on the surface through voice comms. I had a limited supply of oxygen but she directed me to a nearby underwater base. It had many supplies which I could use for some time to come.
Day 3 - I fought a shark last night. He constantly came at me and wouldn't stop. His teeth versus my knife! I was rewarded with a lot of meat to last me for a couple days.
Day 5 - With the help of a couple extractors, I managed to craft a new copper helmet which allowed me to dive much further than normal. I found a huge underwater base with lots of chests full of helpful items! However the base had leaks. I discovered that I needed to repair these, after which the water drained SLOWLY out of the base.
Day 6 - I travelled out to retrieve the fourth piece of my submarine when I discovered a Droid. I powered it on and discovered it would not only follow me, and carry some items, but it would also fire small but accurate harpoons at anything that decided to attack me. This proved invaluable for my future hunting trips.
Day 7 - 6/9 Submarine parts acquired. I didn't have long left to go. I improved my armor so that I could dive to the max depths and travel for long distances without resurfacing for air and even go toe to toe with a shark and live.
Day 9 - My final voyage. I would pick up the remaining two parts of my submarine on this trip. Along the way I found a second droid! If things continued like this I'd have my own personal, underwater army. We neared part number 8 where I found some crystal. This stuff is rare! Might as well drill it and take some home eh? Nope. Not 1, not 2, but 3 Kraken surrounded me and we fought a brutal fight. My droids were like machine guns while the kraken took turns launching themseleves at me. I had to keep munching away at cooked shark meat I had in reserves. During the fight, the most epic battle music I've heard in a while, was playing making the battle all the more enjoyable. An anglerfish took a particular dislike for me and joined in the fight. I made quick work of him with my harpoon and focused my attention on these seemingly invulnerable kraken. Finally we broke through their ranks as one fell to the might of my harpoon. The other two quickly followed as I celebrated a victory. But time was running out. I still had to find the last piece of my sub with two minutes remaining on my oxygen. I pulled out my propeller and went full speed towards the last beacon.
As I rose to the surface I felt pretty sad I had to leave my droid friends below. They helped me so much....but I missed the feel of dry land. The choice was obvious. I hated being hunted at night and even though the view at night was amazing, it was time to head home.
Pros
- Amazing Underwater atmosphere.
- Variety of Sea Creatures.
- Depth Progression system.
- Easy base crafting system.
- Beautiful views especially through glass.
- Relaxing sounds.
- Pretty fun gameplay.
- Time consuming!
Cons
- Only one type of Knife which does low damage.
- Wish it could go deeper.
- Every predator can be beaten without ever taking damage yourself by simply attacking them before they attack you.
Overall this game was very enjoyable. I spent over 4 hours playing this (offline) and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Buy it. Now.

So i wanted to pop in here (sad pun) and give my recommendation/review of this game. HuniePop (to me) feels targeted to thee different types of gamers who may enjoy the atmosphere and gameplay. The three types (as i would put it) are the Anime Fan, the Puzzle/Gem matching fan or the Completionist.  Any combination of two out of those three types will likely find something here to enjoy, though if you feel you only fit into one catagory or none; you may want to consider this game a pass.
For the Anime  Fan:
Me personally, I am a fan of anime shows such as High School DxD, Rosario Vampire, Sekirei, etc. and as a fan i can say there are minor similarities between the plots of those shows and HuniePop.  Essentially, you are the perverted/awkward main character with sex on the brain thrust into a world where abnormal things are happening and you need to adapt.  HuniePop, nowhere near as extreme as the shows has the main character visited by a "fairy" who teaches you/him/her how to talk to girls.  The main goal is to have sex with each of the (approx.) 6 characters.  The art style in the game is very much like those animes i mentioned above all the way down to the fan service/nudity.  All in all, the art is good. Voice acting isnt to bad either.
The Completionist:
Id say if you like to unlock things, the game has that in spades.  The game has artwork, items, steam trading cards, achievemnts etc., so theres much to unlock.  Additionally, the goal is to have sex with all the girls so you'll need to travel down every "path" to achieve that goal.  in total, it shouldnt take more then 5 or so hours to achieve this.  As a side note, for me, the draw here was getting to the final conversation of each girl.  Each girls final diolog was .... interesting, some better then others.
The Puzzle/Gem matching fan:
This isnt really my space, though i do find those games addicting while im playing them.  The challenge for me, is getting to the point where i would pick that style of game over others.  That aside, ive played a variety here and there, and this one (to me) doesnt really stand out over any other.  What was neat though was the "traits". Kind of like an RPG; you rank up traits with a specific currency that you earn by talking with the girls.  The traits help increase your points in the matching game which in tearn earns you another currency to purchase items.  You give the items to girls which increase the amount of that other currency that you get for talking to them that you invest into traits....  and around it goes.
Conclusion:
All in all HuniePop is a good game, though if you'e not an anime fan (specifically of the Ecchi genera), and not a Puzzle/Gem Matching gamer, id say stay away.  If you are either/or AND a completionist to boot then the game may just be up your alley.

I've been playing Hand of the Gods (formerly known as Smite Tactics) since the closed beta, and I've seen that a lot of people have been comparing this to Hearthstone and that it's a carbon copy of it. Well, it does have similarities to Hearthstone, it has it's differences.

Duelyst is one of the many games on Steam, but has gone unnoticed for the most part by some users.
Why do I bring up Duelyst?
Duelyst was released on April 27th, 2016
SMITE Tactics was announced October 19th of the same year.
So that brings up the discussion of Smite Tactics being a copy of Duelyst.
Compare the gameplay, they're exactly the same. Though I'd like to point out one thing.
Smite Tactics originally had the little shard thingy your leader, and it was movable. Which is ALSO in Duelyst.
Duelyst has cards of monsters with their own distinct actives. Just like Tactics does with the gods.
This REALLY needed to be pointed out, the comparisons to Hearthstone have been bugging me since Duelyst has gone unnoticed by the community, with it being even more copied than Hearthstone was. I suggest if you want a more polished version of turn-based strategy, play Duelyst.

This game is not recommended in its current state.
So first things first.  The game is nothing like Xcom, and the reviewer who said that is an idiot.  It's a blatant and shameless use of Xcom's brand, and the devs/publishers would be better served to remove that insulting line from its store page. It's more like Hearthstone (HS) + Heroes of Might and Magic if anything, and is EXACTLY like Duelyst, so use those as comparisons instead.  Until HotG has unit loadouts, ability trees, overworld map, base building, terrain elevation, then it is NOTHING like Xcom.
Gameplay wise the game is extremely snowball-y. Player going first has the attacking advantage with favourable attacks and trades.  This happens in every game ever - fine.  What's worse here than say HS is the existence of Ranged minions.  These are repeatable damage sources that basically gain 'Immune' against melee minions.  As soon as you fall even slightly behind, it will be extremely hard to stabilise.  The board is so small that it may as well not exist.  This is a core mechanic and is not something that can be easily balanced.
UI in deckbuilding is awful.  No search filters - at all. Worse, as soon as you mouse over a card it triggers its animation.  Cool the first couple times, extremely annoying after that.  I'm thinking about how to build a deck and I'm bombarded with loud and annoying animations as I scroll through the cards - again because there is no search filter. Ugh.
If your deck list is too long, you have to click up and down arrows.  No slider, and the mouse wheel only cycles the card collection book.  It's 2017 and they can't even make a context sensitive scroll function?  Also no tool tips on cards in decklist.  As a newbie if I don't know what a keyword does, I have to scroll my book to find the actual card (again no search and annoying animations) to see what the keywords mean.  Even when there is tooltip, the information is poor.  For example, on Zeus card Poseidon, it says replace hero ability with The Kraken.  Well what does The Kraken do?  Game doesn't tell me.
Perhaps things will improve on release.  However at present it is not worth the time and definitely not the money.

This might be my favorite commercial RPGMaker game.
Ever.

The mix of not being able to load a game straight away after defeat (like most RPGs would, which is why they let you usually save before a boss encounter),
the Wait stat that's just a complete trial and error math problem that you can't predict before fighting an enemy (making the constant backtrack from your bed to where you last were defeated even more aggravating)
and the AI being easily manipulated into doing an infinite Guard stance makes this one such a chore to play.
I don't feel accomplished breaking the game's AI or just bashing my head against a wall until it breaks. The little strategy involved with this game's combat system only boils down to seeing whether your chosen skill's Wait stat is equal or lower than the remaining time to the opponent's attack. That's it. Unless after even more tedious hours of this game it finally manages to mix in something worth two brain cells that I just didn't manage to get to before quitting out of sheer boredom. But I doubt it.
For what it's worth, I get why the game gets positive reviews, and I get what people like about it. It's just not enough for me to be excited about.

This game was a huge surprise. It's well reviewed but I had never heard of it so I was skeptical. This game is absolutely
.
The game has a unique battle system that is fun to discover. The system requires you to manage which ability you use based on your enemy's next move and in how much time they will use their ability. By studying your enemy's skillset you can trick them into using specific abilities which would you put you in a better situation. For example, if you start the battle with a quick attack they will start with a defense ability that lasts a while which gives you plenty of time to cast your spells. Learning how to juggle your foe is awesome.
The game also has very well designed levels. Nothing feels inflated for the sake of increasing the game time. Not only do the levels feel right, there are secret passages that lead to new items -- it rewards exploration. The secret passages are super obvious but there are visual cues that hint at something, so if you're attentive you'll be rewarded!
Another aspect that I loved about this game was the story. While the game starts off light on story, it's unravels itself as you explore the castle. I wanted to keep playing to find out what was going to happen next. This feeling was intensified by the awesome cast of characters. If I were to describe them in reference to another game, I'd say they are UnderTale-like. The type of characters I wouldn't be surprised to find in a Saturday morning cartoon. Fun and full of personality.
While I loved the characters, I think some of the charm is removed by the naming convention.
The protagonist is Helen. I mean, might as well call it Brittney's Mysterious Castle. It's not a huge deal but it is a little immersion breaking, doesn't quite fit the setting.
Some of the translation was a little sloppy. There were a few typos (albeit not many) but quite a few broken characters.
Let's be honest, the game makes use of some of the default assets. That's a bit of a turnoff and is one of the reason I was skeptical when I was going into the game. While Satra designed extra frames for these characters, they are still part of the default assets, it is quite the turn off.
Combat system and enemy design encourages adaptation. Soundtrack is great.

Freakin' loved this game! It has a cute and mysterious charm. The gameplay is simple but captivating. I enjoyed uncovering the mystery of the story each step of the way. The music fit well with the game at all times. Also, the battle sprites were just so awesome. I seriously wondered how interesting it would be to have multiple characters in your party using this battle system. The dialogue felt a little rushed as it neared the end of the game but it was okay. This game inspired me to get back into RPG Maker, so at the time, I went and bought VX Ace, and then eventually MV!

A fun little RPG that combines the turn based elements of Final Fantasy, a spice of battle from Fire Emblem, and a wait system of that similar to Grandia. It's very light hearted with clean comedy thrown into the pot. If you're looking for a break from serious titles, give Helen a shot.
What pulled me into the game was the sprite work and battle system. The sprite work is wonderful to watch and the battle system is simple to the point of breathing. The game is a walk in the park, but it still takes effort and time walking though it. Like a good walk to wherever you enjoy, you'll find it relaxing and colorful. Instead of filling you in with so much detail like stinky plot dumps, the game drops you in with less and makes you take in the journey more.
Helen's Mysterious Castle is a game I really enjoyed, and that's the most important thing. The developer made this game to be enjoyed, not one to struggle through. So if you find yourself having a tough time, it's alright to sit back and find some more experience or find that Heal spell you clearly missed.
* Light Hearted RPG
* Pocket Change Value
+/- Few hours in length

Definitely worth your $2. The game itself is a pretty standard RPG, although the timing-based combat mechanic is really unique and interesting. That said, the art, music, and writing in this is far, far beyond the quality you'd expect from a $2 RPGMaker game. Really enjoyed my 7 hours with this game, right through to the credits.
Some other reviews have called this game very unfair, and I thought I agreed at first, but it turns out I hadn't figured out the weapon/magic upgrade mechanics. (In fairness, the game spells out none of it; you're on your own. Hit Esc outside of battle, pick the thing you want to upgrade, and spend EXP on it. Suddenly those bosses are much more reasonable.)
Just a charming, wonderful little game, and the $2 price point can't be beat.

Star Trek Online (STO) is a free to play MMORPG for Windows PC.
I have been playing on and off since the start of Star Trek Online,  Just added STO on Steam just long enough to write the review.  I have 1 account that i paid money on and 3 accounts that are Free to Play.  I use the STO standalone game client only.
Positves:
STO is great if you want to play for FREE as a simple starship captain in the Star Trek MMO universe.  You don't have to pay any real money to experience the complete Star Trek universe.
You can make 4 different faction captains ( Federation, Romulan, Klingon, 23rd Century Starfleet ) on 1 free account.  There are three classes of captains:  Science = Mage, Engineering = Tank / Support, Tactical = DPS.
The level cap is now level 60, afterward you earn specialization points when reaching another level.  Plenty of extra specializations and traits you can add to your captain to improve ground and space combat.  You can mix your skill points between the three class trees.
It is easy enough to get to level 50 in a short amount of time, but going to level 60 will take some more grinding and time.
PWI does give away stuff for STO.  Check the website news often, check the store, attend in-game events, check your email. Check google for reward codes, either free or for donations on other websites.
Basic gear is plentyful in mob loot drops. Mission rewards and Faction Reputation grinding provide your higher tier gear.  Crafting is ok way to improve your gear, with grinding.
Participate in an established guild to buy better gear with in-game currency.
Plenty of free cosmetic customization is available for your captains, bridge crew and ships.
Plenty of PVE missions that are soloable and a few Co-Op battle areas.  Plenty of missions and areas for you to explore with you and your 4 bridge crew. There is player created missions in the Foundry to try out.  Plenty of Events to play throughout the year.
Free players get a free basic ship each rank up to tier 4, each modeled after classic ships from Star Trek universe. You can buy some extra tier 5 and 6 ships from the exchange, if you can earn enough energy credits or if you find free giveaway codes or earn enough dilithium.  3 types of ships: Escort = DPS, Science = Support, Cruiser = Tank.
Has a mini-game that you can send your duty officers and your fleet of ships on their own missions offline and you reap the rewards of their success and other mini-games for different activities.
STO is Free to Play friendly, not as bad with limitations added to free accounts as other games. Usually the e-mail / chat unlocks with 21 plus hours in-game.  Inventory and bank is big enough, has in-space access to bank and email.  Free players have enough slots in the Exchange to sell items.
-------------------------------------
Negatives:
Free to play accounts are limited in number of bridge officer slots, smaller bank and bags space.
The game is still very buggy, but it has been Expanded, nerfed, simplified, reworked and changed over the years.  The game is pretty laggy at times, it has not always been.  Lately, The devs keep breaking old things and not fixing anything.  Game client crashes and disconnections happen often now.  But when the game works for you, it is great.
If you are into playing PVP, forget about PVP, new players will die every time in a match with veterans, DPS crazy players and whale players. Matchmaking is non-existant, and nobody queues for public pvp.
PWI is milking this game for money, but if you can buy PWI money cards they can be used to buy STO stuff.  You have to spend real money to play in style or be competative at elite end level content.  You can grind for the in-game currency to convert to store coin, but it is equivalent to a job.
Give it a try. Play it for FREE only.

One of the greatest games I have ever played.
I just want to highlight the skill system here, for some of the good and inherently bad things about it.
The thing about the skill system in Morrowind is that it has many skills and possibilities, but it is solely based on the gods of RNG. The thing that's so bad about this (or, based on your perspective- good), is that everything you do is based on a percentage, a number, a sliver of chance as a new character. This means that even if you are an extremely powerful level 50 character, mastering all there is to know in the school of swordplay, you'll still have a chance of completely missing the enemy and doing no damage.
Another thing I see people fail to realise in their nostalgia is the fatigue system. There is literally no reason for me not to be able to throw fireballs at people's faces because my Fatigue is low. And because of this, the chance of casting is significantly lowered...that's all I'll say about that. It's incredibly aggravating.
The Graphics...they're extremely dated and about 13 years old. They haven't exactly aged well. But although this game doesn't look terrible, it can still be jarring for a new player to come from Skyrim or Oblivion into this game.
The Gameplay isn't incredible, but still fun. Even despite it's odd skill system. It's Classic RPG fundamentals are, in a way, the lifeblood of this game, despite it's oddities. In no other game can you walk up to a slow-moving mudcrab at level 1, completely miss every swing, and get yourself killed. Despite this, you can do anything you want, kill anyone or anything you want, steal, plunder, or even become the Grandmaster of almost every guild. Despite this, the game does NOT hold your hand. You have to work for what you want. Don't have enough gold for that Dreugh Helmet? Go to that dwarven ruin over the hill, kill everything inside, and find the treasures within. This game really captures the scope and expanse you would expect of an entire continent, even in just the space of an island. You can be running through the rolling hills of the grazelands, and the next minute you're in the middle of Molag Amur, in the midst of pools of lava and ash. That being said, it still takes a while for that transition. Even for an old game, the map is huge.
The Story is one of the pinnacles of this game. In more recent years, the story has not been bland, per se- but rather, it has been turned into this constant story that the game will try to make you feel inclined to stay with until that story has ended. For example, in Skyrim the main story was very heavily forced upon you. They try to create this false sense of "urgency" that you just do not find in this game. You are thrust into this world with no money, no hope, and no future. You are not respected as an outlander. People don't like the idea of integrating the ignorant "n'wahs" into their society. As with anything in this game, you must earn their respect. There is tons of side-quests which, I will argue, are about 30-40% "Go fetch this for me" quests or, "Go kill this man for me". But even in these quests, Morrowind most definitely has an extensive story to tell, and quite an enthralling one at that.
The DLC in this game is phenominal! Much like the other Elderscrolls games, the downloadable content in this game is extremely good. (Minus the horse armor from Oblivion!) Rich, and deep with story- the activites and things to do in them are quite extensive. The first time I had gone to the Clockwork City in Tribunal, I KNEW that I would remember that experience in gaming forever. I was in awe of this world created by a man-turned-god. Which is a feeling you don't get in most games today.
All-in-all, I think that this is a great game- and definitely stands the test of time today. With a few mods (which are still being made in 2015), this game can definitely net you countless hours of mudcrab-bashing fun. Definitely worth picking up, if you haven't already.

FarSky is a first-person survival game set in an underwater world. The goal is simple, you need to survive and find all the parts of your broken submarine. Without it you stuck on the bottom of the ocean.
Pros:
Pleasant visuals and nice sound design ensures the creepy underwater atmosphere. Gameplay is solid, sometimes maybe a bit dull due to the weird behavior of some species. Exploration is fun, going into deeper parts of the ocean and encountering new dangerous creatures is frightening. Crafting is well made, there are a handful of stuff that can be crafted, most of them useful. Crafting recipes locked with the availability of the resource needed for each piece. Resources found in the world are nicely placed and varied. Base building is one thing that can keep you going for a while.
Cons:
Sometimes the underwater world can be overwhelming. It is too easy to gain enough resources on the first playthrough, making progress faster and rare ores useless after a few extractor placed. Food can be harvested too quickly, eliminating the need of hunting for fish. Some weird stuff with the building section. The game is not long on the first run and does not provide much to do once the story object is completed.
Overall, I really enjoyed my first playthrough with the game. I do not really want to play it again. It does not have much content left I suppose. I would like to see a second game with a little bit more to explore and build. Still, this is a worthy game, a nice addition to a genre filled with zombie survivals.

You "evolve" a creature through various stages. It starts out very simple as the different game types are mini games. Only the mini games become longer and longer, and their complexity stays that of mini games. There is no depth. The final space age takes this to the extreme.
Example 1: Every colony you build (3 per planet), you have to drag and drop 8 turrets halfway accross the screen, then you have to set 3 factories, 1 entertainment building and about 7 houses in a simple pattern (again by drag and drop halfway across the screen). Then, if your planet is attacked, you should also check each colony individually by flying to each one in your space ship, and replace any lost buildings by drag and drop halfway accross the screen.
Example 2: The enemy "AI" doesn't rebuild. To take an enemy planet, fly there, destroy some buildings, fly back to base, refuel, do some missions/alerts/trades in between (because they keep piling up), refuel again, fly to the enemy planet, destroy some more buildings, repeat until planet surrenders.
Example 3: In the 4th stage, there is 1 land unit, which will be replaced with 1 air unit when air units become available.
Example 4: In the 3rd stage, the only way to wipe out an enemy tribe is to wait for them to attack you, kill the attacker with your special ability, then wipe out the remaining enemies at their camp. Repeat 4 times.
There are a few things that hurt the game apart from the boring gameplay:
- It occasionally crashes, but  rarely enough that it's acceptable. Except that there are no autosaves. It only asks you to save on exit (unless it crashes).
- Login is very annoying. You need an EA account. Not sure what for, since there's absolutely no online content (was removed from the game after release).
- Controls in the 5 stages have nothing in common, except that they all work with mouse and an optional keyboard. It seems the 5 mini games have been designed by completely different teams.
This game is not made for adults or adolescents, it's made for kids - and for kids there's no educational value, unlike Civilization, which I played at 10. If you expect a game even remotely similar to Civ, Homeworld, MoO2, or C&C, this game is nothing like any of them. I cannot recommend this game even on a sale, unless you buy it for the creature editor. There are plenty of free to play games that are better, and hundreds of 2$ strategy titles on GoG that are a couple leagues above Spore.

FarSky is a survival game where the main character is cast into the ocean depths after his submarine got destroyed. Your goal is to find all the submarine pieces or succumb to your death. As any survival game, FarSky has a hunger bar and instead of the thirst bar it has an Oxygen bar. Scattered around the bottom of the ocean are the parts for you submarine, but also random droids, dirt patches, coal patches that look like oil and chests filled with items or gold coins. To survive you will either have to farm plants or hunt for fish, while upgrading your base and equipment. My experience so far was pretty negative. It feels like an undeveloped game, as if it were still Early Access and ever since it was published it didn't get a single update. Overall it is all very unintuitive. The hammer tool makes no sense, it took me 10 minutes to realize that somehow I removed the roof of my house and rather than another block, so building is bad unless you don't mind doing mistakes and not fixing them. There is no clock and you will have little warning of when it turns to night. The first time it happened I died. All the warning I got was "It's getting dark" - and it got dark and I was eaten alive. The crafting system is pretty bad and a lot of the times you will accidentally craft something you don't need because all it takes is a press of a button. The game also doesn't feature a save button, but instead a "Save and Quit", so if you're scared of it crashing like it did for me you will have to constantly quit the game to the main menu. Another thing I want to add that so far I have no idea what the gold coins are for, perhaps for the final score? Many of the things are left unexplained and are random. Overall the game feels pretty barren.
>I'd give it a 4/10. Cool concept, poorly executed
>Pros: The graphics are pretty nice, interesting concept, offers several game-modes, tight controls.
>Cons: Bugs, crashes, can't kill anything unless you got a Knife or other weapon(drills won't do anything), poor combat/crafting/building systems, not many explanations, no way to save the game without quitting, bad day/night cycle and you've got nothing to do while it's night time.
EDIT: The game now stopped counting my playtime, and when I play it I am "Online" rather than in-game.

I really enjoy this approach to a card game. It's pretty refreshing actually. If HiRez refines this game more I see it being a pretty big player in the genre in a couple years. However, as much I like the game, it has some pretty brutal flaws that need to be worked out still. The games card crafting system is pretty straight forward. The rate you acquire the materials to craft the cards is sloth like.
In order to craft the cards you want, it requires you to scrap your spare cards to get teh materials. New/ F2P players have almost 0 spare cards for a very long time. A player might not get a single spare card until they've opened 20 or more packs. It took me about 18 packs to get 3 spare cards. I got 7 materials for crafting. Most of the cards that you would want to craft are in the hundreds. It's not balanced properly in that regard. I think the packs are overpriced and should cost 200 instead of 300.
While it's true you gain 10 gold per win which is better than Hearthstone that gives 10 for every 3 wins, The packs in that game are only 100 and you can get usually 1-3 packs a day just from logging on for your dailies fairly easily. You are more likely to get only 1 a day due to the cost of packs in HotG.
The rate at which you are able to collect cards and progress through the game is greatly staggered by this issue imo. The game is basically pushing people into making cash purchases  in order to compete and have decks that enable you to continue progressing. I'm hopeful this will all be balanced out in future updates.
That out of the way, the actual combat in the game is pretty enjoyable. It is engaging and entertaining. The animations of the minions are pretty cool. The card abilities are fun. Overall I really like what this game is. The gameplay is a mix of your typical card game with a minion based combat system reminescent of the battles in Heroes of Might and Magic. If this game is taken proper care of it has a bright future. Definitely a diamond in the rough. Would recommend to anyone that likes online card games or tactics games. Just be aware that at some point you might hit a serious wall in your progress.

I will start this review off saying I have played and beaten every installment released in the Metal Slug Series. I would definitely recommend this port of the classic arcade sidescroller! The visual and control options are not super in-depth but meet every requirement the average gamer would ask for. This game is tough, but can be played at 4 different difficulty levels which is helpful for new players. Local multiplayer is great fun and the campaign can be beaten in one sitting, which although short is good for group sessions of gameplay. The artwork is absolutely stunning and makes the game worth picking up all on its own. The unlock-able concept art is a really cool feature that will be appreciated by long time fans of the series. The varying environments are unique and provide nice backdrops for each level, and the enemy variation is enough to keep things mixed up. Although the game is short, it has great replayability due to the different difficulty options and the skill it takes to beat the game in arcade mode. Overall I would recommend one to pick this game up, but unless you are a long time fan of the series think about waiting for a sale.

I dare say with a few mods this game rivals skyrim, though they are different enough that you cannot say either is better.

All the rest of the mods are just icing on the cake. The best of them are abot's water life, MCA (fills in the world with npcs), morrowind crafting - need furniture for your lair! - Thanks to mark, recall, and the ability to easily place objects- that stay put- you can make a home anywhere the heart is, anywhere that is captivating to you. This is a feature that the other ES do not have. If you download Grow Televani Towers you can cast spells that grow towers, bridges, and mushroom houses in real time. So you can create your own town anywhere you like. With MC you can build furniture for those houses.
The vampire mods for TES3 are the best. You can even build up an army of vampires and thralls to terrorize and plunder the land.
Advanced bartering makes the monetary system tolerable.
Herbalism 1.1 allows you to gather seeds (if your skill is high) and plant them - to grow herb gardens etc.
With ultimate galleon you can own a big ship with working cannons.
Ashlander tent gives you a mobile home to use as a base for exploration (I like the simpler older versions).
My only advice about modding is, be very conservative. Modding is very addicting. You can easily find yourself spending all your time downloading, searching, and creating them and not spending any time actually playing the game. Then you wonder why the game feels one dimensional (and why there are so many errors).
I also should mention, tho the game is ENORMOUS, the real enjoyment is in the little things.

Okay, first off, I didn't pay $14.99 for this game. It only cost $1 on Humble Bundle currently (you get this, along with 2 other games for $1). Considering what I saw on the trailer, and the price of $1, and now that I got to play the game and actually completed Adventerer mode in slightly under 2 hours (said clear time was like an hour and 3 minutes, dunno why my play time says 2 hours, probably took me 3 minutes to mess with settings, check stuff on the title screen, then start the game). In any case, onto the pros and cons:
Pros:
1. To me, I find this to be quite intriguing and original. At first glance I thought it was Minecraft underwater, but not quite as much, as gathering materials doesn't remove blocks, so in a sense, you can't dig yourself to hell or anything like that if you're a digger.
2. It felt immersive and relaxing, quite a pretty game I must say. Not the "best" graphics in the world, but pleasant enough. I can only imagine how something like this would look with the Unreal engine...
3. Unlike most games, at least this one had somewhat of a story (not a fantastic story, but at least it's there), which gives you a sort of purpose to continue to reach the end goal which is to repair your submarine so you can go home.
And now...
Cons:
1. Not much variety or complexity in equipment you can get. I managed to get the best diving gear quite easily after awhile (never did get the Overpowered Drill as I didn't find enough Crystal). However, that is one of the few problems is that it was fairly easy to get just about everything you needed to succeed, not much challenge really.
2. Enemy AI is predictable. At first, shark got me off guard, I then pulled out my Spear gun and was aiming at it, watching its movement. I noticed it'll swim away a few feet, then turn around and charge directly at you. One spear shot to the shark (doesn't matter where you hit it) will deal damage and cause it to stop charging. For cautious players, wash, rinse, repeat. For those with good aim, you may be able to hit it a few more times as it swims away, preparing for another charge.
3. NO MULTIPLAYER!? WHY!?!?!?
Final thoughts:
There you have it. It's a short single player game if you decide you wanna play Adventurer mode. Probably endless gameplay with Sandbox mode, haven't tried it yet. As for enemies, sharks aren't the only ones in the game, as there are many other oceanic creatures you will discover, who's AI may seem abit better than the shark, but still able to easily get by them. My only disappointment is how little there is in the way of crafting, materials, building, etc. There just isn't much to play with. This game has sooo much potential to be better, loads of potential. It feels as though it's unfinished in a way, however.
Would I recommend?
Considering I paid only a dollar on Humble Bundle (that's $1 USD) for this and 2 other games, then yes. It's worth at least a buck for a decent enjoyable game with a pretty atmosphere. Would I recommend at the $14.99 price however? ABSOLUTELY NOT! Either catch this game on sale, or don't buy it at all.
(Since I can't choose both Thumbs Up and Thumbs Down, I'm giving it a Thumbs Up cause I paid $1 for it! Thumbs Down if you paid $14.99 for it)

This is a beautiful, unique sandbox game that stands out from the crowd with its amazing underwater setting.
The single best part of this game are the visuals. They are just plain beautiful, breathtakingly so at times. The presence of a story with an overarching goal that gives some background is a nice touch that is missing from far too many sandbox style games (even though the story in this game is completely contrived, you're only down maybe 300-400 feet yet they have no way to rescue you so you have to fix your sub...). I like the resource gathering system with automated extractors and mostly unlimited resources once you find suitable deposits.
Unfortunately, this game also has some major issues and really falls short of being a great game and ends up being merely mediocre and not worth the asking price.
First off, although the adventure mode has a basic tutorial built in, it misses some key points that sent me to the wiki to figure out how to play the game.
There's also several game mechanics more or less copied wholesale from minecraft that have no place in this game. This is a near future sci-fi game, why do I have to mine coal to cook my food!?! At night, the predators hunt you down from a mile away, but completely ignore you in the daytime. I've never seen them even try to catch any of the numerous other fish that are more appropriate for their size. At least the penalty from dying is minimal, all your stuff is put in a chest and you get a death marker so you can swim back and retrieve it.
Base building is a lot more difficult than it should be. Your base can take damage from a boss enemy, but the tool to repair the damage is the same as the removal tool, so if you accidentally click on a part that's NOT damaged it's removed and you often have to go outside the base to replace a floor panel you accidentally removed while inside.
Probably the biggest reason why I can't honestly recommend this game at the asking price is that there really isn't much content here. I played through the story for the first time with having to look through the wiki in under 2 hours, and in that time I was able to get the highest tier equipment. The simplistic base building mechanics mean that there's not really much interesting you can do as far as base building (other than trying to reach the surface by building your base up to it I guess) and the lack of multiplayer kills a lot of the replay value.
Overall, a beautiful game that sadly falls short of its potential.

If there is a game somewhere in here, I can't find it. If this game is good, I will never know the answer because it is almost impossible to play. The game has aged to the point of borderline unplayability. And it's not even THAT old... even Unreal Tournament 1999 had better graphics.
The combat is a joke. I could understand a dice-roll system in a game like Knights of the Old Republic, but in this game it is just unnecessary.
AND the enemies on which you use this god-awful combat system are themselves god-awful. They range from tiny slugs to  pterodactyl things.
The UI is the icing on the cake... It makes playing this game feel like trying to paint a mural while on stilts AND rollerskates on a skateboard.
On the plus side, it does give you nearly absolute freedom to do whatever the heck you want, and the main quest is more of a suggested starting point, which I appreciate. But there's a difference between excessive hand-holding (Skyrim) and ACTUALLY GETTING INSTRUCTIONS! They will literally give you quest pointers like "Go 40 paces north, look approximately 12 degrees to your left, and you should see a clump of seaweed. That's your cue to go into the cave located somewhere within a 3-mile radius of the seaweed, and find the Dwarven Ruin within." Does your character think far enough ahead to write this down? NO! "I'll remember it" Pretentious people on the Internet often rail at some games for "not being intelligent" and they praise Half-Life 2 as the pinnacle of intelligent games, when it is essentially just a long hallway. Those people will try to pitch this game as "intelligent, unlike today's games" but pitching poor design as an integral and innovative gameplay element is... well... "it's got heart!"
Unless you played this game 13 years ago and are planning to get it on Steam... please keep in mind everything mentioned above. If poorly-refined gameplay is your cup of tea, by all means, get this game. If not, get Oblivion instead, which is 100x better. (not to mention, actually playable)

Ever since starting off with Skyrim, then eventually buying this game on the Steam store after having seen "Why Morrowind is the best Elder Scrolls game" I loaded up the 2002 game for the first time. I remember that prisoner in the ship telling you that he thinks "We've arrived in Morrowind, I'm sure they'll let us go." then being led off by an Imperial guard, creating your character, and stepping out into the large alien island of Vvardenfell. A province of Morrowind. i remember seeing all the betty netches and berry netches floating around thinking "What the hell are these things?" As well as walking into Balmora and seeing that huge flea shaped Silt strider. To me, this game was a mixture of medievel and alien culture, offering unique landscapes, animals, ingredients and a rich taste of Dunmer culture. I remember arriving in Caius Cosades house, where he is confused as to the instructions of "Reporting to Caius Cosades". I remember waking up in his home after having slept, and being attacked by a Dark Brotherhood Assassin, and in the process of taking hits at the black armoured intruder, accidently hit Caius, causing him to cast a magic spell at me and kill me. I remember one day when I was sick, I sat down at my computer, and attempt to fulfill Caius's first task: Go talk to a man at the Fighters Guild and find out about the 'Neravarine prophecies' and about 'Dagoth Ur' subjects I had no knowledge or understanding of. After having travelled across Balmora to meet the guy, I was told to go to a dwemer ruin and collect a 'Puzzle box' for the man himself. I remember fighting a bunch of bandits while there, and thinking what a strange place I was in. I remember exploring different towns, before oneday, I was instructed to head to Vivec to talk to 3 people about the subjects Caius had an interest in. I remember watching the large canton of the Foreign Quarter render into view as I walked towards, and remember exploring the huge buildings while being greeted by the gold armoured Ordinators in a rude manner. I remember exploring the West Gash region, and coming across a naked nord, wanting "revenge on a witch" and then as we were heading up north, we got seperated. I remember arriving at the city of Ald-Ruhn just as an Ash storm was setting in. Being asked by a woman at the entrance to "find her husband". Well. To sum up this entire review, I will just say that this game has excellant creativity, and stands out against all the other RPG games as a "creative, original, unique and fascinating game" and brings a whole culture with it. I would definitely suggest this game, however if you're an Elder Scrolls fan whos only played Oblivion or Skyrim, you may get frustrated by the "hit and miss" combat mechanics. Or the fact that you have to use your brain more when it comes to quests and finding your way around.
