Hi.
If you're looking at this game and wondering whether to bother because of the negative reviews about the Russian translation then my advice would be to give it a try.
There is an English chat channel, the people on it are helpful and friendly and will be happy to explain things to you.
Onto the game.
Well, in my opinion, this is the best fishing game on steam by a country mile.
It's based in a post apocalyptic world where you have to fish to survive.
The fish you catch can be sold or can be made into mince, which is then turned into biofuel and used in other recipes.
When you start your gear is very poor and you can have your rod break, line snap, hook break off, quite easily.
The starting gear is in one of the vending machines in "The Shelter", the area you start in.
All this beginner gear costs just 0.01 of a game coin, so my advice is to take a couple of rods, reels, line and hooks with you so you can swap your tackle out if it gets smashed!
You also get quests from the notice board, which fall into several categories.These give you cash, rep, xp etc and renew every forty minutes, except for the daily quest.
You are given a supply of radiation pills and first aid kits to start you off but it's doubtful you'll need em for the first few levels as you'll level up well before your stats get critical.
When you spawn into your chosen fishing area, it's well worth having a scout around cos you find things like mole hills that give you free bait.
The game includes an auction house, which is very good. You can buy or sell things, finances permitting.
You can also buy a second type of coin from the devs as a kind of dlc.
With these coins you can buy items to aid you and although you can't buy any of the in game cash you can use your purchased "Real" coins to buy items and then sell on the auction house to generate some much needed funds.
Buying single day "vip" passes is a good way of generating cash.
You can also purchase a "Starter Kit" dlc.
This gives you a pretty decent rod and line and a very decent reel, for $4.99 or about £3.50 in UK money.
This kit will give you a big boost so my advice would be to try the game and if you like it buy this kit, it's not much to pay for the benefit it gives you.
As you work your way up the levels you start collecting items from quests.
These items enable you to construct your own rods,reel and lines and are far more powerful than the low level items but if you do buy the starter dlc don't bother buying another reel, just make some better line and keep the reel from the pack.
I'm level 15 and I'm still using that reel on my spinning rod!
So my advice would be to download and try it, the graphics are nice and the sound is good, it's only about a 1gb download as well and it runs pretty stable!
I'm happy to recommend this game and give it 7.5/10.

Star Trek Online began as a subscription based MMO. When it experienced a lack of players, it trannsitioned to a f2p model. I have to say, out of all the f2p MMO's I've played, this one does it by far the best.
The story is well-written and does an excellent job at being both open and welcoming to newcomers, as well as including throwbacks, references, and tie-ins for those invested in Star Trek lore.
Combat is divided into 2 parts: Ground and Space.
The ground combat is what you might expect from away team missions from the show. Most of it consists of you beaming to an area along with 4 of your Bridge Officers. Both your officers' and your own character's equipment and skills can be customized at your leisure. You can micro-manage or automate as much as you want. You can play the ground segments like a Mass Effect game, a micro-rts of sorts with micromanagment of everyone, or a run-of-the-mill mmo... all are equally viable and fun.
The space combat is where the gameplay of STO really shines. It does an excellent of balancing things like energy-management, weapon-firing arcs, and ship movement with the more traditional skill bar that you've probably come to expect from an MMO. Different kinds of weapons have different firing arcs and cooldowns, and the differnet ship systems like shields, engines, and weaposn will require you to find a good power distribution for what you want to focus on when playing. For example, on my engineering character on a heavy, slow moving cruiser with lots of health, but a slow turn rate, I would put lots of weapons with a wide firing arc (like Beam Arrays) with maybe 1 or 2 aft torpedos. I'd also sink most of my energy into shields, as I'd be tanking damage most of the time. A tactical or science captain with a different or perhaps even the same ship might choose to take a different approach. A side-note: choosing your character's class does not in any way restrict the kinds of ships your character will have access to. Only your characters faction affects this in any way, shape, or form. For example, a character allied with the Klingon Defense Force would not be able to commandeer a Constitution class starship (like the Enterprise-A). Just as a Starfleet character would not be able to pilot a Klingon Bird-of-Prey.
All that being said, ship customization, that's right SHIP customization, is pretty damn amazing. You can mix and match several variations of your ships components (such as different saucer sections, nacelles, hull, etc.), apply patterns and decals, customize the windows on the exterior of your ship... all in all, each ship can feel as unique as you want it to.
Character customization is by far the best I've seen in an MMO. The only one that has a more sophisticated character creator and customizer would have to be Black Desert... seriously, if it's humanoid, you can most likely make it. There are a few minor character attributes that you need to pay money for, but the only real cosmetics that you might want to pay money for are the cosmetics in the cash-shop. Though, given the abundance of customization content available for free, I don't think you'd be likely to ever spend money on this.
Speaking of the cash-shop...
It's a good thing this game's primary focus is on PvE. The cash-shop offers a distinct power-advantage to those who wish to buy ships off of it, as certain powerful equipment (consoles) can only be gained by refitting it from a premium cash-shop ship to another one. Were this a PvP driven game I'd cry foul and declare this pay-to-win, but as it's a PvE game, no-one really cares. Yes, there's a PvP gamemode, but you'll quickly find that it's devoid of life.
And speaking of life...
If you're set on grinding out high-level gear to get crazy DPS... it will take a _lot_ of time and resources for you to get there. Seriously, I find the end-game to be among the weakest aspects of STO. It boils down to a sheer DPS fest, with no real need to pay any regard to team composition. The traditional mix of healer, tank, and dps does not matter. It is probably my largest complaint with the game by far, that the game designers seem to not understand how support role players think and (mistakenly) assume that if you aren't dealing damage, you must not be enjoying yourself. I can appreciate the versatility of playstyles that the story offers, but the endgame just makes certain builds completely unviable. Which really is a shame, as the base game itself already offers everything you'd need to encourage varied and mixed team composition. But, alas, the level and enemy design only needs high DPS.
Again, this only applies to end-game content. The base missions allow for each style to work just fine. I'm extremely frustrated as to why the designers chose to not keep this line of thinking for the end content...
All in all, I think I've done a good job at giving my opinion of the general game mechanics. If you have any questions, or wish for me to clarify something, feel free to ask.
As always, I hope you found this review to be helpful.

Now I know what your thinking. MX vs ATV? How can it be bad? Well it probably is...on a console. MX vs ATV Reflex is one sad excuse of a PC port. The game runs terribly. I can barely get 20 FPS even running on very low settings. Also the graphics aren't really that good. There kind of sloppy, and you can see where the developers added little pretties to hide the ugly monster within.
Another thing to mention is the cameras. This game holds the most dimwitted camera system there is. And adding the lagginess to the game makes the camera even worse. It nearly gives you motion sickness.
There is another thing that is bad to. The sounds. Oh my goodness the sounds! They go from making your ear drums bleed to quiet whispers with no transition. Also the developers have clearly never heard of the fact that trucks and most offroad vehicles have a thing called a transmission. The sound is just a loop. You never change up or down, so all you hear is a constant poorly recorded single engine note the entire time. It is just annoying. And as I said about the cameras, when you add the laginess it is much worse.
Now I try to find good in everything. And I am happy to say this game does have a few things going this way, such as the amazing terrain deformation and the somewhat cool tricks system.
But sadly those cool features are overtaken by the badness and the little silly things that are just annoying.
You saw the things above, but guess what? Theres more. The developers thought it was vital to our gameplay experience to add scadily dressed line girls and a narrarator that sounds like batman. There is also use of words such as "rad" and "knarly" which is ok, but a little overdone if you know what I mean.
Now ok, I understand the clients that they are trying to get to, such as real offroad enthusiasts like this kind of thing. But newsflash!  Real offroad enthusiasts have real offroad toys, so why would they play this silly game when they could go out (in real life) and thrash around on there motorcycle? See what I'm getting to? For us normal joes who just want to play a motorcycle game. We don't need line girls, or words of yobs. We just want to thrash around on a virtual motorcycle.
This fact and the horrid laginess gets this game what it deserves.
Rating 3.5/10

I love this game, probably too much.  It's hard, short, and occasionally unforgivingly buggy, but it's a complete game and almost elegant in it's minimalism.  For me it really scratches that retro, post-apocalyptic late 80's arcade itch.
The concept is super simple, you play a guy driving down a broken road in some post apocalypse wasteland heading for some unstated destination.  Along the way there are towns where you can pay for repairs and buy ammo, fuel, guns etc for you and your car.  In between the towns are bad guys you have to avoid or kill for loot.  Entering each town triggers a fight either with some waves of bad guys or one of 5 scripted bosses that you have to beat before you can do your shopping.  The difficulty is in preserving your armor, conserving your ammo and picking up enough cash along the way.  Oh and avoiding canyons.  Those things can be brutal.

The perfect sort of stupid fun. It makes no apologies for its ridiculousness and it doesn't need to. Fantastic at getting some actual adrenaline pumping and on the higher difficulties in the campaign it can provide an actual challenge. The races, which are the focus of the single player, are fun enough but are not the highlight of the game. The absolute highlight is the deathmatches, and capture the flag modes. Deathmatches make me amazingly nostalgic for my Twisted metal days and feel like the perfect blend of that old school gameplay with modern gaming tech. Capture the flag is a fun thing I haven't seen done in a car combat game before and actually works really well, the mad dash for the flag closest to you when the respawn is chaotic and the feeling of crashing into the opposing flag carrier, destroying them, and depositing your own flag is incredibly satisfying. A few shortcomings are the lack of clarity in how to advance in the campaign and the UI design could use some work, I found myself not being able to figure out what team I was on in a team game without bringing up the race stats on the overlay which I found a bit annoying. Additionally the Last Man Standing game mode, while very fun in multi, can be infuriating in single player considering when the difficulty advances enough the opposing AI develops the ability to know exactly where every repair powerup on the map is and as soon as you get them below half health in a fight they will turn and make a break for it. When there are multiple enemies remaining this isnt a problem as gun fire is coming from multiple directions and they usually cant make it however when it comes down to you and one CPU having to try and chase them down and finish them off before they can reach a repair powerup becomes nearly impossible and it can make the game drag on for an eternity. I had a few of them last for over 30 minutes before I decided to just give up on the mode in singleplayer entirely. Overall however this is the most surprisingly exciting I have ever found a game. I have put far more hours into it than I thought I would already and I'm just getting started.

is a little plateformer with combat element that I looked into almost randomly. It has a lot of good ideas but sometimes fails to executes them, making the game very frustrating sometimes.
: So. This game is a 2D plateformer where the protagonist have parkour and fighting skills. You basicaly have to go from point A to point B to point A again to point C and so on. Of course your errand won't be without obstacle. You will have to go through lasers, surveillance drones and many other traps that sometimes have no reasons to be here. The run is quite enjoyable, you first feel like you can try to rush all levels because of the character's parkour assets but you will soon realize that is not the case because of the controls. You will eventually get the hang of it but still. They sometimes feel really inaccurate and some level with precise jump can become really frustrating to play. Plus, the condition to trigger the wall run are too specific (the wall which you want to run on have to be close from where you start the jump, too close), making the game more realistic in terms of wall running but in a game where some ennemies can hadoken and others can do Demon fang it feels out of place. Ah, while we are getting on it, there is combat too. The problem is : why. There is absolutly no point to introduce combat mechanism in a game like that, when you enter in a room where you have to fight, you cannot just run past them you have to knock them  out and it breaks the rythme of the game, You have to stop and just spam the A button, because battle are very easy. The story for this one: you are 14, a famous artist, a prodigy martial artist, and you are high... seriously,  in this one, the main character just does the auteur artist "thing" and gives his own version of "by the power of grey skull" right before he runs off for an appointment or opts to take a side quest. he goes on like this for a while, sometimes going into a huge goth/ anime/ Shakespearean sonnet when he runs into new people. Hikikomori No Chuunibyou is a pseudo 8-bit platform-adventure game with beat-em-up, puzzle, and stealth elements. At its heart it is a classically inspired platform game with retro graphics and outstanding storytelling.
However, unlike classic platformers the unique selling point here is the utilization of parkour-style abilities and martial arts techniques.
Unfortunately, I have mixed feelings this time around. There’s something about the gameplay that isn’t as well executed or as fluid. I cannot quite put my finger on it. The parkour-style wall jumping and platforming don’t feel as engaging nor as pleasurable as the Ninjahtic games. In fact, they were often quite frustrating and rage inducing.
One of the problems was that there were rooms where I found myself stuck in for extended periods of time. This didn’t happen previously. I breezed through the tutorial and learned the commands required to play the game. However, when it came to the scenes following those early ones I struggled. This is unlike me. Others have reported having similar issues. Many who had successfully completed the Ninjahtic games.
I thoroughly enjoyed the presentation of the game. Blaze Epic have continuity in their games presentation and production value wise. For such an inexpensive game to achieve such a consistent level is pleasing.
What I have come to expect from their games is honesty. In many of the games that I play I feel that the screen shots are not representative of the game that you play at all. With Blaze Epic games I know that they are the genuine article. If you enjoy the artwork that is demonstrated in the screenshots then you’re going to enjoy the in game art. The same logic applies with the soundtrack. If the music used in the trailer appeals to you then you’ll find the same type of music utilized in the game.
Blaze Epic is a developer that understands the needs and wants of the Steam community. Therefore, the game does include trading cards and Steam achievements. The game comes with a set of six trading cards while for hunters there’s a total of 13 Steam achievements.
Obviously I have stated that I found the gameplay to be lacking the fluidity of the Ninjahtic games. However, despite this fact, it would be overly critical to not recommend the game. There are more highs than lows. Those who enjoy platforming games will find much to love here as well. The game scores highly on the value proposition. There’s more than enough content here to justify the inexpensive purchase price. I do recommend that beginners to Blaze Epic snap up The Ninjahtic Series as well.

When I first picked up this game, I was not sure what to expect. When all you know about a game is that it has to do with toilets and guns, there is much to be skeptical about. However, shortly after getting into the game I was pleasantly surprised by a simple, fun concept that provided what I would say was a good value, for a 99 cent game.
Soon after reaching the first checkpoint, I experienced my first death. Restarting was no big deal, since I had made progress and I was okay with having to go back a few steps once a lesson was learned. What I did not expect (or enjoy) was the many, many deaths it took me to reach the next few checkpoints. I rethought my strategy several times, buying many different upgrades and never forgetting to refill on health and supplies. But checkpoints were few and far between, and dying became tedious and very unpleasant.
Once, after barely cruising into a checkpoint, I dismounted my vehicle, weary and ready for another fight. However, instead of aiming for me, a resudial enemy from the road came in and destroyed my car, leaving me without a vehicle. Not built to handle this phenomenon, the game then had me walk for miles with no vehicle enemy spawns. Once I had reached the end of the road and arrived at the next town, I braced myself for the foot soldier attacks that would come before I could claim my checkpoint. However, they never did come. Since I had never dismounted my vehicle, the game had never been signaled to spawn the enemies for my battle!
Unable to save and stuck with no action, I left to the main menu to try Test Drive mode, which had worked bug-free for me prior to my little dilemma. Upon entering of the Test Drive section, the game promptly crashed (which I suspect had something to do with my previous bug).
That said, Kivi, Toilet and Shotgun is a great game for the price it's at. It's pretty fun, with a moderate replay value. However, the difficulty slant in this game along with the many bugs I have experienced make this review a downvote.

I wish I could give a "neutral" rating to this game, because I cannot in good conscience say "yes" or "no" without a lot of caveats.
First, I have played the game for abut 9 hours thus far. It's lovely, the gameplay is fairly smooth, and the ever-present battle against the air tank adds a little suspense, particularly before any upgrades are peformed.
However, the game plays like a beta - there is very little content or diversity. I love a good survival/hoarding game, and this should fit the bill perfectly; however, the extremely limited crafting and resources are disappointing.
When I purchased this, I thought it was a beta, and I continued to think that until I sat down to write this review and saw the others. It's very sad the devs are done with the game, as it could have a lot more added to it.
Things I like:
* Novel concept and storyline (thought it's far too short)
* Beautiful, rich, underwater environment
* Automated defenses, like drones and turrets
* Extra cargo space with drones
* Exploration which requires upgrades to complete (though it can all be seen and done within a couple of hours)
* Increased danger from predators at night
* Upgradable equipment
* Automated resource extraction
* Decent hunger/food system
* Blood mechanics (blood in the water from injuries or hunting attracts predators)
* Music and sound effects
* Decent world topographical map showing major points of interest/resources
* Decent agricultural system (but it would benefit from more options)
Things I dislike:
* Terrible gravity system - I understand we can't just have the ability to limitlessly ascend, but the current system is infuriatingly limited.
* Limited crafting - number of possible objects/upgrades is very small.
* Limited construction - More base options would be nice.
* Storage chests are far too small and non-stackable.
* No way to recover items after death - at least none I've found.
* No way to sleep through the night to fast-forward
* No way to split stacks in inventory at all - at least none I've found.
* Some items are ridiculously expensive to craft/consume for the reward.
* No ability to save the game without quitting.
What I would like to see:
* More diverse predators
* More storyline
* More biomes to explore
* More craftable items
* More and better base construction
* More discoverable points of interest - different wrecks, caves, et cetera
* More resource types
* Less expensive cooking - each item of cooked food takes 1 coal, which can be difficult to find
I got this on sale for less than $5, and it was definitely worth that amount. I might even say it's worth the $14.99 if you're the sort of person who doesn't want a seriously challenging game, and are more in the mood to mindlessly (in a pleasant way) gather resources and live out your life on the ocean floor.
Still, it could be so much more. I hope the devs might revisit it at some point; however, if they don't, they made a very nice (albeit short and very limited) and interesting distraction.

It's horrifying to think that although humans rule the earth, we are totally outclassed in the sea. This is the pivot that FarSky works on. You are a survivor of a submarine crash and need to survive long enough to retrieve the pieces of your craft and make it to safety.

Exploration is mandatory and soon enough you get into the gameplay loop of guessing when it's dawn, scooting out to find a little more resources, or travel a little further down. The world is procedurally generated, so that's both fun and frustrating in equal measures.
It's probably a nice game to play for a weekend. Music is nice and the graphics are at times stunning despite their simplicity. With a little more gameplay or variety, this could be quite a refreshing alternative to Minecraft, but lacks the complexity and creativity.

It may not look like much when you see it in videos/photos for the first time but let me tell you that Mount & Blade is a game like no other; Innovative in many aspects.
In short you start of as a lone commoner with whatever backstory you choose in a open medieval world. You are now free to do as you wish. Most likely you'll want to find some type of goal that reflects the backstory you chose in the character creation. And then you just work your way up in whatever way you want towards that goal. In most scenarios you'll want to recruit people for your cause.
Whether it is simply being a gladiator in tournaments; or leading a band of pirates and preying on farmers and pillaging villages, ships, etc; or if you want to serve under a king as a lord - commanding hundreds of soldiers on the battlefield as you take part in sieges or whatever political agendas are involved - M&B offers all of it. Or hell; even start your own kingdom where you command other lords. Gaining reputation and being persuasive and charismatic can be just as important, if not more so, as pure combat and strategic skills in this game, depending on what you want to do.
I think all the different skills highlights how fun and complex this seemingly simple game is. There are skills for how well you engineer stuff (for your own villages, castles, etc.). There are skills governing your leadership ability (how many troops you're able to command, their loyalty to you, how well your army or fleet navigates terrain and seas and tracks other armies, etc.). Morrowind Strength points :
1- Good quests that require thinking and the game tend to not babysit you like the later TES games.
2- Great selection of spells and the ability to make spells and enchanted items with spells is awesome.
3- The replay value is very high, as the other TES games too.
4- Great leveling system, much better than the system they implemented in Oblivion.
5- I like the Marksman in this game.
6- Enchanting is awesome and you have more freedom than either Oblivion or Skyrim.
7- Joining the factions have consequences on others.
8- there are more factions than either Oblivion or Skyrim.
Weakness points :-
1- Generic and forgittable NPCs. NPCs will give you some generic♥♥♥♥♥lines over and over again.
2- No voice acting
3- Melee combat is terrible
4- repetitative and boring music
5- boring and reptitative environment architectures (even with the overhaul), you will find every two or three cities share the same textures, and look the same and the interiors all look the same too.
6- For some quests sometimes the NPCs give you terrible or erratic directions...
7- Cliff Racers are very annoying. Every few steps you will encounter at least 2 or 3 in the wilderness, they just won't let you explore in peace and fighting them is distracting and time consuming.
8- you are the only targeted character by the aggressive NPCs. The whole world is against you in this game, and everybody is a**hole.
9- The AI is not advanced enough to accept your yields and NPCs with high disposition or followers will be aggressive on you if you hit them by accident, this can be annoying as sometimes they have the tendency to block your way.
10- NPCs in interiors can block your way, and you cannot push them like Oblivion which is very stupid.
11- Easy to get stuck between objects
12- Morrowind is a very sad, empty and dead world and you are the only moving character in the game. Everybody stands still in their place like a statue.
I give this game 7/10 despite the bad things about it, it is a good game regardless. I also understand the nostalgia for some people who played the game when they were kids, but this game is very overrated, it is not the perfect or the best RPG ever made, it has a lot of weaknesses and is undeserving of those titles.

Based on the trailer, I thought I would end up enjoying this game quite a bit. I love retro-styled platformers, and the idea of one that incorporated a free-running movements system into a 2D platformer seemed intriguing. Unfortunately, the parkour system is a huge frustration, as it doesn't seem as if the wall running triggers reliably when it should. Pair this with the unnecessary repetition of screens by having to play every one at least twice on each level, and things get annoying quickly. There are also some issues with being able to tell when the character will grab onto a ledge or hang from a bar, which can lead to seemingly random deaths.
The game also seems to have an identity problem, as the parkour movement encourages speed and free-flowing platforming (when it works), but then there will be things inserted into the levels that you have to stop and wait for, such as drones to hide from or precise jumps to time between laser beams. Similarly, the combat sections seem to want to replicate a martial arts fight, and while you have various types of attacks, you can simply mash your basic attacks and get through pretty much any fight.
The story also makes no sense. I assume that the concept of "chuunibyou" is something that Japanese people or fans of anime and manga would understand, but I had to look it up. Once I did, though, it seemed like a simple enough idea. In the game, though, it seems less clear what is real and what is in the character's delusion. There are also times where there are sentences that just don't make any sense, and the dialogue is often awkward and unnatural (such as the time the characters are discussing the virtues of manga artists and how they should be viewed, which feels very preachy directly toward the player). It was all very bizarre.
It's really a shame, too, as it has a lot of potential, and when things work like they're supposed to, it can be really fun. I try to keep in mind that the game was only $2, so I wasn't expecting something as polished as a Shovel Knight or Freedom Planet, but the four hours I spent with the game were four of the most frustrating hours I've spent with a game in recent memory.
From the 2 hours I've played, I've got to say this is a pretty good game especially for being only 2 dollars. It is easily one of the better 2D platformers I've played.

Kivi, Toilet and shotgun is a classical top-down shooter with 16-bit graphics, in which the goal is simply for the main character Kivi to arrive at the end of the road while defeating enemies and and stopping by villages from time to time in order restock on supplies.
The game basically features two playstyles, shooting on foot and shooting while driving. The player constantly changes between both of them while traversing the wasteland. On foot Kivi can use multiple weapons in order to defeat foes and visit shops. Upon entering a car the player can also use nitro and run enemies over in addition to shooting at them.
The game is essentially split up into driving and on foot levels which freely flow into each other and in which all past upgrades are carried over.
As the game is split between driving and walking, the enemies are also divided along these lines. There are driving enemies and walking enemies which not only have different attack patterns but also different loot, since supplies are only dropped by vehicles.
Otherwise supplies can only be purchased in one of three shops which are present in every village. This is a very crucial step as a lack of acquiring fuel ends the game prematurely and a lack of ammunition leaves no way of defending against armoured vehicles.
The other two shops provide upgrades to either Kivi or his car. The selection of upgrades is pretty sizeable, but nothing out of the ordinary with additional weapons and upgrades to all other parameters, like fuel or armour.
In addition to the story mode there is also a Drive Test. This game mode allows the player to choose any of the existing car models in game and upgrading them from the start. By defeating bosses or getting other in-game achievements you can unlock more starting money for this game mode. While it does not offer much it it atleast some additional content, supplementing the base game. It can also crash your game upon access, as this happened to me personally every time I tried to access this mode after playing the main story.
The visuals are pretty bland with mostly orange, brown and grey hues dominating the wasteland. While this is fitting for the setting, which is very reminiscent of the 80’s classic Mad Max, the transitions between night and day augment this problem. By nighttime most of the screen is barely visible with only a small portion of the screen illuminated by the players flashlight or by the car's headlights. While there is a way to upgrade the nightly visibility on foot, this problem hinders gameplay while driving significantly, since the cones of the car’s headlights are pretty small and there is no way to improve upon them, which results in either deliberately sluggish driving at night or collisions with objects or enemies.
The music is pretty repetitive with only one track playing throughout the whole game. While it is not bad per se it can get annoying on longer play sessions. There is also an issue with the volume. If it is not set to the maximum setting the game will automatically play the music at that volume after it loops once, which is unfortunate since there is no way to access the option menu without exiting the game and losing some progress.

+Challenging gameplay
+Competent shooting mechanics
+Variety in boss design

-Repetitive music
-Can be buggy sometimes
-Bland visuals
While the game has it’s shortcomings it still delivers a challenging gameplay which requires a little bit of strategy and planning to master it. With the low asking price in mind the game can be recommended to play in short sittings.
6,2/10

This game feels like a Top-Down Mad Max experience with a low budget and quite a lot of troubles with this game. The first time you pay this game you
fail, it'll be a learning experience. However, for a £0.79 game what else can you expect? And since it's such a cheap game I am going to recommend this game. It has a nice concept to it with some nice graphics and other things that kinda bring this game up. I feel like it still needs a lot of work on it even though it's a full game.
This game has a few issues with the controls and the way what they tell you the controls. First off the controls that they tell you are WSAD to move your character/car, Q to enter the car and E to use your nitrous when your in your car. You can also shoot while pressing U. Excuse me? So I have to move with WSAD, press U to shoot and move the mouse to aim? Why didn't you just say that the left mouse button is to shoot as well... It kinda fails to tell you the basic controls. That and to enter shops and stuff you have to press Q, which you aren't told. There are then also no way to change the controls which would've been helpful. Sometimes the game can be a little bit too difficult, with the limited life you have with your car and yourself as your character can sometimes feel like there isn't really much balance in the game. Say that you where playing the game for the first time and you drove past the town after defeating all the enemies there and then you just realised that you had money to spend. So possibly you can go back to the town and buy some things? No you can't, the game forces you to keep on driving forward, this shouldn't be. You must be able to go back to where you just came from to buy some stuff. Despite all the bad things I have just said there are a few things that make this game great. There is a nice variety of gadget upgrades for your car, these can help you get better weapons for your car so that you can dispose of the enemies cars more quickly and efficiently. This provides to be very useful as the enemies can kind of gang up on you and destroy your car pretty quickly, this then results in a instant game over. It's a nice game if you're playing it in short sessions and want to kill some time. I felt playing it in long sessions made the game just seem boring and repetitive. So to eliminate this play it in shorter sessions to increase the amount of fun you can get out of this game. There is a real nice way of how this game makes you think about how to spend your money. You could, if you wanted, spend it all on your characters weapons. But then you run out of fuel and then it's a instant game over again. It really makes you think and plan your journey ahead on what you need to prioritise about your car or character, otherwise you won't get very far.
So to start of, your game loads up in windowed mode which isn't much of a problem as you can change it to full screen in the options menu but would've been nice if you could've started the game in full screen. You also can't change the music setting while in game, I am unsure why they would do this but they did. Make sure that you change the music and sounds volume to your desired volume before playing the game. As for the graphics of this game, I really like the retro kind of feel you get from the game. There isn't much variation when it comes to the colours of the game, and that it's just a constant road the goes forward. A nice little feature about this game is the lighting when it turns to night or day. I really like that transaction between the night and day cycle.
As for the music and sound there isn't really that much to talk about. The music that plays in the background just constantly goes on, even when you die and go onto the main menu it's just constantly on. Would've liked some more variation when it comes to the Music. The sounds are pretty basic and generic, but they really missed out on some of the basic sounds such as the car driving, there's no sound of that at all.
So, taking into consideration that this game only costs £0.79, I do still recommend this game to people who like a retro, difficult kind of game. Just don't expect a lot of variety when it comes to music and the sound. Play it shorter sessions to get the most enjoyment out of this game, as this game is really just a time killer.

To clarify, I am basing the following opinions around the fact that the full game, which I am reviewing, is only $1, which is a very appropriate price for a game of this length. Most of the work put into this game shows in the art style and 'inside-esc' right leaning humor, which means you probably won't enjoy this game that much if you're a cuck. I beat it quickly, but decided to stay around a bit longer to find a few 'hidden-ish' secrets and to stare at the milo picture hanging in the oval office, which by itself would make the game worth buying. There are few specific areas I'd like to criticize the game on however.
Technical:
As someone with about two years experience casually developing mini projects (for school) with Unity, I have a pretty good idea how most of the game has been put together. It seems odd that there is no option for higher resolutions or a widescreen aspect ratio. I understand that the game's art and gameplay was most likely made with a 4:3 aspect ratio in mind, but unless there was something strange I'm not thinking of, you should be able to offer higher resolutions and different aspect ratios but include black bars on the edges that hide any off-screen assets you don't want to been seen. This would make it so the game could be played at my monitor's native 1080p resolution without having to upscale up from 960p, the highest offered resolution.
Gameplay:
Gameplay is kinda slow. I've never been a huge fan of turn based games, so take this as a general complaint about the genre. The attacks were creative, but I felt as if the heath items (food) was generic and didn't pack as much of a joke as it cold have (tell me if I'm missing some amazing inside joke though). This is random, but what if instead of eating chicken, Trump gained health by feeding on the hopes and dreams of the poor mexican immigrant farm child who just wanted a better life for him and his eight family members that got in through chain migration- yeah that wouldn't fit in the box.
To conclude, this was a fun little game. While it is true that I'm writing this review on the same evening I got the game, I don't regret buying it and wouldn't get a refund even if it let me. If the developer plans to add more "Episodes", I'd suggest trying to emulate another type of game with a different gameplay style, maybe a traditional platformer.

Gas Guzzlers Extreme; an excellent combat racing game published by Iceberg Interactive. Now with free demo.

"Very nische racing type of game, yet entartaining as nothing else."
There has been not many games that actually have cars and weapons mixed together. This type of racing game is pretty "nische" and there were games in the past (Road Wars for example) that did it nicely. This one is new, fresh, and does it stand up to the great game name?
That question is pretty tough, but in my honest opinion - yes it does. Previous Gas Guzzlers was plagued by loads of problems: from barely working controls, via terrible physics, to horrible optimisation. This one as sequel on the other hand, does everything better, as expected.
Game starts you with sponsored car. You get the money by winning races. The more races you win, the more money you get. Also winning unlocks cars, upgrades, rims, stickers and weapons, but this happens every 3-4 races. There is a lot to do in single player, however, the beginning of the campaign is pretty slow, and boring, but it does get better as you progress more. In the race you have various objectives that can give you more money, like "destroy x amount of cars in 1 lap". This adds variety to the gameplay and does add the replay value to the game.
Graphics are much better. They are shiny (but it's not overdone) colourful, with nice shadows and particle effects. Models look nice, and most of cars are based on their real counterparts which is good, but they have really cheesy names. Overall game has really cheesy humour, which could be considered childish, but for me, it doesn't matter, but let's get back to technical stuff. Damage done to cars is somewhat 'meh' but it does job well on harder difficulties. Ai does it's job too. They're challenging, they are intelligent and they use their weapons with caution and can be deadly sometimes. Optimisation here is also better than previous one. I have mid-range PC and 60FPS all the time on ultra settings, which is amazing. There are many options to customise so you won't be dissapointed. Sound departament delivers funny yet very high quality sounds, for example there are voice-overs from Duke Nukem (!) which is a nice touch (they sound exactly like duke!), engines have that "punch" and differ from car to car... Just awesome. Music is outstanding, some heavy metal tunes over there, but opinions may vary here.
Controls are improved, as it should be done in sequel. Car instantly responds to your commands, they have feel of weight, but at the same time they handle well. I had no problems handling the cars. Keep in mind that every car handles differently, and there are noticable differencies between all of them. Same goes to weapons. Some can shoot even backwards, which is awesome. There are some powerups on map such as repair, oil that you can spill on the track, mines etc. It all works together very well.
Multiplayer is a typical madness. Capture the Flag, Deathmatch, Last Man Standing. Just Awesome. Too bad that nobody plays this game on MP which is shame because it's so much fun even with bots. Runs fluid smooth, has no lag issues, so what's the matter?
There are some flaws. Sometimes Ai runs in circles when FPS goes down on older PC's. There were some problems for me with my steering wheel, but I got them resolved, and mentioned above slow single player campaign start which is annoying and can make you bored of game quickly if you won't get new car soon. I also wish for more cars, and weapons. There were some problems with achievements, but other than that, I had no glitches.
Game is good for what it is. It does entertain you, and it does it pretty well. Question is, is it worth 22,99? For me, yes, for others looking for a realistic racing game - not really. Buckle up, this is going to be hell of a ride!
8/10

How about your fast travel? Gone.
Oh, don't you LOVE your dual-wielding, shouts, infinite mana with the right gear, vampires that don't catch on fire on contact with the sun, followers, and anything else that is softcore? GONE.

Overall, I would say this is a must-buy for any challenge-seeker, fan of classic games, elder scrolls fan, or those looking for a great RPG. This game is NOT for everyone, and I can understand that. This game is very memorable, though, and I would recommend for sure.

Summary: Imagine a game where your actions can help turn the tide of a persistent online war being fought by thousands of other real players, either in the role of a hardened soldier engaged in blistering first-person shooter combat, or as a strategic officer managing the grand scheme of the campaign on a tactical war map. Heroes & Generals will deliver this combined one-two punch in a thrilling multiplayer online battle across authentic WW II settings.
My review: This is an amazing game, it's an FTP first-person shooter that's set in the European Theater of WWII. You start as a standard infantryman, but as you increase in rank you can unlock new classes (like tank crewman, fighter pilot, recon, and paratrooper). The game also allows you to unlock new weapons and vehicles through both rank and by earning combat ribbons (basically an achievement system). There is also a place to get together with friends of the same class and form a squad so you can all play together (number of friends in you squad is dependent on your class, i.e. infantry can have six, while tanks can have three). You can also have multiple soldiers, so you can have a variety of classes to play with (I have an infantryman, a tank crewman and a fighter pilot).
There is also a place where you can pay to unlock vehicles and weapons early (although for tank crewman, if you buy a heavy armor off the bat you will not be able to use it very often until you get to a rank where there are heavy armor squads).
Another neat feature is you can unlock upgrades for your weapons, like a hair trigger for your guns that will increase ROF but decrease stability. Or for tanks and jeeps you can get infantry support crates (ammo and health, or anti-tank weapons).
All in all, this is a great game and it's only in beta form. It has a great diversity of classes, weapons, and vehicles. If first-person shooters are your thing, then you should definitely try this game, and since it's free, it can't hurt to try it.
Overall rating: A perfect 5/7

All political opinions aside, Super POTUS Trump is a game where you need a good understanding/appreciation of what happened in the 2016 Presidential election to understand and potentially enjoy this game. If you do not care about United States politics, you will not enjoy this game.
Obviously, this game takes a lot of inspiration from Paper Mario, where it dedicates all of its gameplay to RPG-esque boss battles based on opponents towards Trump during the 2016 election. There are two different difficulties; an easy mode (that disables achievements/coins), and a hard mode.
, but the scary guise of hard mode will only dissappear after you understand the basics of the game. Most of the struggle in the game comes from the reflex-based attacks you do, while being easy to accomplish. Throughout the game, you get more attacks/heals to use against bosses, and that's pretty much it for gameplay. Appeal-wise, the game tries reference-based humor with mentions to specific events in the 2016 election related to Trump. It also tries for nostalgia, with the Paper Mario based art style.
I personally think that (1hour>) of limited gameplay isn't worth the 2 dollars, and the reference-based humor also doesn't cover it unless you need a re-cap of what happened during the 2016 election. Flash games on other websites can do what this game did, but for no charge.

Ever play a game in the "Thief" series? This is what you get when someone decides to make a Thief game with RPG Maker and it's a fun experience.
No combat, just sneaking through shadows, crouching behind counters and fences, hiding in crates and closets while observing the guards patrol patterns and waiting for the right opening to make your move. Get spotted even once and you have to restart from the last checkpoint but since every room you enter is a checkpoint this is not an issue and the game maintains a quick pace.
Graphically, other than the main character's sprite, the game seems to use default RPG maker assets. If you ever played an RPG Maker game you know how this looks and controls.  Nonetheless visual design is clean. Everything is laid out well, for the most part it's clear where you can hide and important details like treasures to pick up or entrances to secret passages are clearly visible. There is also a minimal but decent story about the character trying to sabotage war preparations, it does the job providing some context on the missions and the character's motivations.
On the negative side there are odd spelling errors here and there. Controls are solid but they have some quirks that could have been ironed out (my main gripe is how you have to be completely still to crouch or get up from the crouching position) and early on it requires some trial and error to figure out how the enemies field of vision works. Also keep in mind the game is extremely linear, each room/screen has one solution/route you have to figure out so it's best to get into it knowing each mission is a series of connected stealth/timing puzzles rather than expecting an "open" stealth game.
In conclusion this is a neat little indie title well worht it's full (low) prize. If you're a fan of stealth games and don't specifically dislike RPG Maker games this should earn a cozy spot in your wishlist and hopefully your library. Heartily recommended.

Yes another RPG Maker game...
Here is my quick look video:
But this one is pretty well done and has the unique aspect of trying to use stealth and shadows to sneak through halls and rooms unseen.  It's actually quite fun and makes it feel and play a little different then all of the other RPG Maker games I've played.

My biggest gripe in the time I've played the game so far is that the escape key doesn't work at all, and I was forced to CTRL-ALT-DEL to manually abort the game.  The game saves automatically, but still the ESC key should work as a method of escaping the game.
These are pretty minor gripes, and I think people who enjoy these classic RPG style games will be very happy with this entry on Steam, especially at it's low price point of $3.99 USD.  Catch this game on sale, and it's even a better value.
If you are the type that doesn't usually enjoy these kind of RPG Maker games, then the unique steath aspect of the game will not likely make it fun for you, so I'd caution against buying it just for that aspect alone.
Grading this game on what I've played of the game.. I'd give it a 7 out of a possible 10.  Recommended for people who enjoy these classic RPG sort of games, and not recommended for people who enjoy fancier/pretty RPGs or more action oriented games.

Car combat has been the red headed stepchild of video game genres almost since its inception. The rash of Twisted Metal clones that came in the early days soured many, and even Sweet Tooth and the gang haven’t had the best track record as of late. Last generation, Burnout took up the car chaos crown, with its traffic checking and Crash Mode, but the developers got lost in Paradise City and are now toiling away at the endless barrage of samey Need For Speed titles. Gas Guzzlers Extreme, a new entry in the genre by Gamepires, isn’t going to set the world on fire, mostly due to its lack of flamethrowers. However, the game does strike a nice balance between the crash heavy races of Burnout and the heat seeking missiles of Twisted Metal that any fan of the genre should take notice of.

I love me some arcade racing. Gas Guzzlers delivers.
Fans of cars and explosions will have a blast zooming around the game's large selection of tracks across a variety of environments, including deserts, snowy mountaintops, tarmac tracks, and backwoods trails.
There's a good selection of cars and even more weapons to equip them with, as well lots of other unlockable goodies to upgrade and decorate your cars. The solo campaign is great, but beginner racers might find it slightly difficult. The AI racers also all have really stupid (and frankly immature) names too, but that's not really a huge deal I guess.
Controls are responsive, and gameplay is tight and rewarding; there's something satisfying about blasting away your fellow racers, or forcing them to crash into things. You may also find it's reminiscent of kart racers like Mario Kart and Diddy Kong racing as you dash around collecting powerups, repairs, and cash bonuses.
There's also a wealth of multiplayer modes, so you can choose your flavour and start blowing up your friends however you like.
I highly recommend this one, can't get enough of it.

I was browsing the most absolutely cheapest things on sale on the Lunar New Year Sale and I stumble upon this little thing. I mostly got it because I felt confident about spending for nearly anything after replenishing my steam wallet and that I really dig this kind of deserty wasteland theme.
It was alright enough. I haven't played for that long or gotten too far but, from what I've played so far, I'm pretty sure it's good enough for a 99₵ pricetag. It does what it's suppose to do thoroughly and it doesn't hold your hand. You have to really think and be cautious when progressing and to also be aware about all the variables that you have to take care of. I've noticed that most of these other reviewers are saying that they can't get to the 2nd town because "the game's unfair" when they probably didn't upgrade their vehicle (repair vehicle if below 60, fuel up, attach 2nd AK turret, and maybe buy some off-road tires) and keep their distance from enemy cars.
This game is more complicated than I anticipated and you need to plan out your journey so that you won't be relying only on the RNG. It does not have everything that it should. It should give you the ability to rebind some controls (the controls could take some getting used to), it's sort of luck based, the combat could be better and more built upon, and there's a major lack of toilets here.
It's alright, especially for it price, it's not garbage, it is challenging (like how old NES games were challenging), and it may be a good distraction in between of doing things or waiting for a bigger game of yours to get patched.
I may have only played around a halfhour but I don't regret this small purchase. Heck, you could probably just get a refund if you don't like it after a few sessions or go for the trading cards and make a profit of the marketplace. I know that I'm gonna keep this one around.

It starts good with an instruction of the few basic elements it has, but later on it completly destroys itself with really bad balancing. (You will barely take a scratch from the first boss, but regular enemies can drain your hp within seconds.) There is a lot of wasted potential and it feels like the devs abandoned it when they were halfway through.
The items drop randomly, so if you are not really carefully how and when you speed up while driving and keep your distance to enemies, you will have a hard time to survive, because HP-Packs won't drop at all sometimes. Some of the items are not explained, so you have to figure it out on your own, what exactly they do.
There are a few upgrades that doesn't make sense, since it would make the game harder. Why should i buy a pistol for my car, when it has an automatic rifle by default? You can beat the entire game with the automatic rifles (for the Car and Char). You won't need anything else.
The balancing for the boss battles would really need some improvements and changes. The second boss is probably the hardest, while every other boss is rather too easy. You can even hit them, when they can't hit you and some of them are stationary.
Graphics are okay for such a simple game and have some fine details.
It could have a few more sounds. You don't even hear your car while driving.
But beside all of that you can get fun out of it, when you like games of this kind and if you want a challenge that can be frustrating from time to time. The concept is good, but it has much wasted potential. It's hard to give a yes or no, since you can see some effort the devs put into that game, but it feels in many situations like they haven't finished their job.

ZRoller (or "LandscapeMountains" as the game window is titled!) is about moving around as a heavy, unruly ball. The goal is to collect 51 fiery runes (called totems) in every level, however the counter in the game only goes up to 50.
There are 6 levels total, but each of them are just the same 1st level with various filters and lighting adjustments. The "3rd level" places a blur effect that is so badly implemented that the game lags on a really good PC.
The achievements are bugged. After completing the entire game and collecting every "totem", my achievements are still only at 84% because some of them never registered upon completion.
The design of the one level is of a small, enclosed space with some invisible walls and floating platforms that you need to magically hop around on. You can't move the camera to see what's around you so you can't plan very far ahead. It's super easy to fall, and to add to the difficulty, you don't know for certain what will happen to you due to the inconsistent barriers and the ball's fake shadow. You know how when you're trying to land on something in a game and you look to see where the shadow is down below in order to gauge where you're headed? That's not possible in this game. The ball does have a shadow but it's like it's 2-dimensional in a 3D world.
At first glance the game looks pretty but the assets the game uses were pre-bought or free and they are so poorly placed; there are floating patches of grass, grass stuck in walls, trees with no collision, trees WITH collision, and for some reason the upper part of the area is a fire asset that has (yet again) been poorly added. The music itself I kind of like but it loops endlessly with no variation.
Lastly, another example of the lack of effort put into this game is that even the cards are lame, named after the assets ... some of the greats being "Tree" and "Water Plants".
I do not recommend buying this game even if it's on sale, as it will give money to someone who wants cash for no effort. Achievement hunters, stay away. If Finnish Roller had a successor, then it would be this game.
As a spherical object, you will face the struggles of having to take the extra cautions on slowing down, stopping or avoiding obstacles in this platformer game. I had a rough with gliding to the objectives, and having missed touching the totems in millimeters when playing. The only controls you have for your sphere is the AWSD keys and the Space key to jump. I was surprised to find that the balls movement was more fluid and stable, compared to other roller games. I could even do little wall jumps when headed into one, rather than falling automatically, which made movements much easier during the gameplay.
The graphics are fairly bland, and minimalistic in textures. Its levels features mainly gravel, brick walls that surround the map, along with wooden platforms that you must jump onto. A little bit of plant life is added here and there, but that’s it. Some more detail and refining could have been added here: the grasses and flowers getting pushed or squashed whenever we roll over them, or some dust effects when we land from a certain height onto the ground below. Even the ball’s design could have a new outlook on each level too. I’ll also give a compliment to the design of the totems, as they were more than mere cylinders planted on the ground. You’ll easily recognize them, and they give a magical effect whenever one is collected too!
The music used was very calming and serene, although there didn’t seem to be any audio present at all in the game. We don’t hear any noises when we jump, roll over specific platforms or bump into the walls. Another thing considered for the developer when/if they decide to update the game.
Overall, I’d say ZRoll was all right for a game, albeit not the best. It’s definitely better than Finnish Roller at least, and that’s enough for me to say yes to this game.

Dual stick shooters don't often cross over into the rogue like game genre making 'Gemstone Keeper' a bit of an rarity.  The controls are responsive during play, but a bit wonky while in the menus.  The ASCII art and faux CRT beveling lends a strong visual aesthetic but it tends to always be a bit out of focus and hard on the eyes.

EDIT: Since my review, the dev has updated the game, and believes they have fixed a number of issues. I have not confirmed this, but feel it's worth noting.
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Gemstone Keeper is a solid foundation in an unfinished game.
The shooting mechanics, enemy behaviours, weapon combinations and art are well done and feel good, but between bugs, design failures, boring procedural generation, and just a lack of content overall, I don't think this game is ready for general consumption.
Issues I had include:
Only being able to see keybinds when you start a new game.
Randomly not being able to start from the depth I got to on the last run.
Not knowing what stats do.
There are 5 bosses, and by the time you've reached the second, you've probably bought all the weapons and seen everything the procedural generation can throw at you, then it's just grinding through a lot of samey levels until you reach the end.
The last boss relies on shields to stop you shooting it until you can break through for a hit, except one of the weapons is piercing, so it just ignores the shields and kills the boss in seconds.
After a while, you can afford to buy a hundred medkits, buff your health, and then just tank from one end of the game to the other.
If you're curious about other issues, I posted even more on the forums a few weeks ago. Unfortunately, the dev doesn't seem to be interested in responding. Which, considering the game has only been out a couple of months, is a bit disappointing.
So yeah, I do not recommend spending money on this game unless the devs make some serious improvements. Not likely, but if it happened, this could be a fun game.
EDIT: Dev has noticed my feedback and says they're going to work on some of the issues I've raised, so that's something.

First of all, I really loved how this game pretty much only uses ASCII symbols for its graphical design. Very retro-y, while still visually pleasing for a modern game. It was nice seeing variety in level designs and mechanics, and I think the enemy mobs are cute.

What I personally hope to see in this game in the future is difficulty settings. I felt it got really easy at some point, and I got through the game (minus collecting all the gems) in less than an hour. It didn't take away much of the fun, but still, it would be nice to test our skills on a higher difficulty. While I've only got a couple hours on the clock with Gemstone Keeper, first impressions are really quite good. The game plays precisely as sold, there's an interesting variety of enemy types, the moving & shooting is super smooth, the weapon combinations make for a fun arsenal, the gem collecting aspect is rewarding enough and the overall look & feel of the game, to me, has huge appeal.
The somber, suped-up ASCII art style is awesome and shows from the dev a particular reverence for the roguelikes that started it all. Enemies are all easily distinguished and the shifting environment palettes from floor to floor help change things up during a run, although the everpresent hashtag walls are an inescapable visual sameness. There's a variety of trippy screen effects (identified in-game as "mists") that distort & obfuscate the play area, from watery ripples to a rapidly pulsing screen blur to just straight up fog-of-war-ing the edges of the viewport. These add flavour and interest to the floors where they occur but I must admit the pulsing effect makes me a little queasy; I understand their gameplay-altering intent but some control over the intensity of these effects would be most welcome for sensitive players.
Sound design is excellent - atmospheric and polished with cold, ambient electronic music, glassy shatters, satisfying crumbles and squeaking monsters comprising the majority of the soundscape. I'd dig some additional audio feedback sprinkled throughout, such as when bullets impact, but everything that's here sounds lovely. The soundtrack sets the perfect mood and I'd totally listen to the main dungeon theme outside the game. One special detail worth noting is the tempo of the music shifts in response to a floor's current mist, turning slow and heavy when submerged or going double time when meth'd (for lack of a better term).
On the configuration side, I very much appreciate the flexible graphics settings offered as the ability to disable filters & bloom gets on my laptop's good side. It's worth noting that graphic / audio options are only accessible from the escape menu, never from the main menu. Windowed resolution presets to switch between would be welcome, as opposed to the free resizing the game exclusively offers now, but there's an adequate level of configurability here, and while controls don't appear to be rebindable, the default is perfectly sensible for QWERTY users (WASD + mouse). The game detected (and plays quite nicely with) an Xbox 360 gamepad, but it would seem controller support is limited to xinput devices as a Logitech Dual Action wasn't seen at all. Tiny side note, the boot-up sequence is supremely charming and an early sign of the attention to detail & quirky personality present throughout Gemstone Keeper.
I've run into some bugs during my relatively brief time with the game which have required the session be killed, such as getting stuck on a purely white or glitched-out screen. Here's a link to a thread on the community forums with more detail on the technical issues encountered:
All in all, recommended based on my experience thus far. Gemstone Keeper is just begging to be played by more people, fingers crossed it finds an appreciable audience here on Steam :)

I have played this game so many times over and each time I find something new to be intrigued by!
Morrowind, while pretty old, is incredibly detailed and can be a challenging game. I've played oblivion, skyrim, and online too, and I still always come back to play Morrowind.
To get a good idea of the level of detail and vastness of the game, have a look at the Morrowind UESP Wiki. I loved browsing all the stuff I didn't yet know about on that wiki.
I'll put the game in perspective though... It's old, looks old, feels old. It can be boring and slow at times, and very hard. You may die a lot at first as your levels are crap, you may keep inflicting no damage hit after hit in combat untill you get your levels up. Walking will take ages and you will probably get lost and not be able to find your destination. BUT if you can push your way through the hardships at first and get use to the game and the world of Morrowind, then you will find some very challenging and enjoyable rpg game play! As you get the hang of the game, you will also love that the learning and discovering does not stop there! You will keep finding new and awesome things!!! Have a look at my positives list for why I loved the game and what it's main attraction points are.
Anyway, positives and negatives!!!
Positives:
-Extremely rich detail in all key game areas! Loads of different armour types(and I recon the old quality graphics makes everything look really detailed and realistic due to a more rough/worn look). Loads of different weapon types, there are spears, staffs, throwing knives, even ninja stars!!! Loads of unique items. A lot more guilds/factions than the other TES games, there is fighters, mages, thieves, imperial legion, imperial cult, east empire trading company, morag tong, tribunal temple, aundae/berne/quarra clan, ashlander tribes, and all the Great Houses of Morrowind(Hlaalu, Redoran, and Telvanni).
-Great sound track! Classic Elder Scrolls amazing music.
-Good voice actors(lol oblivion), the unique and outlandish voices for some of the cool characters/races really serve to immerse you in the game. If it bothers you though, there is a narrow range of different voices...
-Awesome spells!!! There are levitation spells for goodness sake!!
-Ban Hammer item :D
-Detailed quests/game information/history.
-Good books, (The Lusty Argonian Maid).    ;)
-Dungeons and ruins and tombs and ship wrecks and dwemmer ruins and forts and caves and bandit camps and bandit hideouts and tons of cool locations EVERYWHERE! You will never run out of places to explore!
-Some very uniqe scenery/settings in Morrowind. The tree/plant/mushroom buildings of the Telvanni people are awesome!
-Great loot everywhere, hidden.
-Also, just the level of detail put into the game by the developers is great. Rarely will you have a 'boring' quest or dungeon, there is often cool little features put in, or cool background stories that serve no purpose but to intrigue! I can remember many occasions where I have gone into a cave or such and been really challenged with actually navigating it, the path to the objective/destination can be hidden really well.
-I have to emphasise the point of amazing in game detail! xD I just loved how there was so much to do and all of it felt unique and challenging. I loved moments like breaking into vaults filled with treasures in Vivec. Or finding amazing loot just placed in hiding spots for you to find, that could really help you in game, I recall the 'Sword of White Woe' being hidden in a guard tower ontop of a tall wardrobe. I could either use my stealth to get it, lure the guard, or assassinate the guard... I assassinated. :D
-Differnet quality lockpicks, and probes(probes are used to disarm traps on doors/chests). Also different quality alchemy tools, and not  just a mortar and pestle, but also alembic, retort, and callcinator! I really felt like an alchemist with all those tools in Master Quality.
-The enchantments on enchanted items can be cast as normal spells! A ring can have healing on it and may have 5 uses an ingame day, so you can keep that ring handy to heal you through out your exploring! (Fargoth heuheu)
-Your player gold as an actual item!!! So you can store it! I really liked that. :)
-Jiub.
Negatives:
-Walking is really slow... So when you have to make that inevitable long trip where there are no transportation or teleportation methods, it will take ages.
-Cliff Racers.
-Some people may hate the lack of guidance in the game; I loved the extra challenge though and I found it forced me to get fully immersed in the game. I really had to listen to/read and remember what people said.
-It's hard to sell your really expensive items as there are not many vendors with large sums of gold...

Out of all the elder scrolls games I've played Morrowwind is still my favorite.
Yes it needs a fast travel like skyrim, or at least faster running without spending forever leveling athletics, but there's just something about Morrowwind that I love. I think it's the overall plot of the game, there's no sense of immediacy to follow the main story like I felt in skyrim. I joined up with the various guilds and spent most of my first play through ignoring the main quest completely in favor of becoming the boss of the Warriors, Mages and Thieves guilds.
Because "why not?"
I wandered around hunting for daedric artifacts and gear, pretending I knew anything about training certain skills, and just exploring. The world wasn't and isn't very pretty. It's blocky and poorly textured -- but Morrowwind was one of the first games I ever played that felt like I was in total control of the pace of it all. If I wanted to explore every cave before doing the main story line -- there was nothing to stop me from doing so. Granted, I had to use console codes to respawn several people I had killed off (opps) but beyond that I played about as non-linearly as you could ever want to and loved every minute of it.
The reason I don't recommend it is that unless you have a guide open with all the console commands to teleport places, you will spent probably 80% of your play time walking between locations. Not even running, because running is a skill that you have to level first, but just getting places. It takes FOREVER. I played in such a way that I broke up the walking by picking everything in sight and taking on every side quest -- but if you were to try and just play the main quest line straight through -- it would be torturous getting places.
The AI for followers is also really stupid. There's a bunch of "bring me this person" or "rescue" quests that are twenty times harder because your follower just stops, or occasionally runs the absolute wrong way. You can also accidently kill your followers -- which again console codes fix -- but in a game that is honestly mostly walking the AI should be a little bit better about it.
And sadly half the skills were filler skills that just drove me nuts. Athletics as a separate skill then aerobatics; which means that I had to stand in place jumping for 20 minutes because I couldn't jump high enough to escape the dungeon I was in; because jumping as a skill makes total sense.
The other downside is that there's forever "stuff" in all the dungeons and buildings you go through. Expect to search 200 sacks of potatoes for every 1 that has something useful in it; especially in quest lines that say "x-item is in a sack in y-place" there is no way to tell without a guidebook which of the million crates or sacks you need to look through.
Pros
+ Massive open world
+ great story line
+ play at your own pace
Cons
- Useless skills
- WALKING EVERYWHERE
- wonky AI

I love me some arcade racing. Gas Guzzlers delivers.
Fans of cars and explosions will have a blast zooming around the game's large selection of tracks across a variety of environments, including deserts, snowy mountaintops, tarmac tracks, and backwoods trails.
There's a good selection of cars and even more weapons to equip them with, as well lots of other unlockable goodies to upgrade and decorate your cars. The solo campaign is great, but beginner racers might find it slightly difficult. The AI racers also all have really stupid (and frankly immature) names too, but that's not really a huge deal I guess.
Controls are responsive, and gameplay is tight and rewarding; there's something satisfying about blasting away your fellow racers, or forcing them to crash into things. You may also find it's reminiscent of kart racers like Mario Kart and Diddy Kong racing as you dash around collecting powerups, repairs, and cash bonuses.
There's also a wealth of multiplayer modes, so you can choose your flavour and start blowing up your friends however you like.
I highly recommend this one, can't get enough of it.

Summary: Fun little Mad Max themed game at first but a (minor) imbalance in the game and hard AI makes this game very hard, even frustrating when you're first starting out.
This is a Mad Max themed game where you drive your upgradable vehicle towards the destination 7km away. On route you will encounter enemy vehicles which can be destroyed with on board weaponry and you shall stop at each village/checkpoint to endure a wave of enemies in order to liberate them so you can purchase your vehicle and personal upgrades there.
This game is difficult, very difficult, even unbalanced maybe? I'm able to reach the first village without problems but the rest depends on RNGesus and which enemies he spawns. I've had times I barely made it to the next, other times I got killed early on cause I either ran out of fuel or didn't have enough armor to protect my health. In all those scenarios I had around the same amount of cash, just a different upgrade.
You could say that you need to find which upgrade is best at which checkpoint and dependent on the amount of cash you have. While this is true, I must admit the gameplay is rather repetitive if you die many times. Therefore finding the commitment/motivation to try a next time decreases drastically with each death on the record.

Ace of Spades
The Basics: A blend of voxel based block crafting and classic team first person shooter.
Previous Time Spent: 36
Expectation of learning Curve: Low
Why I bought this: Minecraft Phase
My 3 Hours with the Game: I began getting back into the game with an astoundingly small download on steam, which earned the game a bunch of points from the get-go. From there, I dove in to the game itself.
Knowing little about what to expect, and with a very fuzzy memory of the game-play from a few years ago, I decided to go ahead and join a random server. This turned out to be a very fast paced and fun zombie mode, where players begin as human, and attempt to survive against a growing horde of undead. This has been done plenty of times before, but I enjoyed the added lunacy of mutable environments. I spent a good deal of time trying to build a massive tower to protect myself from the dead, and was surprised when it came collapsing on itself, leading to brief violence and a quick transformation into a zombie.
Playing as a zombie was a delight, and had a completely different feel and basic strategy, which I appreciated. All in all, the zombie mode provided solid, engaging and bizarre mindless fun. I could choose to strategically defend myself, run around like an idiot, or just dig a hole and cover myself with dirt, hoping that the undead didn't find me.
I spent a lot of time digging holes in this game. Even in the engaging classic capture the flag mode. When I started playing capture the flag, I was a bit worried, as the server was more quiet, and clearly less chaotic. However, after finding my bearings, learning to follow the map, and getting into it, it felt a lot like playing capture the flag as a kid, only with bolt action rifles.
The levels are huge, and the ability to dig and build allows a lot of opportunity for creative strategy and silly low cunning.
The bottom line: This is the first game in my steam backlog that I'm happy to have purchased. It's the first that I will keep installed, and occasionally go back to as a silly time-waster. The low learning curve helped quite a bit, and I enjoyed the cutesy, retro-inspired graphical touches.
