Huniepop is a fairly simple dating sim/puzzle game; you talk to girls and learn things about them to earn points that can be used to upgrade one's personal traits. Then, when you feel you've upgraded those traits adequately enough, you take girls on dates where you play a simple Bejeweled/Candycrush-like puzzle game where you try to match the trait symbols the girl you're dating most likes as much as possible within the number of allotted turns available. Should your date go well, she gains a heart, and once you've done this enough, you and her can have sex after a date.
I know I put that I recommend this game, but really it all depends. What's appealing and neat about the game is that it has pretty good artwork and decent voice acting, which i great since every word a girl says is spoken by voice actors (unless you choose to turn that off in the options). Its a nice change of pace from games that are only semi-voice acted. The dialogue is also pretty fun to read. The game can also be downright sexy in this manner, as it has fully voiced sex scenes, moans and all.
The problem is that this game comes off as sleazy and unrealistic. I mean yes, this is essentially a porn game (well, if you added/made the uncensor patch like I did), but it kind of sucks that the end-goal is not to form a lasting relationship with the girl of your dreams, the one you love, but to simply have sex with a girl. You won't be getting to achieve your dream of being with, loving, and marrying your waifu in this (If your waifu is actually in this game...I'm so sorry). What's worse is that you can date all the girls in the game and have sex with them all. Its completely unrealistic to how dating works. And while I said that the dialogue was fun, its unrealistic too. A lot of things brought up in conversations with many of the girls is very, ...no, EXTREMELY unlikely to be the same sort of things asked and said in a real life date. For instance, if you choose to chat with a girl she might ask you out of the blue things like "How often do you watch porn?". On the other hand, when you ask other girls things you can ask what size their breasts are or how old they are and none of the girls will complain or be upset by such questions. I get that not everyone acts the same way, but there are certain social norms that just aren't followed in this game. Its silly.
If you were looking to play a simple and kind of fun game and aren't worried about any real depth, or if you were simply wanting to have some good art and porn, then I can recommend this game. But if you were hoping for some masterpiece or a really deep in depth dating sim, you're best looking elsewhere.

I'm doing a lets play in the game. Please check it out. Note: I paid for the game myself & I am not affiliated with the developers. My opinions are my own.
Bunker Punks is a fantastic framework on which the devs plan to create an extremely fun rogue-like-like (rogue lite?). I bought Bunker Punks in probably the stupidest way. Impulsively. When purchasing games ESPECIALLY early access games one should always do thurogh research, and think before making a decision. Do I regret buying the game? No, but I regret how I bought it.
Now more importantly how is Bunker Punks? It is an excellent framework. There are procedurally generated levels. Different types of enemies which scale and appear as you progress. The levels are random but there is an over arching world map (a la Mario 3) which gives you choice on your way to the end. There are 4 armor slots (head, chest, hands, & feet) and there are a variety of different sets which give varying different bonuses everything is mix and match as you choose. There are 5 different weapons(I assume they are weapons groups too but there aren't more weapons yet) they are: baseball bat(melee); pistol; shotgun; auto rifle; rocket launcher. Each weapon feels unique and requires different strategies for each. The weapons and armor that are in the game now work great and are fun; once a wider variety are added it's going to make the gameplay much more fun.
This being a rogue lite (like-like) there is a meta game. Upon starting you pick a character(or more if you've unlocked them) and immediately enter a lever (I believe it's your base that your clearing out). Once cleared you arrive at your base. Here you can spend Credits that you find on enemies and boxes on leveling up your base. You can buy medical labs, firing ranges, and other buildings(modules). These modules can individually be leveled up. For example: one of the modules is the rifle range. Each level of this module gives +25% to rifle damage. The upgrades are quite valuable. Upgrades combined with appropriate armor bonuses can be awesome giving you + 100% damage or more! There is another collectible besides Credits and it is Tech. Upon the death of all of your characters you're sent back to the beginning (character selection). This is where Tech comes into play. You can spend the tech you've acquired on more characters, items, armor, modules, etc.
If you're a fan of this genera Bunker Punks is a game to check out. Currently there is a very solid base game. If it was to never receive an update it wouldn't be worth the money. It would be too dull. However because the groundwork has already been laid the updates should come relatively easily. The devs don't need to build fundamentals but rather add all the fun stuff. Perhaps don't buy it quite yet. Unless you're prepared for the plausibility that this game is abandoned. Definitely add it to your wish list or follow it because soon enough this game is gonna be really freaking awesome!!!!

to have a lot of depth (and the developers claim this), although I cannot speak past what I have played

This is first and foremost a game similiar (very) to Dungeons Of Dredmor; hence a rogue-like; even when it also offers a campaing mode without the typical permadeath.
gamepay works just like in Dredmor, basicaly the game is turnbased: move, attack, use items skills; every action uses one "turn", you enemies and allies (you can have up to two pets at once fighting for ya) move after you made your "turn";
similiar to Dredmor you can either play the game more fast paced or take your time..the choice is up to.
what the game differs from Dredmor and other rogue-likes is the character-system, there is no skill/talent or anything progression; when you level you get stat-upgrades automaticaly, which take away alot of the good rogue-likes normaly present: character-building; yes, you can still make different choices depending on your equipment (which there`s a metric ton of...and wearable at the same time)...but still it feels alot more shallow than normal rogue-likes/lights.
new skills/spells are aquired just like gear/loot is and can be equiped just aswell.
the game offers over 500 crafting recipes, all from food to gear..so there`s alot to collect.
the game has one major strength: it`s visual design; Pratchett, Grimm, typical fantasy sticks all blend into a very upbeat, colourfull gameworld with some amazing 2D backround and character art. the soundtrack isn`t outstanding, but it works..there`s basicaly no voice-over.
what doesn`t work is the humor, there`s alot of the wit and "joke" missing the visuals suggest; it`s not terrible just a tad underwhelming.
all in all a rather streamlined rogue-like, Dredmor, yet still great fun in small haps; if you can dig the price and got a nack for tbs rogue-likes or the visual still (some light rpg) definitly worth a look.

I have only played this game for an hour or so, but I enjoyed it contrary to the other reviews. Here is why.
I was one of the kickstarter backers for this game. I was aware from the screenshots what kind of game it will be but I took a risk and backed it anyhow. The way the game is built is like it is one big Final Fantasy tactics map, but unlike that kind of game, the "step by step" map system is active even outside of battles. This may be frustrating at times but also fun as it gives you the feeling that you are playing the game the whole time, as opposed to feeling that you are playing a challenge only when battles arise. At times you will find the movement clunky, especially if you are using joypad, but you could always use the mouse to select where to go and she will go there automatically, or u can destroy the trees and obstacles in your path to create your own path, collecting loot as you do so.
If you can get past the clunkiness and accept that the game was intentionally created this way, there is a deep sense of fun and involvement. I like the world and the idea. A drunken "red riding hood" and her pet wolf working as mercenaries for hire while also trying to discover her past. The artwork, character and mood of the ambient music makes u feel very involved. Remember, when you feel stuck or can't get past some place, that means there is something u need to do or figure out. Whether it is a puzzle or simply needing to destroy the obstacle down to keep moving, any obstacles or "clunkiness" in the game is intentional. It feels this way.
Overall it is a fun experience if you want to try something new and wiling to get past the default preconceptions of how a game SHOULD be. The obstacles and clunkiness are no different than the frustration one feels when you play the original megaman games and you realize that you can't duck. :) It is part of the game
Also knowing that this game was made by 5 indie developers, they did quiet a good job. Also the artwork and world inspired by the Grimm Brothers' tales really connects to me. :)
To sum up
Pros:
-Lovely Artwork
-New Idea
-Involving gameplay
-Interesting Music
-Loveable characters
-Nice contradiction between a colorful world and a moral-less culture
-You get better at it the more you play it
-Some puzzles are not explained and you feel a sense of satisfaction when you figure them out on your own
-It feels like one big game as opposed to separate layouts for battles and walking the map (turned based environment, like one big chess board)
-Tons of looting. There is crafting too but haven't tried it yet. :)
- Even though it is a rogue-like game, the default storymode offers you an option to restore when dead as well as saves, so you have the choice between playing a normal game in story mode or a permadeath game in survival mode. :)
Cons:
-Not what you expect it at first to be
-the clunky turned based movement takes you off guard at first
-no tutorial whatsoever. The instructions are with the manual included with the game. I got it as a kickstarter backer. Not sure if it's included with steam purchase (update: discovered the manual exists in the main menu under the title "Read or Die" :) )
-can make u feel confused at times and wondering if you are doing the right thing
-puzzles not being explained can be frustrating to some people
Overall if you give it a chance you find yourself enjoying it. There was definitely effort invested in this game. I personally enjoyed it. Feel free to see which cons and pros matter more to you before you purchase it. :)
I personally give it 7/10 :)

As someone who kickstarted DFS, I have to admit that I'm impressed with the game so far. Considering this is Grimm Bros.' first game, it's a lot of fun and has a lot of charm packed into its story. It's got flaws (the UI, the crafting), but roguelike fans should still get a kick out of it.
PROS:
- Three game modes (Story, Survival, Endless Labyrinth)
- Two difficulties (Normal and Hardcore/Permadeath)
- Unlockable characters in Endless Labyrinth
- Controller support (and it feels great now, thanks to patch)
- Pets to collect, up to two in your party
- Crafting and fishing systems to play around with (fishing bug has been patched)
- The dungeon areas have a lot of little secrets
- Devs are listening, taking in feedback, and releasing patches to fix major issues
CONS:
- Crafting UI is awful.
- Menu system needs to be reworked
- Not enough information in battle
- Dungeons can feel "cluttered" and sometimes tricky to see/escape
- A lack of keybindings
- Storage space is small
SUBJECTIVE:
- The game can be difficult as hell (For me, a huge pro)
- The aesthetics (bright/vibrant colors!)
Having put some time into it, I can definitely recommend this to fans of the roguelike genre. The combat mixes in melee with ranged. Pets provides some tactical advantage since it allows for flanking/backstabbing, and they have leveling independent from your own. You've got a rage meter, magic spells, and a crafting system to play around with. Scattered throughout the dungeons themselves are traps, switches that benefit or harm, rare merchants that sell crazy stuff, switches that create surprises when hit in the right order, and more.
And now to clarify some of the cons.
Most of these are small gripes. Admittedly, a lack of keybindings does hurt the game, especially since you're forced to navigate the (rather simple) menu in order to access Inventory, Equipment, Magic, etc. Adding keys to individually open up these specific menus would be great, but it's a small issue since the menu is easy enough to navigate. Also, you DO have storage space - but it's not terribly large and you may run out of space fairly quickly. Fellow packrats, be warned.
The crafting UI, on the other hand, is just plain bad. Your learned complex recipes (gear and such) are on the left-hand side and this is fine. However, simpler recipes such as creating planks out of raw wood, or the number of zinc required to make an ingot, are absent. Either memorization or documentation is needed for these, unless I'm missing something obvious. Additionally, you can only craft one item at a time. When crafted, it's required to move the finished product out of the "completed" slot before crafting the next one. It's tedious as hell and really needs to be modified.
Additionally, the menu doesn't need an Inventory screen. It's redundant when compared to the Equipment screen. Combat, while a lot of fun, also just doesn't give you enough information on your enemies and pets. You can't check individual pet HP, you can't scroll through enemy HP to prioritize them (a problem when in a crowd, since it could be a bit tricky to make out which bar belongs to who). I'm still wrapping my head around terrain bonuses, which would have benefitted from some kind of mouse-over or something. In short, the UI needs love. Lots of it.
CLOSING:
Overall, I personally feel that the game feels FUN despite its flaws, although (once again) you need to be a fan of roguelikes. This game is *hard.* If you enjoyed Dungeons of Dredmor, Izuna, Shiren the Wanderer, etc. then there's a good chance you'll enjoy what's here.
That and the idea of Red Riding Hood traipsing through the woods, cheerfully murdering monsters is an idea that appeals to me.
As stated before, this is Grimm Bros.' first game. It's kinda rough, it's by no means perfect, but it's a solid title. I gave the devs my money and put my faith in them, and I've got faith that they'll keep updating/supporting this title by making it shine even more. Patches have already been shoved through the pipeline and they're checking their forums as well as Steam's.
Will update this review as necessary.
Edit: Added some details on the dungeon-crawling and removed the detail saying that DFS has farming. There is NO farming, I was writing this at 4am and had just finished a surreal dream about Kevin Costner. Also, my biggest cons have been patched, so huzzah! DEFINITELY recommend it now!

Quick Initial Impressions after ~3 hours. Quick note to people playing this atm, I would suggest reading up on the in game manual guide to get a better sense of what all the status ailments are and stats on your hero do.
PROS
+Humor, for example, each piece of loot has a tiny line of description. I found a shield with poorly written handwriting on it and the description something of the likes of: "May have been written by a dyxlexic person."
+Tons of Loot with an accompanied slot on the hero, such as earings, ring slots, head slot, cape slot? (for her hood?) the type of ammo she equips, her gun (shotgun, rifle or handgun,) and it goes on and on.
+As above, you can customize your "loadout" so to speak, and choose if you want a more defensive approach, instead of dual wielding weapons, perhaps you want to use a sword and board approach. While you may do less damage, your shield will provide you the proper defenses necessary. You can also choose what type of ammo you want to use. There are a plethora of ammo types with their own strengths and weaknesses (perhaps even elemental attributes later on in the game?)
+Tons of crafting, there are a ton of recipes to be found in all the maps. While crafting isn't necessary, I can already tell I will be at an advantage if I choose to.
+Exploration is rewarded, every map that is randomly generated (as far as I am aware of) has nooks and crannies filled with crafting recipes, potions, or random loot.  The more your dig the more you may find.
+Artstyle is amazing, there are three levels of zoom during the game. You can zoom out to see a large portion of the map and your hero, or zoom in really close up to get right in the action. Each enemy is well drawn in game and their hero portrait reminds me of games like Jeanne D arc or Tactics Ogre for the PSP. Love love love the art design, and what is amazing is that is was done all by one guy.
+Day and night effects really effect the game. As you progress through a quest and time passes by, the map gets darker as it gets later. When it gets really dark, it can make things difficult to see. A cool feature in my opinion that isn't done in many games.
+Weather effects! So far I have seen sunny, rainy, and windy effects. It makes the world you are slaying monsters in feel a bit more alive as everything isn't so stagnant. The weather effects really are great! Hopefully there is snow later on!
+Random events as you travel from quest to quest. So far its just bandits trying to steal your money, you are given the option to give them your gold or fight them to the death to keep it.  Hopefully these random events change up, but I liked that there was some random element to the game.
Indifferent
+- Dumps you in to the game world without really a tutorial or a quick learning guide. What does MP do in this game? What does each stat mean on your hero? Why should you craft? You gave me a wolf at the start of the game as my pet, it attacks monsters, is there anything else to it?
+-There is a ton of loot in the game, and as far as I can tell none of it changes the appearance of your hero. While I can understand that would be difficult to implement, it really would have brought up the immersion to your hero one extra notch. Like in Zelda Link to the past, when Link gets a different color tunic, he changes to red or blue link. Or in Diablo where your weapon and armor constantly change your appearance. What you see in the trailers is what you get, red Robin (the name of our hero in this game.)
+-I am at the point where monsters are getting really tough and all the potions I bought from the shop are not restocking. They haven't restocked at all during my first three hours, and to be honest you kind of need to balance slaying and quaffing potions from time to time throughout each quest/map.  Without potions, you are going to die sooner or later as there is no block mechanic in this game.
CONS
-So you are pretty much a mercenary for hire, where you go get odd jobs for money at the local pub.  Story starts off super slow, at the two to three hour mark is when you start learning about the protagonist Robin, for an RPG (and roguelike) that is a bit on the slower end of things. The first couple of hours you are just doing a couple fetch quests and kill quests from some dude in the pub, and without a sense of purpose of why you are going on these missions there really is no value you what you are doing. I was asking myself, why does gold matter, why do I want to progress to the next level?
-Soundtrack is decent, but whats more upsetting is the sound effects. The trailer narrator is poor and that is also the intro of the game, but what is hands down unbearable in this game is the monster sound effects. All of them sound like they come out of a speaker then recorded back in to the speaker. There isn't a precise sound with them, they sound muffled and sound really low quality. Furthermore, many of the monster sounds all blend together and when they make their noise each time they attack you, it can be annoying at times.
Wrap up: I had my eyes on this game many years ago and have been following along on it ever since.  I am having fun with the game more so now that the story is opening up. Yes the fetch quests and kill quests at the beggining make you wonder why exactly you are doing it, but after the first story sequence I am more inclined to press forward. I do like exploring each and every map for the goodies. There is a certain rewarding feeling of leveling up your charachter and equipping new loot along the way. For people that love loot and customizing their hero, this will be a rewarding game for you. I feel like if you know there is going to be a slow start to the game, I would say pick it up!
If I get the time I will definitely add a quick lookish video tomorrow letting you visually see what it is I am talking about. I haven't even gotten a chance to dive in to the rogue like modes (that is initially why I was interested in the game in the first place many years ago) or the endless mode. There is a lot of content here to be had, perhaps Grim Bros should have really nailed one gameplay option?

When I first saw it, the game looked amazing. The style and fluidity of controls really drew me in, but what pushed me out was the artificial difficulty of ridiculous level design and terrible enemy placements. I tried really hard to enjoy the game, but I couldn't bring myself to play past chapter three before uninstalling. You are pushed into too many situations which you are only able to maneuver out of either by luring away the slow moving spirits, which tend to be more a nuisance than a threat, or by sheer luck you manage to avoid the tight congregations of three spirits huddled together in some otherworldly orgy. I found the mechanics to be refreshingly simplistic and very well thought out such as being able to throw objects to distract the spirits, if only these mechanics actually worked. Not once was I able to lure away the attention of a spirit and manage to get past it without it giving chase. The stamina bar is basically just your "I just want to get from point A to B as quickly as possible" feature, since it all but entirely ceases to exist when you are getting chased by spirits, which is a LOT. I understand the game is trying to convey the hopelessness of a little girl out alone in a town crawling with evil ghosts all bent on murdering her ruthlessly, but I have always thought adrenaline makes it HARDER for you to run out of breath when trying to escape something, not immediately suffer an asthma attack because you saw a floating eyeball that barely moves faster than a snail's pace. We can probably just chalk it up to me being bad at games like this, but I just don't have the patience to suffer through something a million times due to trial and error solely because it's "part of the experience." I love the artstyle, I love the ambience, and I love the IDEAS the game had; I just sincerely think it wasn't well executed and fell considerably short with gameplay, which is obviously what actually makes the game a game instead of a terrible drudge. It's an incredibly well made game and I am by no means saying it's bad, I see a ton of people love it and have WAY more patience with stuff like this than I do, I just personally cannot recommend the game due to what I perceive to be terrible design choices and artificial difficulty.

Huniepop is a fairly simple dating sim/puzzle game; you talk to girls and learn things about them to earn points that can be used to upgrade one's personal traits. Then, when you feel you've upgraded those traits adequately enough, you take girls on dates where you play a simple Bejeweled/Candycrush-like puzzle game where you try to match the trait symbols the girl you're dating most likes as much as possible within the number of allotted turns available. Should your date go well, she gains a heart, and once you've done this enough, you and her can have sex after a date.
I know I put that I recommend this game, but really it all depends. What's appealing and neat about the game is that it has pretty good artwork and decent voice acting, which i great since every word a girl says is spoken by voice actors (unless you choose to turn that off in the options). Its a nice change of pace from games that are only semi-voice acted. The dialogue is also pretty fun to read. The game can also be downright sexy in this manner, as it has fully voiced sex scenes, moans and all.
The problem is that this game comes off as sleazy and unrealistic. I mean yes, this is essentially a porn game (well, if you added/made the uncensor patch like I did), but it kind of sucks that the end-goal is not to form a lasting relationship with the girl of your dreams, the one you love, but to simply have sex with a girl. You won't be getting to achieve your dream of being with, loving, and marrying your waifu in this (If your waifu is actually in this game...I'm so sorry). What's worse is that you can date all the girls in the game and have sex with them all. Its completely unrealistic to how dating works. And while I said that the dialogue was fun, its unrealistic too. A lot of things brought up in conversations with many of the girls is very, ...no, EXTREMELY unlikely to be the same sort of things asked and said in a real life date. For instance, if you choose to chat with a girl she might ask you out of the blue things like "How often do you watch porn?". On the other hand, when you ask other girls things you can ask what size their breasts are or how old they are and none of the girls will complain or be upset by such questions. I get that not everyone acts the same way, but there are certain social norms that just aren't followed in this game. Its silly.
If you were looking to play a simple and kind of fun game and aren't worried about any real depth, or if you were simply wanting to have some good art and porn, then I can recommend this game. But if you were hoping for some masterpiece or a really deep in depth dating sim, you're best looking elsewhere.

+: This game is so good I re-bought it on Steam just so I could write a review talking about how good it is.
+: Pretty much the best TES game other than a heavily modded Oblivion or extremely modded Skyrim if you like old school RPGs.
+: Has an absurd amount of mods that increase the graphics to be more modern or add lots of content (Soltha Sil Expanded is
, there's a mod that adds an entire new continent, etc), so you can make this game look beautiful or even better if you want to. Those who have played Oblivion or Skyrim know the deal here, but Morrowind has a lot of great content made for it since it's an older game.
+: The amount of freedom you have is pretty unrivaled. You can make spells that completely break the game, like make your character fly so fast the game crashes from loading too many cells at once (at least on older PCs, and I think there are mods to help fix this). It takes a long time, but you can do it.
-: If you don't like old school mechanics like having to find stuff manually in the world based on directions and not having an arrow navigate you everywhere you'll hate this game.
-: The combat system is mechanically terrible and unfortunately not fixable until OpenMorrowind comes out since it's mostly hard coded at an engine level preventing stuff from proper dual wielding etc from happening. The experience of playing this game and atmosphere of the world is so good I don't care though.

It's okay, but feels a little thin.  Using a shotgun and certain abilities feels pretty satisfying, but the melee combat is pretty bland.  It lacks the depth of a good roguelike, and there are certain things that keep it from having the flow they were looking for.  The crafting system seems big and complicated, but honestly I don't care enough about it to really want to use it.
The story mode is pretty boring and honestly not that great from what I've seen so far.  Endless mode is a bit more fun.. but for that, I feel like I have a dozen games that do this type of thing 10x better.
It feels like it was made for consoles/tablets first, and haphazardly ported to PC.
You can't rebind the controls, and if you want to use a controller, you have to go edit filenames to make sure the included controller preset file for your type of controller is named _controls.csv... and you better hope they included a preset for your controller, since there are only like 4 availible.  I'm not kidding.  This is VERY LAZY on the developer's part, and I imagine some users who aren't so great with computers will struggle with this.  In-game menu, please!  Is that so much to ask?
The keyboard controls are wiggity-whack.  Why can't "I" be inventory?  E for equipment?  Q or L for Questlog? S or K for skills?  You know, like most roguelike/lite games?  You can move with QWEASDZC, the numpad, the mouse, or the left-stick on the controller.  Facing different directions is easy enough on controller, since you just use the right-stick, but to turn with the keyboard you have to hold space and press a direction.  It's very clunky.  I hear an update is coming soon that will allow users to rebind controls... via (you guessed it!) an INI file.  ugh.  Again...  IN. GAME. MENU. PLEASE.
The controls are much more bearable with my 360 controller during actual gameplay, but are slow and annoying to use in the inventory menus.
The UI is full of big buttons, and menus that pop out of the sides of the screen.  It looks like a tablet game.
You have 3 levels of zoom. "way too close" "okay, but I'd like to zoom out maybe just a little" and "way too far away"
The sounds and music are pretty good.  Not great, not bad.. just alright.
Kinda pretty.. pre-rendered 3D-esque sprites.. nice shaders and effects.  It looks pretty nice, though sometimes walls and other objects on the terrain just get in the way of me seeing what I'm doing.  The graphics are one of this game's strongest aspects.. but sometimes the big sprites and terrain objects are just too much.
In conclusion... Wait and see if the devs get their act together on the controls... and maybe see if it goes on sale or something.  At this time, I wouldn't recommend it.  Certainly not at full price.

=====================Second Edition==================
Hello Ash and Grimm Bros Team,
It is nice to see that the dev team is willing to improve the current product and hear the customers’ opinions and observations. Since you took the time to take my opinion into account I would be more than happy to provide you a more detailed answer.
Before getting into those details I want to express that I’m aware of the complexity that is involved on the creation of any interactive media product and how difficult it is to create an accurate user-product dynamic. I do apologize for my English as well, since it is not my first language. With that said, lets begin with the answer you requested me.
USER FEEDBACK RELATED ISSUES:
Cut-Scenes:
When watching the intro cut scene I saw no “press <input> to skip” kind of message so my first thoughts were that transition between one cut scene image and the other one was automatic. Then the dialog stopped and it didn’t advance automatically. Hmmm…maybe I should press a key but which Key? There were no clues to figure out the key that I should press. I wanted to see the intro cut scene so my concern was: “what if I press an input to close or skip the whole cut scene instead of advancing to the next part of the cut scene”. I tried pressing space, enter and a bunch of other keys. But the game wasn’t asking me for a key. It wanted me to perform a click. Too much user-guessing right from the beginning.
Game Mini Map:
A mini-map’s main functionality is to allow the players to locate themselves on it. That means that you main focal stress on a mini-map should be the convention that represents the player on the map. A yellow pixel on top of equal sized brow pixels are not the best pallet and form choices to achieve this. All the other secondary elements on the mini-map (NPC and items) are more visible than the main character’s location itself. Conventions take a while to figure them out since there is no visible map legend to take a look at. Also it would be nice to be able to see key level features on the minimal like where are the local-zone teleporters located.
Party health and stats:
Moment to moment feedback of you party member’s is a must have. I can only see my party members’ health-bar briefly when moving from one tile to another one. Why not showing it always to allow the player to take more accurate decision and weight the risks before moving.
Key bindings:
In the beginning I thought that there were no key shortcuts on this game. Then I read in some forums that apparently there is some key shortcuts but not much information about them. The game should include a control scheme section to be able to see the possible inputs for the user.
Also the ESC key functionality could be a little bit more practical. Open main menu and close menus will be a more common setup for this key.
Curse Skull Icon:
I didn’t notice when it was added to my screen or for what reason. I thought maybe is the time that I have to complete my quest. Then I notice that I ran out of time but I didn’t failed the quest. Then my conclusion was maybe is a period of time in which the undead enemies spawns. But again I was misled to believe that because of the undead iconography. Then I notice that it didn’t appear again. Long story short the 4th time I got cursed was when I realized that that Icon was meant to be the curse duration GUI representation element.
Chosen Path for the main character:
If you give the players the ability to move by clicking on the ground at least show them which path is the one that the AI is going to choose since the best path decided by the AI is not always the path that the player has in mind or would like to take. Moving by clicking is rather risky since the player is not able to forecast which path the AI is going to pick.
READABILITY RELATED ISSUES:
Overlaying Objects:
I can see how important was to create non-square art assets to maintain the overall aesthetic of the game. But, the proportions of the objects combined with the chosen orthogonal perspective create a lot of undesired overlapping. I can see that the current solution allows the player to see the main character through the front objects by reducing the opacity of the last ones but the low opacity is not enough to see the immediate surroundings of the player. It is really difficult to spot obstacles, path and items on dense vegetation areas were a lot of overlapping occurs.
Input inconsistency:
In terms of inputs there are some dynamics that are natural for the user to expect. One user input equals to one outcome. If the user press the movement key once he or she would be expecting for the character to move one step on the map instead of two. The same can be said on the menu. If the user press the down key to go to the next option it should go down one step not two.
Vegetation and Terrain coexistence:
The Vegetation and the terrain does not integrate well in terms of creating a clear paths for the player to follow. Sometimes the vegetation can spawn in some places where it would give the impression that the player reached the boundaries of the map but is only an illusion created by the graphic composition on screen. This can be rather annoying if a target or objective is located on an area that is only reachable through that path. This is one of the biggest risks of leaving the level design to a procedural process. It can work very well sometimes but other times it could go really wrong.
UI Usability:
Trying to open the options menu is rather risky if you miss the button. The icon that brings the in-game main menu has a rather small clickable area and size. If you miss the click your character will walk towards the border of the screen no matter how far it is and how dangerous it is. You could step over several traps or get into undesirable fights. Also it would be nice to be able to close the menus by clicking outside them instead of closing each menu one by one.
Once again thank you for hearing my observations and I will look forward to see the evolution process of your product.

Simply put: this game is not worth $22.00, and I would only recommend this game if it appeals to you AND is offered at $10.00 or less (at which point I will switch my rating and judge less harsh in my review)
PROS:
- Feels very satisfying being able to 'kite' enemies with your shotgun blasts with AoE damage while your pets soak up damage. Best feature hands down.
- The characters have solid amount of energy in dialogue and art.
- Unlockable playable characters for replay value.
- Music is surprisingly impressive.
CONS:
-  There is a huge lack of a main objective/plot/quest. I've spent the entire game so far just talking to a bar owner for pointless side quests (it's the only way to progress).
- Lack of wit in dialogues, which is odd/disappointing for these types of games.
- Animations are played at ~6 frames/second and it makes it feel like a RPG Maker game.
- Being "turn-based" means nothing. It feels weird and unnecessary; playing it in real time would make the game feel smoother and take away only a very small amount of strategy.

I watched a friend play this on Twitch and I fell in love with it without even trying it.  I immediately recognised it as a traditional, old school Roguelike game, and being a fan of that genre I'm finding it amusing how game reviews keep describing it as a blend of Tactical RPG and Roguelike, or a blend of Chrono Trigger and Diablo, or whatever.  Naw, it's straight up old school Roguelike gameplay, and I love it.
I keep picking up hints that this is a game made by people who love video games, just little references to other games here and there.  This makes the game very enjoyable for me.
I'm actually playing it on a computer that's not at all deisgned for gaming (a bargain bin, single core laptop) and the game is playing just fine, minus some lengthly loading times.  Since it's a turn based game I can't see this being much of a problem.  So good job!
My only complaints just far, echoing some of the others I've read, is that there's no way to rebind keys.  The game also promises quite a bit of replay value, and I hope it lives up to its promise.
If you like old school Roguelike you'll probably love this game.  If you like contemporary roguelikes and want to try something fun with an old school flavour then I would highyl recommend this title.

Great if you like playing games in god mode (aka unlimited continues, which is by default enabled), otherwise forget it. You'll go through dozens upon dozens of continues playing this as it's basically designed around you pouring more and more quarters into the arcade machine. The bosses are pure bullet sponges that you just keep on pounding with whatever gun you have available while they keep killing you, until their hitpoints are eventually drained. Other enemies swarm you in such a pattern that no matter how hard you try, you eventually die. You have a single hit point, so you will die a lot.
That means that the challenge is purely artificial. but on the bright side you feel proud of yourself if you manage to stay alive for more than 5 minutes at a time (I'm not kidding either).
It's also over incredibly quick. There are 5 stages, none of which lasts longer than around 20 minutes, unless you're a masochist and switch the default unlimited continues off, at which point I would imagine the game is in fact unfinishable.

Bunker Punks is the Steam debut for the coolly named Ninja Robot Dinosaur. Shane Neville is an independent video game developer and artist living in Vancouver, BC, Canada. He develops games under Ninja Robot Dinosaur Entertainment. The reason that he named his company this is because his games often feature ninjas, robots and/or dinosaurs. In this instance robots feature heavily.
Bunker Punks is a retro FPS that features roguelike and basebuilding mechanics. The FPS action is an instant reminder of some of the classic FPS games from gaming’s past including the early DOOM and Quake games. However, intelligently designed procedural generation, permadeath and the customization of roguelikes have been incorporated into the game.
Players can expect to find the action to become increasingly difficult due to its frantic high-speed action and enemies that can truly be sponges. I accept that some players don’t appreciate ammo sponges with enemies that require you to unload entire clips on a single enemy but I believe that it is well suited to the game. This ultimately means that players will have to strategize on many of the game’s enemies including on the best way to use the environment to your advantage.
One of my favorite features in the game was the bunker building aspect of the gameplay. It adds a tremendous level of depth to the game and provides the necessary tools to differentiate the game from much of its competition. Players can enable new abilities in order to strengthen their punks. The non-linear skill tree also offers a level of customization not often seen in games within the genre. It’s a well considered and thoughtful approach that makes no two games the same.
I also enjoyed the pixelized graphics and thought that the music composed by Gordon McGladdery and Réal Cardinal was also well thought out and inspired. This flows through to the in game audio developed by Power-up audio. Everything is designed to fit nicely and encapsulate the intended atmosphere.
Unlike many other early access games there is no intention to raise the price of the game as it leaves early access but for FPS fans this is a game that you will want to get in early and provide feedback on to inspire the changes that will make the game even better. It is already an intelligently designed game that has consistently incorporates the feedback of its player base. It’s a sleeper hit and one of the best Steam debuts that I have come across. A very easy recommendation.

Right now you're probably thinking "oh great, another 8-bit pixel roguelike shooter, why should i play this stupid game?" well sit down and read:
Bunker Punks has gameplay that's a throwback to good old fashioned first person shooters like Doom(in fact this game is practically doom but with a completely different setting). this game is challenging in a way that's a nice balance between feeling as though you're being spoon fed the victory while being hand held all the way through the game and being a rage inducing nightmare to beat.
-no inherent health regeneration, pick up the health kits if you want healing
-you're more than welcome to sweep the entire room for extra goodies like credits or tech
-no cutscenes to keep you waiting till it's time to shoot up bad guys, just walk through the elevator door and open fire
-enemies can kill you even if you have enough armor to reduce the damage taken to 1 point of damage per hit for most enemy attacks.
-you can run yourself out of ammo with certain weapons but fortunately enemies drop ammo(or credits, tech, medkits, and sometimes new weapons or armor) like they're pinatas full of candy.
"what's with this base building stuff in this game?" that's where old and new come together, in addition to the Doom style gameplay once you've completed each level you go back to your bunker to build rooms(and addons to those rooms if they're already built) to give your punks a better edge in future levels, using the credits you got in the level you completed. the rooms you can build basically have these roles:
-Firing Range: addons available are all devoted to increasing the damage output of your punks(except melee users as of now)
-Infirmary: addons available are all devoted towards increasing the survivability of your punks in some way
-Lab: addons available are all devoted toward increasing resource gain from resource pickups
-Gym: addons available are a mixed bag of offense, mobility, and defense.
the bunker is just a skill tree
i will also add that this is another game that does early access right. it certainly isn't finished yet, but
-i have yet to encounter a bug aside from the resolution error that occurs upon entering the main menu sometimes, the 2+ years spent developing this game must have squashed them all
-addicting as can be due to the game being challenging even if you have unlocked all of the characters, gear, rooms, addons, etc in the game currently(like i have, and now i can either beat the game with what i got or wait till an update that brings in new content comes)
overall, i'd say this is a game with potential, just needs more content(more characters, more addons for rooms, and other stuff to spend tech points on, for i just ran out of stuff to spend tech points on), good thing theres more on the way to ensure that the 14.99 dollar price tag is justified.

Farsky, the first title from the imaginatively titled Farsky Interactive, is a game about surviving in the ocean’s dark depths. You are Nathan, the survivor of a submarine crash who must learn to withstand the dangers of the ocean while attempting to repair his wrecked submarine and return to the surface world. Sounds easy right?  Think again.
Where this game really nails it is with the visuals. The seascape is extremely detailed, there’s kelp, seaweed, fish, and the like everywhere. Stingrays gracefully soar by overhead. Schools of many kinds of fish float by, and occasionally a shark will even swim up!
Farsky, in essence, is all about adapting to the oceanic environment. You start with some very basic tools – a drill, a few seeds, and a small base where you can refill your oxygen. You will have to learn to manage your time spent exploring, unless you really enjoy drowning from running out of oxygen. Using your drill, you can collect many types of resources such as iron, copper, and gold, to craft a variety of tools, weapons, and base items. You can expand your base, create a spear gun, grow a farm, hunt fish to eat, explore the depths, etc. There are a lot of things to do!
At the start, you can only go so deep underwater. As you craft better equipment, you can stay out exploring for longer and go deeper. The deeper you go, the darker and more dangerous it gets, but the rarer resources are found at lower depths! If you go too deep without equipment, your helmet will break and you will drown. Luckily the game has a depth meter in the interface that displays your current depth along with the deepest your current equipment can handle.
Farksy has a Story mode and a Sandbox mode. As you play either mode, you will find small chests of gold coins that you can use to buy starting items for Sandbox mode to give you a head start. Every map is randomly generated as well, creating a new, fresh experience each time you play.
If you like games such as Minecraft, Terraria, or even Edge of Space, you will enjoy Farsky. Other games have used an underwater setting before, but not like this. This is a fresh new concept, and Farsky has nailed it.

Morrowind's greatest triumph is that it crafts a distinctly unique fantasy world, from its various cultures and politics to its dwellings, landscapes, and species.  There is a great deal to discover and an epic story to be experienced - one that still stands as one of the best, even all these years later.
However, the game is not without its flaws.  In particular, combat and its related skills are a bit unrefined.  For example, you won't be able to hit anything with melee attacks until you raise your melee skill, which is only raised by successfully hitting things.  Luckily, this game was very popular and you can find many mods to get around the aspects of the game that aren't up to modern snuff.
If you have the time and see what fantasy can be like when it isn't just piggy-backing off of Tolkien, play this game!

For me, Morrowind is one of the most influential RPGs of all time. With hundreds of hours into Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim, Morrowind edges the other two out for the strongest title of the series.
The art and world design is, to this day, astounding. From the moment stepping of the boat in Seyda Neen, all the way to the final confrontation on Red Mountain is filled with memorable vistas of the strange, alien land of Vvardenfell. Giant mushroom towers, strange animals and monsters, and mysterious Dwemer ruins show  the creativity that went into this game simply cannot be understated, especially compared with its rather bland successor.
A lot of people (players who started with ES IV or V) find that the mechanics and graphics of Morrowind are dated and thus they can't get into the game. I urge anyone to give the game a shot. There is definitely a learning curve, but you'll get past it, I promise. As for the graphics, look up the fan-made Morrowind Graphics and Sound Overhaul, and prepare to be amazed.
The game is not without its faults. Combat is somewhat clunky, and many of the sidequests (there are probably hundreds) are uninspired. That said, the main quest is very compelling. This, combined with the incredibly rich world that Bethesda has created, make this a very easy game to recommend.

The gameplay is a fast paced FPS, with heavy rogue-like elements. Bases are randomly generated on the map, with different types of floors, and each floor is randomly generated. If you enjoyed tower of guns or paranautical activity, you may have an idea of what you're in for. The game has beautiful pixel art, solid music (in my opinion. It's heavy industrial, really fitting of the mood but it's certainly a genre that won't be for everyone). There's base building, multiple characters, and a nice difficulty climb.
The bad, however, is the level art (the walls, etc), while fitting to the setting do blur together after a while. Different types of levels (medical, security, survey, etc) look slightly different from eachother (some more than others), but it's not a large enough difference. As is the game is unfinished, so i won't comment on length, but it has a good amount of replayability at the moment (certainly a lot more if you're not skilled at these genres going in)
I highly recommend you play through until you die that first time. When i started playing I had a lot of questions, and I started to chalk it up to early access, but you'll start unlocking a lot of things and answering all those questions after your first run ends.
Overall, 8/10 at the moment. If the updates keep coming and add more bosses, another world / challenge passed the first, and some new level art, i'd happily bump it up to 8.5. The developers have the 'seeds' for levels displayed, so I don't see why a speed run seed input like the binding of isaac has couldn't happen down the road. As someone who rates 5 as average, and finds most games at or below that, I hope you'll understand this is high praise and something to keep your eyes on.

Man,
Almost 90 hours now and only purchased the game like 2 weeks ago... Let me start by saying, I don't know the first thing about F1 Racing, nor have ever really have had an interest in it (did like the 2 movies I've seen on them though, the Ron Howard directed one and the other that was a bit more campy called Drive I think that Sly Stallone in it..), but I was looking for something to play on the simulation side of things, and came across this and notice the amount of positive reviews for it.
On a whim, decided to pick it up, (probably helped there was a similiar review like this that said the same thing about not really ever being into F1 racing, but somehow totally addicted to this, heh..).. and boy, I don't regret it at all. Ya, i'm shooting myself in the foot a bit, since now the game is on sale for just 8 bucks, and man I thought the game was worth it at 35 bucks, but it's a total steal at just 8 bucks if you happen to pick it up during the current winter sale going on.
While I did spend some time in the vanilla experience, that sort of totally faded out, as when it comes to simulation games like this I'm always drawn to RL mods, even if I have no clue what the sport is in RL.. (last F1 driver I think I ever remembered was , hmm Mario Andretti? I guess...), I tend to gravitate towards it to get the full immersion experience when it comes to actual RL car suppliers, sponsers, and hell started to learn a little about the more popular racers now since I decided to go with a RL mod instead. (shout out to the Fire 2017 mod, as that one is rather excellent and what I'm currenty playing..), and that's what this game can do so well as it really does make you feel like you're running a racing team through season after season.
However, if you are slowly going for the vanilla experience a lot went into the teams they did, and also the drivers that are introduced and stuff. There's a good management aspect in terms of trying to find the best mechanics (with their 2 special unlock abilities that you could use in a race if you so choose) with the right driver.. And once you've found that happy balance the glee of seeing your team perform is quite satistifying like any other simulator that's usually out there.
You also got your chairman (note you get one even if you decided to pick up the free DLC and create your own team) or boss to meet happy demands with, while it's not as extensive as say Football Manager or Out of the Park Baseball in terms of the goals they want each season (here it's simply just a team place finish during the season), there's still a pressure aspect applied to your team, especially if you join a highly well oiled machine that expects to win the team championships year in and year out.
The race day events are pretty fun, and the actual race itself, while you can speed up the races, are pretty fun the watch if you go with the 3D setting, the Tracks while fictional are beautiful to see and never seem to get boring as there's also different variations of each track that could be voted in for next season for use instead of the current one that's being used in the current season by the team owners of the championship series you are participating in (yes you take part in those votes and perhaps could influence to a certain degree as well..) Now , I did hear complaints if you're a true F1 fan you may not like some of the moves and such they do during the race day (as some call it very unrealistic..).. but since I don't really know a thing about F1 in RL, that doesn't bother me in the slightest.
As fun as I've had with this game, the one thing I really wish there was more of was a better stat history aspect added to the game.. While the game keeps track of your drivers performance that current year and how they place on each track for that season and any wins they may have had in the mutilple seasons you'll play, that's pretty much as far is it goes..
Meaning, if I like to compare how certain drivers have performed on certain tracks , year over year, you can't do that, unless of course you're willing to keep track of this yourself outside of the game on an excel spreadsheet, but ehh who has the time to remember or really do that sometimes, lol... Being that I'm coming from the Football Manager series, and the Out of the Park series from way back when (haven't gotten the newer versions although I hear they just as good now too..), to see that lack in stat tracking is very disappointing for a simulation game.
But hey, that's why there's perhaps always Motorsports 2 down the line one day that could hopefully remedy that..
So yea, I could go on and on about perhaps give more nitty gritty details of the other aspect of the game, but I just feel that other good reviews on here have really done that and all. This review is kind of just to give a perspective if you're someone like me who perhaps never had an interest in F1 racing before, but if you have played simulation type games like Football Manager, out of the park baseball, etc... Than this one is certainly worth checking out.
If you're able to snag it while it's still on sale, totally worth it too as mentioned earlier!.

When adventure mode us complete you unlock survivor, it is the same basic premise of finding your sub, but opponants are more common, you only have one life (no respawns), and most importantly the sub parts have no locators, so you need to manually find them, which can be quite hard. This game is actually a lot harder than I remember it being when I was young I remember I did have a tough time with it when I was young but this game really is tough. I enjoy it though. It was so infuriating because when I was young I definitely wasn't as good at it and wasn't able to grasp everything as well as I am now. Now it being a long time later, I get to review it now. It's crazy how time passes and games age.
Review:
Metal Slug 3 is a classic game that I'm not sure if everyone remembers it, but I definitely do. It is an arcade shooter. I don't remember when it was made, but I remember it was more popular when I was young. This arcade shooter only has a handful of levels, but I think that if you get into it it's rich. There are different paths you're able to go down in order to get to the end of the level. For example, in the first level there are three different paths that you can take (to my knowledge) in order to get to the end of the level. I think that is excellent especially for a game of this age. That adds a level of complexity to the game itself and varies it rather than it being a linear arcade shooter, which it is. It gives you some options as far as being able to choose is concerned and seeing where the path of least resistence is and seeing what you can do in order to get to the end without losing a life.
I am still interested in this game, and I've only put a few hours into it but I still like it a lot. I think I will be pumping more hours into this game as time goes on. I still love the secrets this game has to offer. I would recommend this game to anyone who's looking for a good arcade game. This is a simple, solid arcade game. But as always I would recommend you check out the trailers, gameplay videos, and do your research before buying. Right now it's on sale and it's well worth the price, but it won't be for long. Check it out and have fun.

I was seeing every lets-player on youtube play this game, and I thought it was funny at first to see them fail so baddly at match 3. Soon this humor turned to a sort of agitation. I remember watching a lets-play of this game with my brother and I was pointing out all the better moves the youtuber was passing up. My brother asks me (knowing I'm good at puzzle games), "If it was you, would you have been done with this puzzle by now?" To which I replied, "Oh, I would have f*cked her by now." So I bought the game and beat it within two days of owning it, I have not done all the Steam achievements, but I have been with them all (including unlockable characters) and done alpha mode. The game is fairly short if you know what you are doing and are good at puzzle games, and alpha mode is the only thing I've seen past the main 'story', though alpha mode is a big disappointment since it's literally just the game in hard, even though you can play the game on the hard setting at anytime during the main story. The game is very fun and can be extremely addictive, but it is quite short and lacks enough content to make it a really great game: you ask question to get answers you don't even have to remeber because the game remebers them for you, you give the girls gifts, do puzzles, and eventually take them home which is ultimately another puzzle that is impossible for you to lose. Once you find the right combination of date gifts the dates become very easy and since there is no variety in the puzzle types (other than the unlosable final puzzles) the dates start to become pretty boring. The dating sims aspect of the game is good, but also like the puzzles gets repetive and somewhat boring and isn't much of a challenge since the game gives you a kind of cheat sheet for what the girls like and the answers to questions you've asked them so you don't have to remeber.
Overall I think this game is worth your time and money if you like puzzles, dating sims, or just hot anime chicks; however it is by no means the best puzzle game I've ever played nor the best strategy and being a heterosexual female the cute anime girls didn't appeal to me quite as much as the game needs them to in order to make the game feel more fulfilling than it is. I did enjoy it though and would probably play a sequeal or spin-off, and if the creators ever decide to make another HuniePop with guys instead of females... I'm all over that game.

For the price, the game is certainly worth a look, and it is certainly worth the time. Bunker Punks seems pretty simple at first. But the real charm comes from it's simple style, twitch shooter gameplay, the random drops and randomly generated dungeons and the thrill of making it to the elevator. The added perk of stringing together combos to heal yourself while you're in the field is the real golden egg behind the design. Forcing yourself to either stagger your opponents health to kill them all systematically, bathe your opposition in explosives to drop them evenly, or use a high stopping power single-shot weapon to push them all down one by one; is fun and rewarding, especially after a heavy melee of angry red bullets flying at your face.
I'm really happy I jumped on Early Access for this title, it's extremely fun. Let's hope more will be on approach soon. But until then, enjoy the Bunker Punks! It's a wonderful experience.

Winterbottom is superb little gem. One of those that can get lost if you aren't familiar with games from a few years ago. This one slipped by a lot of people, but it still is very much worth checking out. It has a vintage look that will remind one of old cartoons and films from days gone by. The in-game dialogues are done in rhyme and come off as quite likeable considering the material, much like Child of Light in comparison. The platforming and control of character is adequately precise with a DS4 controller. Visuals are basically perfect for the time periods and styles they are trying to provoke, and I personally much prefer this tone of game to Braid, another time puzzler. Gameplay here involves using clones and recording time to conventiently work your way through various contraptions and pie dreams. Altogether short but extremely well made.

My GF got me this game, and we played it together expecting a PC quality game, what we got has the feel of a last minute port from xbox 360.
The graphics are pretty good, but have few actual settings, and your tire tracks shine and sparkle, whether it's in mud, dirt, or snow. Snow and mud make sense, but dirt does not sparkle nor shine, so that is poorly done.
The dynamic terrain is mostly astetic, you need to race several laps to where the dirt piles into mounds before it will actually effect your driving, whether it's in a vehicle or the (what should be) much more sensitive to terrain motocross bike.
The only controller supported is the Xbox 360 one, which is sad since legacy controller support like most PC games use will let you map ANY controller, if you use ANY other controller, have xpadder on hand, and be ready for worse sensitivity than you should ever have with an analog stick.
Another thing on sensitivity, there isn't any settings for it on keyboard, or even if you use the supported controller, so expect to do hard turns on smooth corners a lot.
Tilting should have you Lean and break/gas/steer, the game is supposed to be specifically for the combination of leaning, and throttle/break/steering, but leaning wont effect forward and back tilting in the air, not even on MX, it's only the gas and break, it's unrealistic when you can lean backwards but you tilt forwards because you're breaking, and invalidates the game's primary selling point.
Air time is a little bit much and vaguley borderline realistic, it doesn't really bother gameplay since most people enjoy the extra air time, nor does it stand out as arcade-esk airtime.
All in all, if you still use the dated 360 controller for gaming on PC (Or you like keyboards for racing games), you dont mind the graphics of a last minute console port, and you dont really care about the whole "reflex" part of the game (since it's vaguley there), you may like this game.

Oh, Morrowind. Where shall I begin?
Well, I do want to get this out of the way, for my fellow arachniphobes: Morrowind is one of the few fantasy games that is 100% spider-free. Even the expansion packs lack spiders. The only thing close to a spider is the "dwarven spider constructs" which are really just bowling balls with four mechanical legs.
On to the meat of this review.
I have a love-hate relationship with Morrowind, leaning towards hate. I WANTED to enjoy it, I really did. I loved Skyrim, and I loved Oblivion, and I had heard nothing but high praise for Morrowind. I was EXCITED to play it. And in a few blissful snippets of the game, I truly did enjoy it. My favorite part is one sequence during the Tribunal expansion in a dwemer ruin, that felt a bit like Zork, but in a 3d environment. But I often found myself swinging rapidly between thoughts of "Wow, maybe this game isn't so bad after all; I'm actually having fun!" and "WHAT IS THIS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T?! WHO DESIGNED THIS CRAP?! WHY WOULD YOU EVEN THINK TO DESIGN A GAME THIS WAY?!" followed by some of the worst video game rage I've ever experienced. I'd say about 60% of my Morrowind experience consists of frothing rage at stupid or incredibly unfair game design.
The game simply has not aged well. I'm sure it was amazing for its day, but a lot of the conventions and design choices of that time do not work so well in 2014. The leveling system is like Oblivion, but worse. It's incredibly difficult to time and control your level ups and skill point gains. I had to make a spreadsheet to keep track of it all. Some of the gameplay is needlessly complex. And it is generally admitted, even among people who like the game, that the first few levels are absolute hell.
Some of the design choices are obtuse and incredibly unfair. The worst offender was probably during
I kept dying and wondering why, as I hadn't had any trouble with any of the quests or monsters leading up to that point, so I googled it. Apparently that part of the game is tuned for level 30-40 players. I was level 14, after 100 hours of gameplay. Did I mention that you're not allowed to leave that part until you
? And there's no warning of this. Nothing to indicate that you need to be much higher level than the enemies and preceding quests would suggest. Yes, it lets you know you can't leave until you win. But it doesn't indicate that you need to be much higher level to win than to get to that far! Having sailed through at level 14, I felt pretty confident that I could win, so I said okay and entered, knowing I couldn't leave until then. There was no indication that I wasn't even half the level I needed to be.
What sort of game design is that? Letting a player under HALF the intended level even GET to an area they can't back out of until they beat something more than twice their level, because of a 15+ level JUMP in difficulty? If the player isn't high enough level to win, and therefore be allowed to leave, they should NOT be able to get there in the first place! That's just REALLY BAD game design!
This was immediately following one of those "This game is actually pretty cool!" moments. See what I mean about switching from enjoying myself to frothing rage? If it weren't for console commands, I would have had to reload a much earlier save (and lost my interest in finishing the game, permanently ragequitting) or been stuck there forever (also permanently ragequitting).
When the player is saying "WHAT KIND OF IDIOTIC ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T GAME DESIGN IS THIS?!" multiple times through playing a game, that's a problem.
Then there's the combat system. Dear god. There is a reason "chance to miss/fail" was dropped for oblivion and skyrim. When you swing a weapon at something, you have a chance to miss based on your current fatigue and skill level. At low levels this means you will often be beaten slowly to death by a weak enemy as you flail your weapon uselessly, unable to hit the broad side of a barn at point blank range. Your spells can also fail - but they still cost you magicka! Enjoy spamming your healing spell when you're at low health, eating up all your magicka, and never once getting the spell to successfully cast! Did I mention you have to press a button to switch from holding a weapon to being prepared to cast a spell? Unlike skyrim (where you can either use a quick favorites menu or have a spell in one hand and a weapon in the other) or oblivion (which just has a cast button), you have to switch to spell mode before clicking to cast your spell. Then you have to switch back to fighting mode, and click to swing your weapon.
There's also no fast travel. There are no horses. Sure, you can pay for a silt strider ride, or a boat trip, or use divine/almsivi intervention that take you to a few predefined locations, or use mark/recall to go back to your home base. But they're remarkably inconvenient and you will spend a LOT of time running back and forth in the same general area, fending off cliff racers. Oh, god, the cliff racers. Think zubats, but worse. The less said about them, the better.
All this on top of the fact that I had to spend HOURS struggling with the game to get it to even RUN properly on my computer! For those of you who buy this game (it's your choice, what is rage inducing for me may be fun to you), and can't get it to climb above 10 fps, the problem in my case was primarily the music. Say what you will about Morrowind as a game, but as a PROGRAM it is absolute garbage, cobbled together in the most inefficient and brain-bendingly silly ways. One of the worst offenders was the music system. Try copying the music folder somewhere else, or finding a playlist on youtube, and deleting all the music from the game folders. Then you can play the music from the internet or by selecting your copied folder and playing it in a media player. This will alleviate most of your lag.
On the other hand, it's a testament to Morrowind's story, and sometimes atmosphere (despite the generally bland landscapes, but I'll chalk that up to the limitations of the graphics), that it managed to keep me playing through the end of the main game and one expansion (still working on the other) despite the poor gameplay and design easily producing more gamer rage, and more rage quits, than every other game I've ever played, combined. Hell, I even want to draw some of the characters, which says a lot about how likable they are, given that I DESPISE the gameplay and design, and by extension, am quite bitter about the game as a whole.
There's also the fact that it has probably the best theme song in video game history.
Perhaps a lot of the problems I have with the game can be fixed with mods. If that floats your boat, good for you. But I have played this game without mods because I wanted to be able to review the GAME, not the mods. If you HAVE to mod a game to make it playable/enjoyable, that is, in and of itself, a problem. You shouldn't need the mods to rescue a game. Mods should IMPROVE a game that can, if necessary, stand on its own. In my opinion, Morrowind simply doesn't.
My verdict? Watch a Let's Play, or download Morroblivion (a port of Morrowind to Oblivion, pretty much complete right now) or Skywind (same, but to skyrim, when the mod comes out). This will get you the atmosphere and storyline or Morrowind (the only redeeming features, in my opinion) without you having to actually PLAY MORROWIND. Yes, technically, on a legal level, you have to own Morrowind in order to play the ports, but I still suggest that you never run the original, and instead just play the port. It will save you from dated graphics that aged very poorly, HORRENDOUS combat mechanics, and usually from godawful design/interface/gameplay choices.
Now excuse me while I go finish bloodmoon so I can see how the story ends, and never have to play Morrowind ever again.

Golly gee wiz, just going through the first few reviews of this game wasn't a walk in the park. Granted, many have made valid points and I do agree in some aspects, but some may have been a tad bit biased. That being said, that's not what this is about. Now, let us move on to the actual review, shall we?
Ahem.
Let Blue the Bard (that me) tell all you lovelies a teeny tiny story. A story that you may or may not rage at, but that matter is entirely on your part, not necessarily mine. Blue will admit that they got into the Elder Scrolls series by first playing Skyrim. I know, I know, how n00bish and lame of me, but please, spare Blue the Bard a moment or two! Thing is, Blue hadn't even
of the TES series until Skyrim came out. And even then, they didn't even play it at that time (when it first came out in 2011). Skip to a few years and one of their good ol' friends caused Blue to perk an interest in the game. They were curious, so they decided to try it out. And, to their surprise, they loved it! Blue wanted to get into more of this series, so they did.
Blue tried their hand at TES I: Arena. A bit of a hassle, that one is: what with the DOSbox thingy and remembering the commands, etc. But Blue had minimal knowledge in that area so it wasn't so bad. Skip to a few weeks or months later and TES III: Morrowind and TES IV: Oblivion went on sale. Blue acted quickly and purchased them. First, they tried Morrowind, seeing how that game was released first out of the two.
Blue was very mindful as to not have been biased in any manner, for such a thing is a spell for disaster. They reassured themself that "hey, this is an old game. It's not gonna be fancy-pantsy pretty like them later installments. And maybe the mechanics and gameplay are slightly different. You'll just have to go through with it, like other people have."
Well, I played it, and I loved it. Sure it is a tad bit more complicated, and there are indeed things I could complain about (initial player speed and limited voice acting to name a few specifics) but those aren't things worth giving up this game for. In this game, Blue is nearly unbiased, for they lack the nostalgia factor and they have an understanding of this game being an older thing.
Honestly, despite the early graphics, Blue felt immersed. Here they were, exploring this strange and magnificent land. And, in Blue's humble opinion, this installment has the most relaxing music track. And that is a good thing. Blue felt..happy playing this game. Despite the fact that they have obviously played more Skyrim and Oblivion than Morrowind, Morrowind is something Blue can always come back to. There is still so much more to be explored, after all. And they look forward to it. c:
And that's my review for The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind.
